people.name: Adam
people.description: First man, formed from the dust and given life by the breath of God. Placed in Eden to tend and keep the garden, his disobedience brought sin and death into the human story, and Paul later presents him as the counterpart to Christ, the last Adam who brings life.
people.dateNotes: Ussher chronology (Annales, 1650): created 4004 BC, died 3074 BC (930 years, Gen 5:5). Mainstream scholarship does not date the first humans from the Genesis genealogies.

people.name: Eve
people.description: First woman, fashioned from Adam's side as his companion and counterpart, her name meaning mother of all living. Deceived by the serpent, she shared the forbidden fruit, yet received the first promise of an offspring who would one day crush the deceiver.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: created 4004 BC with Adam (Gen 1:27; 2:22). Scripture does not record her death; 3074 BC is an estimate that simply takes Adam's death year.

people.name: Cain
people.description: Firstborn of Adam and Eve, a tiller of the soil whose rejected offering festered into the murder of his brother Abel. Marked yet protected by God, he became the Bible's first city builder and an enduring warning that sin crouches at the door yet can be mastered.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Scripture gives no dates for Cain: he was born after the Fall (Gen 4:1), before Seth, who was born when Adam was 130 (Gen 5:3), and his death is not recorded. The years are placeholders for display, not a figure we can attribute to Ussher.

people.name: Abel
people.description: Second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of flocks whose offering God accepted, provoking his brother's lethal envy. The first innocent to die in Scripture, he is honored in Hebrews as a man of faith whose blood still speaks, and Jesus names him first among the righteous slain.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Scripture: killed before Seth was born, when Adam was 130 (Gen 4:8, 25; 5:3). Ussher, Annals sec. 13 (130 AM, 3874 BC): the murder came shortly before Seth's birth. Exact year not fixed; the birth year is a placeholder and 3880 BC is an estimate for his death.

people.name: Seth
people.description: Third son of Adam and Eve; ancestor of Noah.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 3874 BC (AM 130), died 2962 BC (912 years, Gen 5:8).

people.name: Enosh
people.description: Son of Seth; in his time people began to call on the name of the LORD.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 3769 BC (AM 235), died 2864 BC (905 years, Gen 5:6-11).

people.name: Kenan
people.description: Son of Enosh; fourth generation from Adam.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 3679 BC (AM 325), died 2769 BC (910 years, Gen 5:9-14).

people.name: Mahalalel
people.description: Son of Kenan; fifth generation from Adam.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 3609 BC (AM 395), died 2714 BC (895 years, Gen 5:12-17).

people.name: Jared
people.description: Son of Mahalalel; father of Enoch. Lived 962 years, second-longest lifespan.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 3544 BC (AM 460), died 2582 BC (962 years, Gen 5:15-20).

people.name: Enoch
people.description: Walked with God and was taken up; did not see death.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 3382 BC (AM 622), translated 3017 BC (365 years, Gen 5:24; Heb 11:5).

people.name: Methuselah
people.description: Longest-lived person in the Bible at 969 years.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 3317 BC (AM 687, Annals sec. 19) and died aged 969 (Gen 5:27) in 2349 BC (AM 1656, Annals sec. 33), the year the Flood began; Ussher remarks that he lived longest of all men. Strictly subtracting 969 years from 3317 BC would give 2348 BC; the Annals date his death to 2349 BC, which is the figure used here.

people.name: Lamech
people.description: Father of Noah; expressed hope for relief from the curse.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 3130 BC (AM 874), died 2353 BC (777 years, Gen 5:31).

people.name: Noah
people.description: Righteous man who walked with God in a corrupt generation, building the ark that carried his family and the animals through the flood. Recipient of the first covenant, sealed by the rainbow; flood traditions across ancient Mesopotamia, including the Gilgamesh epic, echo the memory of a great deluge.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2948 BC (AM 1056), died 1998 BC (950 years, Gen 9:29).

people.name: Japheth
people.description: Son of Noah; ancestor of many European and Asian peoples.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Gen 5:32 (Noah aged 500); Gen 10:21 can be read as calling Japheth the elder brother of Shem, so he takes the earliest year, 2448 BC. No lifespan is given; about 500 years is an estimate on the post-Flood pattern.

events.role: Son of Noah; entered the ark (Gen 7:13)

people.name: Shem
people.description: Son of Noah; ancestor of the Semitic peoples and of Abraham.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2446 BC (AM 1558, Noah aged 502), the year Shem was 100 two years after the Flood (Gen 11:10); died 1846 BC (600 years, Gen 11:10-11). Japheth, listed as the elder (Gen 10:21), is placed at 2448 BC when Noah was 500 (Gen 5:32).

events.role: Son of Noah; entered the ark (Gen 7:13)

people.name: Ham
people.description: Son of Noah; ancestor of the Canaanites, Egyptians, and others.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Noah fathered Shem, Ham and Japheth after he was 500 (Gen 5:32), and Ham is the younger son (Gen 9:24), so he is placed just after Shem (born 2446 BC). No lifespan is given; about 500 years is an estimate on the post-Flood pattern.

events.role: Son of Noah; entered the ark (Gen 7:13)

people.name: Arphaxad
people.description: Son of Shem; born two years after the Flood. Ancestor of Abraham.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2346 BC (AM 1658), died 1908 BC (438 years, Gen 11:10-13). Luke 3:36 and the Septuagint of Gen 11:12-13 place a Cainan between Arphaxad and Salah; the Hebrew text followed here does not.

people.name: Salah
people.description: Son of Arphaxad; father of Eber (Gen 11:12-15).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2311 BC (AM 1693), died 1878 BC (433 years, Gen 11:12-15).

people.name: Eber
people.description: Son of Salah; ancestor of the Hebrews (the name "Hebrew" derives from Eber).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2281 BC (AM 1723), died 1817 BC (464 years, Gen 11:14-17).

people.name: Peleg
people.description: Son of Eber; in his days the earth was divided (Tower of Babel).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2247 BC (AM 1757), died 2008 BC (239 years, Gen 11:16-19). Gen 10:25.

people.name: Reu
people.description: Son of Peleg; continued the post-Flood patriarchal line.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2217 BC (AM 1787), died 1978 BC (239 years, Gen 11:18-21).

people.name: Serug
people.description: Son of Reu; grandfather of Terah.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2185 BC (AM 1819), died 1955 BC (230 years, Gen 11:20-23).

people.name: Nahor
people.description: Son of Serug; grandfather of Abraham. Not to be confused with Abraham's brother Nahor.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2155 BC (AM 1849), died 2007 BC (148 years, Gen 11:22-25).

people.name: Terah
people.description: Son of Nahor; father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran. Died in Haran.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 2126 BC (AM 1878), died 1921 BC (205 years, Gen 11:24-32). Abraham departed after Terah's death (Acts 7:4).

people.name: Haran, brother of Abraham
people.description: Son of Terah and brother of Abraham and Nahor. He was the father of Lot, Milcah and Iscah, and he died in Ur before his father Terah left for Canaan.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals sec. 58: born 2056 BC, when Terah was 70 (Gen 11:26); Abram was born 60 years later (1996 BC, sec. 63). Haran died in Ur before Terah set out (Gen 11:28); Scripture and Ussher give no year for his death.

scripture.context: Father of Lot, Milcah and Iscah; died in Ur

people.name: Nahor, brother of Abraham
people.description: Brother of Abraham who married his niece Milcah. His son Bethuel was the father of Rebekah and Laban, and his family stayed in Mesopotamia.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from his place as Terah's son and brother of Abraham (born 1996 BC). Not to be confused with Nahor, Terah's father. Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Milcah bears him eight sons, including Bethuel

people.name: Abraham
people.description: Patriarch called from Ur of the Chaldees to a land God would show him, receiving the covenant promise that all nations would be blessed through his offspring. His faith, tested in the offering of Isaac, made him the father of the faithful for Jews, Christians, and Muslims alike.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1996 BC (AM 2008), died 1821 BC (175 years, Gen 25:7). Ussher reads Terah as 130 at Abraham's birth (Gen 11:32 with 12:4 and Acts 7:4); a plain reading of Gen 11:26 (Terah 70 when he fathered Abram) would give about 2056 BC, and Abram is probably listed first for rank rather than birth order. Mainstream scholarship, where it dates the patriarchs at all, places them roughly 2000 to 1700 BC.

events.role: Received the covenant sign and circumcised his household (Gen 17)

people.name: Sarah
people.description: Wife of Abraham, mother of Isaac.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1986 BC (10 years younger than Abraham, Gen 17:17), died 1859 BC (127 years, Gen 23:1).

events.role: Promised a son within the covenant (Gen 17:15-16)

people.name: Milcah
people.description: Daughter of Haran and wife of her uncle Nahor. She bore Nahor eight sons, among them Bethuel, the father of Rebekah.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Milcah was born after her father Haran and before her son Bethuel; Scripture gives no dates.

scripture.context: Daughter of Haran; wife of Nahor
Mother of Bethuel and seven other sons

people.name: Lot
people.description: Abraham's nephew; escaped the destruction of Sodom.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Scripture gives no age for Lot; he is Abraham's nephew and travelled with him (Gen 11:27-31; 12:4), and his death is not recorded. Sodom fell c. 1897 BC (Gen 19). The years are estimates, not a figure we can attribute to Ussher.

events.role: Rescued from the city by the angels (Gen 19)

people.name: Bethuel
people.description: Son of Nahor and Milcah, father of Rebekah and Laban. Scripture mentions him by name but records few of his own words or deeds.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born to Nahor and Milcah in the generation after Abraham's brother, and before his children Laban and Rebekah (born 1876 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Son of Milcah; father of Rebekah
Rebekah is born to Bethuel, son of Milcah
Rebekah names her father; Laban her brother

people.name: Hagar
people.description: Sarah's Egyptian servant; mother of Ishmael.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Scripture gives no age for Hagar, and her death is not recorded. Jewish tradition (Pirke de-Rabbi Eliezer 30) identifies her as Pharaoh's daughter; Islamic tradition (Ibn Kathir) places her near Beer-lahai-roi. The years are estimates.

people.name: Ishmael
people.description: Son of Abraham by Hagar; father of twelve princes.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1910 BC (Abraham aged 86, Gen 16:16), died 1773 BC (137 years, Gen 25:17).

people.name: Keturah
people.description: Abraham's wife after Sarah's death; mother of six sons including Midian.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Gen 25:1-4 tells of Abraham's marriage to Keturah and her six sons, after the account of Sarah's death (1859 BC) though the text does not state the order in time; some Jewish tradition identifies her with Hagar. Born about 40 years before that marriage so that she could bear six sons; death not recorded.

people.name: Isaac
people.description: Son of promise, born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age and spared on Mount Moriah when God provided a ram in his place. He reopened his father's wells in the Negev and passed the covenant blessing to Jacob, the quiet link between Abraham and the tribes of Israel.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1896 BC (Abraham aged 100, Gen 21:5), died 1716 BC (180 years, Gen 35:28).

people.name: Moab, son of Lot
people.description: Son of Lot by his elder daughter, born after the destruction of Sodom. Scripture calls him the father of the Moabites, the people from whom Ruth came.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born within a year or so of the destruction of Sodom (1897 BC; Gen 19:30-38). Scripture gives no further dates.

scripture.context: Born to Lot's elder daughter; father of the Moabites

people.name: Ben-ammi
people.description: Son of Lot by his younger daughter. Scripture calls him the father of the Ammonites. His name means "son of my people."
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born within a year or so of the destruction of Sodom (1897 BC; Gen 19:30-38). Scripture gives no further dates.

scripture.context: Born to Lot's younger daughter; father of the Ammonites

people.name: Laban
people.description: Rebekah's brother; father of Leah and Rachel. Tricked Jacob.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Brother of Rebekah (Gen 24:29) and father of Leah and Rachel, and still active when Jacob left Paddan-aram in 1739 BC (Gen 31), so he lived past that year. Birth and death years are estimates.

scripture.context: Brother of Rebekah, son of Bethuel

people.name: Rebekah
people.description: Wife of Isaac, mother of Jacob and Esau.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. She was a 'damsel' when she married Isaac, aged 40, in 1856 BC (Gen 24:16; 25:20), so she is placed about 20 years old then. Her death is not recorded; she was buried at Machpelah (Gen 49:31). The year of death is an estimate.

people.name: Jacob
people.description: Younger twin who obtained birthright and blessing, wrestled with God at Peniel, and received the new name Israel. Father of twelve sons who became Israel's tribes, his long journey from schemer to patriarch traces the transforming grip of covenant grace.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1836 BC (Isaac aged 60, Annals sec. 98; Gen 25:26), died 1689 BC (147 years, sec. 145; Gen 47:28). Fled to Haran 1760 BC (sec. 111, aged 77), married after seven years of service c. 1753 BC (sec. 114), Joseph born 1745 BC (aged 91, sec. 121; Gen 41:46; 45:6; 47:9), returned to Canaan 1739 BC after 20 years with Laban (sec. 123; Gen 31:38, 41).

people.name: Esau
people.description: Jacob's twin brother; sold his birthright; ancestor of the Edomites.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1836 BC (twin of Jacob, Gen 25:26). Death is not recorded in Scripture; 1689 BC is an estimate taking the year of Jacob's death.

people.name: Bilhah
people.description: Rachel's maid, given to Jacob as a wife so that Rachel might have children through her. She bore Dan and Naphtali.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. A young woman in Laban's household when Jacob married (1760 BC, Ussher, Annals section 115), mother of Dan (born about 1748 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

people.name: Zilpah
people.description: Leah's maid, given to Jacob as a wife when Leah had stopped bearing. She bore Gad and Asher.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. A young woman in Laban's household when Jacob married (1760 BC, Ussher, Annals section 115), mother of Gad and Asher (born about 1747 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

people.name: Leah
people.description: Jacob's first wife; mother of six sons and Dinah.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Elder daughter of Laban (Gen 29:16), given to Jacob after his seven years of service, in 1753 BC (Gen 29:20-25); placed about 24 at marriage. Her death is not recorded; she was buried at Machpelah (Gen 49:31).

people.name: Rachel
people.description: Jacob's beloved wife; mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Laban's younger daughter, a shepherdess when Jacob arrived in 1760 BC (Gen 29:9-18), married to him a week after Leah in 1753 BC (29:27-28); placed about 21 at marriage. She bore Joseph in 1745 BC (30:22-25) and died giving birth to Benjamin near Ephrath (35:16-20), placed c. 1730 BC.

people.name: Potiphar
people.description: Egyptian officer who bought Joseph as a slave; captain of Pharaoh's guard.
people.dateNotes: Gen 39:1-20. Captain of Pharaoh's guard. Disappears from narrative after Joseph's imprisonment. Est. death c. 1710 BC.

people.name: Reuben
people.description: Jacob's firstborn; lost his birthright. Tried to save Joseph.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from Scripture: Leah's first son (Gen 29:32), born soon after the marriage of 1753 BC (Gen 29:20-28); placed in 1752 BC. Ussher (Annals 117) has 1758 BC on his earlier dating of the marriage. Entered Egypt in 1706 BC (Gen 46:8-9). Death is not recorded; about 130 years is assumed.

people.name: Simeon
people.description: Second son of Jacob and Leah; ancestor of the tribe of Simeon.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from Scripture: Leah's second son (Gen 29:33), after the marriage of 1753 BC; placed in 1751 BC (Ussher, Annals 118: 1758-1757 BC on his earlier marriage date). Held in prison by Joseph in 1707-1706 BC (Gen 42:24; 43:23). Death is not recorded; about 130 years is assumed.

people.name: Levi
people.description: Third son of Jacob and Leah; ancestor of the priestly tribe. Lived 137 years.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from Scripture: Leah's third son (Gen 29:34), after the marriage of 1753 BC; placed in 1750 BC (Ussher, Annals 119, has 1756 BC on his earlier marriage date). Lived 137 years (Exod 6:16), so died about 1613 BC in Egypt. He fathered Kohath in Canaan and Jochebed in Egypt (Num 26:59).

people.name: Judah
people.description: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah whose offer of himself in place of Benjamin marked one of Genesis's great moments of transformation. Jacob's blessing promised the scepter to his line, and through him came the royal tribe of David and, in Christian reading, the Messiah himself.
people.dateNotes: Estimate from Scripture: Leah's fourth son (Gen 29:35), after the marriage of 1753 BC; placed in 1749 BC (Ussher, Annals 120, has 1755 BC on his earlier marriage date). Entered Egypt in 1706 BC (Gen 46:12). Ussher does not date Gen 38 (Er, Onan, Tamar and Perez). Death is not recorded; about 130 years is assumed.

events.role: brother who had pleaded for Benjamin (Gen 44)

people.name: Dan
people.description: Fifth son of Jacob; ancestor of the tribe of Dan.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Fifth son of Jacob, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah (Gen 30:6); entered Egypt (Gen 46:23). The sons and Dinah are laid out in the order of Gen 29:31-30:24 and 35:16-18 within Ussher's frame (Jacob to Haran and marriage 1760 BC, Leah's first four sons 1758-1755 BC, Joseph born 1745 BC, return 1739 BC: Ussher, Annals sections 112-121, 123); the years are approximate. Death is not recorded; about 130 years is assumed.

events.role: Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:23)

people.name: Naphtali
people.description: Sixth son of Jacob; ancestor of the tribe of Naphtali.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Sixth son of Jacob, born to Bilhah (Gen 30:8); entered Egypt (Gen 46:24). The sons and Dinah are laid out in the order of Gen 29:31-30:24 and 35:16-18 within Ussher's frame (Jacob to Haran and marriage 1760 BC, Leah's first four sons 1758-1755 BC, Joseph born 1745 BC, return 1739 BC: Ussher, Annals sections 112-121, 123); the years are approximate. The non-canonical Testament of Naphtali records 133 years, which gives 1614 BC.

events.role: Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:24)

people.name: Gad
people.description: Seventh son of Jacob; ancestor of the tribe of Gad.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Seventh son of Jacob, born to Leah's servant Zilpah (Gen 30:11); entered Egypt (Gen 46:16). The sons and Dinah are laid out in the order of Gen 29:31-30:24 and 35:16-18 within Ussher's frame (Jacob to Haran and marriage 1760 BC, Leah's first four sons 1758-1755 BC, Joseph born 1745 BC, return 1739 BC: Ussher, Annals sections 112-121, 123); the years are approximate. The non-canonical Testament of Gad records 127 years, which gives 1620 BC.

events.role: Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:16)

people.name: Asher
people.description: Eighth son of Jacob; ancestor of the tribe of Asher.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Eighth son of Jacob, born to Zilpah (Gen 30:13); entered Egypt (Gen 46:17). The sons and Dinah are laid out in the order of Gen 29:31-30:24 and 35:16-18 within Ussher's frame (Jacob to Haran and marriage 1760 BC, Leah's first four sons 1758-1755 BC, Joseph born 1745 BC, return 1739 BC: Ussher, Annals sections 112-121, 123); the years are approximate. The non-canonical Testament of Asher records 127 years, which gives 1619 BC.

events.role: Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:17)

people.name: Issachar
people.description: Ninth son of Jacob; ancestor of the tribe of Issachar.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Ninth son of Jacob and Leah (Gen 30:18); entered Egypt (Gen 46:13). The sons and Dinah are laid out in the order of Gen 29:31-30:24 and 35:16-18 within Ussher's frame (Jacob to Haran and marriage 1760 BC, Leah's first four sons 1758-1755 BC, Joseph born 1745 BC, return 1739 BC: Ussher, Annals sections 112-121, 123); the years are approximate. The non-canonical Testament of Issachar records 122 years, which gives 1624 BC.

events.role: Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:13)

people.name: Joseph
people.description: Favored son of Jacob, sold into Egypt by jealous brothers, who rose from prison to become Pharaoh's vizier through the interpretation of dreams. His grain policy saved Egypt and his own family from famine, and his forgiveness of his brothers remains Scripture's great portrait of providence over evil intent.
people.dateNotes: Scripture: born when Jacob was 91 (Gen 41:46; 45:6; 47:9: Joseph 30 at Pharaoh, nine years before Jacob at 130), at the end of Jacob's 14 years of service (Gen 30:25; 31:41); died aged 110 (Gen 50:26). Jacob's birth in 1836 BC is Ussher's, giving born 1745 BC and died 1635 BC (Annals sections 121, 148).

events.role: son, who brings Ephraim and Manasseh

people.name: Dinah
people.description: Daughter of Jacob and Leah; incident at Shechem.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Daughter of Jacob and Leah, born after Zebulun (Gen 30:21); entered Egypt with Jacob (Gen 46:15). Midrash (Genesis Rabbah 80:11) identifies her as Job's wife. The sons and Dinah are laid out in the order of Gen 29:31-30:24 and 35:16-18 within Ussher's frame (Jacob to Haran and marriage 1760 BC, Leah's first four sons 1758-1755 BC, Joseph born 1745 BC, return 1739 BC: Ussher, Annals sections 112-121, 123); the years are approximate. Death is not recorded; about 68 years is an estimate.

people.name: Zebulun
people.description: Tenth son of Jacob; ancestor of the tribe of Zebulun.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Tenth son of Jacob and Leah (Gen 30:20); entered Egypt (Gen 46:14). The sons and Dinah are laid out in the order of Gen 29:31-30:24 and 35:16-18 within Ussher's frame (Jacob to Haran and marriage 1760 BC, Leah's first four sons 1758-1755 BC, Joseph born 1745 BC, return 1739 BC: Ussher, Annals sections 112-121, 123); the years are approximate. The non-canonical Testament of Zebulun records 114 years, which gives 1631 BC.

events.role: Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:14)

people.name: Tamar
people.description: Daughter-in-law of Judah; mother of Perez and Zerah. In the lineage of David and Jesus.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Scripture gives no dates for Tamar. She became Judah's daughter-in-law and the mother of Perez and Zerah (Gen 38). The years are estimates, and Gen 38 does not fit neatly into the chronology of Judah's sons (see Perez).

people.name: Asenath
people.description: Egyptian wife of Joseph; daughter of Potiphera priest of On. Mother of Manasseh and Ephraim.
people.dateNotes: Gen 41:45, 50-52. Daughter of Potiphera, priest of On. Jewish apocryphal tradition (Joseph and Asenath) describes her conversion. Est. death c. 1640 BC.

events.role: Given to Joseph as wife by Pharaoh (Gen 41:45)

people.name: Benjamin
people.description: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel; born near Bethlehem.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born near Ephrath after Jacob's return in 1739 BC, when Rachel died (Gen 35:16-20), placed c. 1730 BC. At that date he would be about 24 when Jacob entered Egypt in 1706 BC, yet Gen 46:21 lists ten sons for him, a known difficulty (the list may include later descendants). Death is not recorded; about 130 years is an estimate.

people.name: Kohath
people.description: Second son of Levi and grandfather of Moses, Aaron and Miriam. His descendants, the Kohathites, carried the ark and the holy things of the tabernacle.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Ussher, Annals section 151: Levi begot Kohath in Canaan, so he was born before the descent into Egypt in 1706 BC (Gen 46:11); he lived 133 years (Exod 6:18). Scripture and Ussher give no year of birth.

events.role: Grandson of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:11)

scripture.context: The Kohathites' charge over the holy things

people.name: Manasseh, son of Joseph
people.description: Firstborn son of Joseph; adopted by Jacob. Half-tribe of Israel.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born in Egypt before the famine, after Joseph became ruler in 1715 BC (Gen 41:50-51); adopted by Jacob (Gen 48). Death is not recorded; the year is an estimate.

events.role: Joseph's son, born in Egypt and counted among Jacob's house (Gen 46:20,27)

people.name: Ephraim
people.description: Second son of Joseph; adopted by Jacob and given the firstborn blessing.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born in Egypt before the famine, after Manasseh (Gen 41:52); given the firstborn blessing by Jacob (Gen 48:14-20). Death is not recorded; the year is an estimate.

events.role: Joseph's son, born in Egypt and counted among Jacob's house (Gen 46:20,27)

people.name: Perez
people.description: Son of Judah and Tamar; ancestor of David and Jesus.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Judah was born in 1755 BC (Ussher, Annals section 120) and Genesis 38 (Er, Onan and Shelah growing up before Tamar bears Perez) cannot fall much earlier than this. Genesis 46:12 lists Perez and his sons among those who went down to Egypt in 1706 BC, perhaps counted by anticipation.

events.role: Grandson of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:12)

people.name: Job
people.description: A blameless man of Uz whose catastrophic losses became Scripture's deepest exploration of innocent suffering. Refusing his friends' easy explanations, he carried his anguish directly to God, who answered from the whirlwind, and his endurance became proverbial in both testaments.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals (AM 2369, 1635 BC): Job lived at this time and suffered his trials; Scripture fixes no year. Job 42:16: he lived 140 years after his trials, so death about 1495 BC (1635 less 140). Birth 1685 BC is an estimate (he had ten grown children at the time of the trials, Job 1:2, 4). The book names no king or event. Many scholars place Job in the patriarchal age, about 2000 to 1800 BC, or leave it undated.

people.name: Hezron
people.description: Son of Perez; grandson of Judah. Went down to Egypt with Jacob. Ancestor of David and Jesus.
people.dateNotes: Gen 46:12; Ruth 4:18; 1 Chr 2:5. Life dates estimated. Gen 46:12 counts him among those who came into Egypt with Jacob (1706 BC), which leaves very little time after the birth of his father Perez; some interpreters take Hezron and Hamul as born in Egypt but reckoned with Jacob's household.

people.name: Ram
people.description: Son of Hezron; ancestor of David. Mentioned in Ruth's genealogy and Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.
people.dateNotes: Ruth 4:19; 1 Chr 2:9-10; Matt 1:3-4. Life dates estimated.

people.name: Amram
people.description: Levite, son of Kohath, husband of Jochebed and father of Miriam, Aaron and Moses.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. He lived 137 years (Exod 6:20) and, Ussher says (Annals section 151), died shortly before the Israelites left Egypt (1491 BC), which puts his birth about 1630 BC. He was father of Miriam (born c. 1582 BC), Aaron (born 1574 BC) and Moses (born 1571 BC). Exodus 6 may compress the generations between Levi and Moses, as biblical genealogies sometimes do; this timeline follows the text as written.

scripture.context: Married Jochebed; father of Aaron and Moses
Father of Aaron, Moses and Miriam

people.name: Izhar
people.description: Son of Kohath, brother of Amram and uncle of Moses and Aaron. He was the father of Korah, who led the rebellion in the wilderness.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born a few years after his brother Amram, as a son of Kohath (born before 1706 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath

people.name: Jochebed
people.description: Mother of Miriam, Aaron and Moses, who hid her infant son from Pharaoh's decree and was then paid to nurse him for Pharaoh's daughter.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Called a daughter of Levi born in Egypt (Num 26:59) and Amram's father's sister (Exod 6:20), so born after 1706 BC and before Levi's death (c. 1613 BC); placed at about 1620 BC. Her death is not recorded.

scripture.context: Daughter of Levi, mother of Aaron, Moses and Miriam
Hides the infant Moses and nurses him

people.name: Amminadab
people.description: Son of Ram; father of Nahshon. His daughter Elisheba married Aaron. Ancestor of David and Jesus.
people.dateNotes: Ruth 4:19-20; Exod 6:23; 1 Chr 2:10; Matt 1:4. Life dates estimated.

people.name: Jethro
people.description: Moses' father-in-law; priest of Midian who advised Moses on delegation.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated (no age or year is given). Moses married his daughter c. 1531 BC (Exod 2:21), and he visited Moses at Sinai c. 1491-1490 BC (Exod 18; Num 10:29).

events.role: Moses' father-in-law; visited him at the mount of God (Ex 18)

people.name: Hur
people.description: Held up Moses' arms during the battle with Amalek alongside Aaron.
people.dateNotes: Exod 17:10-12; 24:14. Life dates estimated: grandfather of Bezalel (Exod 31:2; 1 Chr 2:19-20) and a leader at Sinai in 1491 BC; last mentioned at Exod 24:14.

people.name: Miriam
people.description: Sister of Moses and Aaron; prophetess.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born c. 1582 BC, reckoning that she lived 130 years (Scripture gives no age); died at Kadesh in the first month of the 40th year (Num 20:1), 1452 BC, four months before Aaron. Daughter of Amram and Jochebed (Num 26:59).

events.role: sister, who watched over the basket
Led the women in song after the crossing (Ex 15:20-21)
Spoke against Moses and died at Kadesh (Num 12; 20:1)

people.name: Aaron
people.description: Elder brother of Moses, his spokesman before Pharaoh, and Israel's first high priest, ancestor of the priestly line. Though he faltered at the golden calf, his benediction endures; the priestly blessing of Numbers 6 appears on the Ketef Hinnom silver amulets, the oldest known copies of biblical text.
people.dateNotes: Scripture: 83 when he and Moses spoke to Pharaoh (Exod 7:7), three years older than Moses (80), and 123 when he died on Mount Hor on the first day of the fifth month of the 40th year (Num 33:38-39). Ussher, Annals sections 160 and 268: born 1574 BC, died 1452 BC; the 122-year difference of the year headings is the 123 years of Scripture counted inclusively (he was born late in the year and died in the summer of the 40th year), a few months before Moses.

events.role: made the calf at the people's demand
Consecrated as priest for the tabernacle (Ex 40:12-15)

people.name: Moses
people.description: Deliverer drawn from the Nile who confronted Pharaoh, led Israel out of Egypt through the sea, and received the law at Sinai. Prophet, lawgiver, and mediator of the covenant, he shepherded Israel through forty wilderness years and viewed the promised land from Nebo; the Torah bears his name.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1571 BC, died 1451 BC (120 years, Deut 34:7). Exodus 1491 BC.

events.role: Oversaw the work and set up the tabernacle (Ex 39-40)

people.name: Nun
people.description: Father of Joshua, Moses' successor. He is named only as "the father of Joshua" and in the genealogy of Ephraim.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-four years before Joshua (born 1536 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Listed in the line of Ephraim as Non, father of Jehoshuah

people.name: Elisheba
people.description: Wife of Aaron, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon, the prince of Judah. She was the mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, and so of Israel's priestly families.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about the same time as Aaron (born 1574 BC) as sister of Nahshon (born about 1550 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

scripture.context: Wife of Aaron; mother of his four sons

people.name: Jephunneh
people.description: Father of Caleb, one of the two faithful spies. He is called a Kenezite, a name linking his family to the clan of Kenaz.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Caleb (born 1530 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenezite

people.name: Beor
people.description: Father of Balaam the seer, who was summoned by the king of Moab to curse Israel. Scripture gives no details of Beor himself.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Balaam (born 1530 BC). In 2 Peter 2:15 the name appears as Bosor.

people.name: Eliab, father of Dathan and Abiram
people.description: Reubenite, son of Pallu and father of Dathan and Abiram, who joined Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty years before Dathan and Abiram (born about 1530 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. Numbers 26:8-9 also names a son Nemuel, not added here.

scripture.context: Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab
Sons of Eliab: Nemuel, Dathan and Abiram

people.name: Zipporah
people.description: Wife of Moses; daughter of Jethro.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Married Moses in Midian c. 1531 BC (Exod 2:21); rejoined him at Sinai (Exod 18:2-5). Death unrecorded.

events.role: Moses' wife; came to him with Jethro (Ex 18:2)

people.name: Uri
people.description: Son of Hur and father of Bezalel, the craftsman of the tabernacle. He is named only in the genealogy of Bezalel.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born between Hur (born 1590 BC) and Bezalel (born 1520 BC). Exodus 31:2 calls Hur his father without further description; identifying this Hur with the Hur who held up Moses' arms (Exod 17:12) is the usual reading but is not stated in the text.

scripture.context: Father of Bezalel, son of Hur

people.name: Joshua son of Nun
people.description: Successor of Moses and one of the two faithful spies, he led Israel across the Jordan, took Jericho, and apportioned the land among the tribes. His farewell charge to choose whom you will serve sealed the covenant at Shechem, and a fierce burn layer at Hazor recalls the conquest narrative.
people.dateNotes: Scripture: died aged 110 (Josh 24:29); the text gives no year. Ussher, Annals 340: died AM 2561, 1443 BC, after living at Timnath-serah many years after the land had rest (c. 1445 BC); birth follows from the age at death (about 62 at the Exodus; Exod 33:11 calls him a young man, using a word that can mean attendant). An earlier c. 1426 BC followed Josephus (Antiquities 5.117).

events.role: waited with Moses on the mountain (Exod 32:17)
spy who urged the people to go up

scripture.context: Oshea the son of Nun, renamed Jehoshua
Moses calls Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua

people.name: Nahshon
people.description: Son of Amminadab; leader of the tribe of Judah during the Exodus. Brother-in-law of Aaron. Ancestor of David.
people.dateNotes: Num 1:7; 2:3; 7:12-17; Ruth 4:20; Matt 1:4. Life dates estimated: prince of Judah at the census of 1490 BC and brother of Aaron's wife Elisheba (Exod 6:23); he died in the wilderness before the second census (Num 26:64-65).

events.role: First prince to bring an offering at its dedication (Num 7:12)

people.name: Pharaoh of the Exodus
people.description: The unnamed Egyptian king who enslaved Israel and defied Moses' demand for release through ten devastating plagues. His army's destruction in the sea sealed Israel's deliverance; Scripture withholds his name, and scholars still debate which historical pharaoh he was.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: Exodus 1491 BC. Perished at the Red Sea (Exod 14:28; Ps 136:15). Identity debated.

people.name: Zippor
people.description: Father of Balak, king of Moab, who hired Balaam to curse Israel. He is named only as Balak's father.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Balak (born 1510 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Balak the son of Zippor, king of the Moabites

people.name: Korah
people.description: Levite who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron; swallowed by the earth.
people.dateNotes: Num 16:1-35. Ussher: c. 1490 BC.

events.role: Led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron (Num 16)

people.name: Nadab, son of Aaron
people.description: Eldest son of Aaron. With his brother Abihu he offered "strange fire" before the LORD and both died at once, soon after the tabernacle was set up.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Aaron's eldest son (Exod 6:23), born about forty years before the Exodus. He died on the day the priesthood began its service, about 1490 BC (Lev 10:1-2; Num 3:4). Not the same as Nadab, king of Israel.

scripture.context: Eldest son of Aaron and Elisheba

people.name: Abihu
people.description: Second son of Aaron. He and his brother Nadab went up with Moses and the elders to see God on Sinai, but died for offering unauthorised fire at the altar.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born just after Nadab. He died with Nadab about 1490 BC, leaving no sons (Lev 10:1-2; Num 3:4).

people.name: Caleb
people.description: One of two faithful spies (with Joshua) who urged Israel to enter Canaan.
people.dateNotes: Born 1530 BC: aged 40 when sent as a spy from Kadesh-barnea (1490 BC) and 85 when he claimed Hebron 45 years later, c. 1445 BC (Josh 14:7-10). Death unrecorded; c. 1420 BC is an estimate.

events.role: spy who urged the people to go up

scripture.context: Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenezite
Gives his daughter Achsah to Othniel

people.name: Balaam
people.description: Pagan prophet hired by Balak to curse Israel; his donkey spoke. Killed by Israel.
people.dateNotes: Num 22-24; 31:8. Killed in the war against Midian in the 40th year, 1452 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated.

people.name: Eleazar son of Aaron
people.description: Son of Aaron; succeeded him as high priest. Served during the conquest.
people.dateNotes: Exod 6:23; Num 20:28; Josh 24:33. Life dates estimated; he succeeded Aaron in 1452 BC and outlived Joshua (Josh 24:33).

people.name: Dathan
people.description: Reubenite who joined Korah's rebellion against Moses; swallowed by the earth.

people.name: Abiram
people.description: Reubenite who joined Korah's rebellion against Moses; swallowed by the earth.

people.name: Gershom
people.description: Elder son of Moses and Zipporah, born in Midian. His name recalls Moses's words, "I have been a stranger in a strange land."
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born in Midian after Moses married Zipporah, about 1531 BC (Exod 2:21-22). His death is not recorded.

events.role: Moses' son; came to him with Jethro (Ex 18:3)

scripture.context: Named for Moses's years as a stranger

people.name: Ithamar
people.description: Youngest son of Aaron. After the deaths of Nadab and Abihu he served as priest with Eleazar and oversaw the work of the Gershonites and Merarites. The line of Eli later traced back to him.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born after Eleazar, before the Exodus (1491 BC). His death is not recorded. Eli is usually taken to be of Ithamar's line (compare 1 Kings 2:27 and 1 Chronicles 24:3), though 1 Samuel does not say so.

scripture.context: Youngest son of Aaron and Elisheba
Oversees the Gershonite and Merarite service

people.name: Eliezer, son of Moses
people.description: Younger son of Moses and Zipporah. His name means "my God is help," for God had delivered Moses from Pharaoh's sword.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born in Midian, after Gershom and before Moses returned to Egypt in 1491 BC (Exod 4:20; 18:3-4). His death is not recorded.

events.role: Moses' son; came to him with Jethro (Ex 18:4)

people.name: Carmi, father of Achan
people.description: Judahite, father of Achan, whose theft of the devoted spoil of Jericho brought defeat at Ai. Joshua's account lists his line back through Zabdi to Zerah.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Achan (born 1490 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. Joshua 7:1 gives the line as Achan, Carmi, Zabdi, Zerah; the names between Carmi and Zerah are not added here.

people.name: Bezalel
people.description: Master craftsman filled with the Spirit of God; built the Tabernacle.
people.dateNotes: Exod 31:1-11; 35:30-35. Filled with the Spirit for Tabernacle construction. Death unrecorded; est. c. 1440 BC (active during wilderness period).

events.role: Craftsman called to build the tabernacle (Ex 31:2-5)

scripture.context: Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur

people.name: Kenaz, father of Othniel
people.description: Father of Othniel, the first judge of Israel. The texts call Othniel "the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother," and the Hebrew does not make clear whether the "younger brother" is Othniel or Kenaz.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about forty-five years before Othniel (born 1470 BC). Caleb is the son of Jephunneh (Num 13:6), so the relationship of Kenaz to Caleb is uncertain: the phrase may mean that Kenaz was Caleb's brother, or that Othniel was a kinsman counted as his brother. No sibling link is recorded here for that reason.

scripture.context: Sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah

people.name: Balak
people.description: King of Moab who hired Balaam to curse Israel.
people.dateNotes: Num 22-24. King of Moab who hired Balaam to curse Israel, shortly before the death of Moses (1451 BC). His death is not recorded; c. 1450 BC is an estimate.

events.role: King of Moab who hired Balaam (Num 22-24)

people.name: Achan
people.description: Israelite who took forbidden plunder from Jericho; caused defeat at Ai.
people.dateNotes: Josh 7:1-26. Ussher, Annals §313: 1451 BC (AM 2553c).

people.name: Salmon
people.description: Son of Nahshon; husband of Rahab according to Matthew. Father of Boaz. Ancestor of David and Jesus.
people.dateNotes: Ruth 4:20-21; Matt 1:4-5; 1 Chr 2:11. Life dates estimated; Matthew makes him the husband of Rahab of Jericho (1451 BC). The line Salmon, Boaz, Obed, Jesse, David spans roughly 1450 to 1085 BC, too long for four generations, so the genealogy is generally taken to be abbreviated, as Hebrew genealogies often are.

people.name: Phinehas
people.description: Zealous priest who stopped a plague by his decisive action.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. A grown man when he killed Zimri at Baal-peor in 1452 BC (Num 25:7-13); still ministering before the ark in the Benjamite war (Judg 20:28), which Ussher places after the death of Joshua's elders, before c. 1413 BC.

events.role: Priest who ended the plague at Baal-peor (Num 25)

people.name: Rahab
people.description: A woman of Jericho who hid Israel's spies and confessed their God as Lord of heaven and earth, securing her family's rescue by a scarlet cord. Grafted into Israel, she appears in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus and is praised for her faith in both Hebrews and James.
people.dateNotes: Josh 2; 6:22-25; Matt 1:5; Heb 11:31. Life dates estimated; an adult at the fall of Jericho in 1451 BC.

people.name: Achsah
people.description: Daughter of Caleb, offered in marriage to whoever would take Kirjath-sepher. Othniel took the city and married her, and she then asked her father for springs of water to go with her southern land.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Married when Caleb was about eighty-five (Josh 14:10; 15:16-19), so born in the 1470s BC. Scripture gives no dates for her.

scripture.context: Given to Othniel after Kirjath-sepher is taken

people.name: Othniel
people.description: First judge of Israel: Othniel son of Kenaz, "Caleb's younger brother" (Judg 3:9), of Judah, who took Kirjath-sepher and married Caleb's daughter Achsah. The Spirit of the LORD came upon him and he delivered Israel from Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia (Judg 3:8-11).
people.dateNotes: Took Kirjath-sepher (Debir) in Joshua's lifetime, which Ussher dates 1446 BC (Annals §328; Josh 15:16-17; Judg 1:11-13), so born by about 1470 BC. Delivered Israel 1405 BC (Annals §342; the eight years of Cushan began 1413, §341) after eight years of oppression by Cushan-rishathaim (Judg 3:8-10). Ussher measures each period of rest (Judg 3:11, 3:30, 5:31, 8:28) from the previous deliverance, so the figure includes the oppression that he ended. Birth and death are estimates; Judg 3:11 records his death without a year. The texts call Othniel the son of Kenaz and Caleb's (younger) brother; since Caleb is the son of Jephunneh (Num 13:6), the wording is ambiguous and no sibling link is recorded.

people.name: Gera, father of Ehud
people.description: Benjamite, father of Ehud, the left-handed judge who killed Eglon, king of Moab.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Ehud (born 1365 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. Other men of the same name appear in Benjamin's genealogies.

scripture.context: Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite

people.name: Ehud
people.description: Left-handed Benjamite judge, son of Gera, who killed Eglon king of Moab with a hidden dagger and then led Israel to subdue Moab (Judg 3:15-30).
people.dateNotes: Moab oppressed Israel eighteen years (Judg 3:14), c. 1343-1325 BC; Ehud killed Eglon c. 1325 BC (Ussher), who counts the eighty years of rest (Judg 3:30) from Othniel's deliverance. Israel sinned again "when Ehud was dead" (Judg 4:1), before Jabin's oppression began c. 1305 BC. Birth and death are estimates.

people.name: Abinoam
people.description: Father of Barak, who led Israel's army with Deborah against Sisera. He was from Kedesh in Naphtali.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Barak (born 1320 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Barak the son of Abinoam of Kedesh-naphtali

people.name: Shamgar
people.description: Son of Anath, named after Ehud as one who "also delivered Israel", killing six hundred Philistines with an ox goad (Judg 3:31). The Song of Deborah recalls "the days of Shamgar" as a time when the highways were deserted (Judg 5:6).
people.dateNotes: No years are given. Ussher places him after Ehud (c. 1325 BC), and Judg 5:6 makes him an older contemporary of Deborah and Jael (c. 1285 BC). Life dates are estimates.

scripture.context: Shamgar delivers Israel with an ox goad

people.name: Joash, father of Gideon
people.description: Abiezrite of Ophrah, father of Gideon. He kept an altar to Baal that Gideon tore down, and defended his son when the townsmen demanded his death.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Gideon (born 1300 BC). Not the same as Joash, king of Judah. Scripture gives no dates for him.

people.name: Deborah
people.description: Prophet and judge who held court beneath a palm in the hill country of Ephraim, she summoned Barak and led Israel to victory over Sisera's Canaanite forces. The Song of Deborah in Judges 5 is widely regarded as one of the oldest poems preserved in the Hebrew Bible.
people.dateNotes: Jabin of Hazor oppressed Israel twenty years (Judg 4:3), c. 1305-1285 BC; Deborah and Barak defeated Sisera c. 1285 BC (Ussher), who counts the forty years of rest (Judg 5:31) from Ehud's deliverance. "A mother in Israel" (Judg 5:7) at the victory; birth and death are estimates.

people.name: Barak
people.description: Military commander who fought alongside Deborah against Sisera.
people.dateNotes: Judg 4-5; Heb 11:32. Life dates estimated around the victory over Sisera, c. 1285 BC (Ussher).

people.name: Sisera
people.description: Canaanite general defeated by Deborah and Barak; killed by Jael.
people.dateNotes: Judg 4-5. Killed by Jael on the day of his defeat, c. 1285 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated.

people.name: Heber the Kenite
people.description: Kenite, of the family of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law. He had separated from the other Kenites and pitched his tent near Kedesh, at peace with Jabin of Hazor; his wife Jael killed Sisera.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Husband of Jael (born about 1315 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him, and the Kenite clan is described as living at peace with Jabins Canaanite kingdom at the time of Sisera's defeat (about 1285 BC).

scripture.context: A Kenite who had pitched his tent near Kedesh
Jael is his wife; his house is at peace with Jabin

people.name: Jael
people.description: Kenite woman who killed Sisera by driving a tent peg through his temple.
people.dateNotes: Judg 4:17-22; 5:24-27. Killed Sisera with a tent peg, c. 1285 BC (Ussher). Life dates estimated.

people.name: Gideon
people.description: Judge called from threshing wheat in a winepress to deliver Israel from Midian, he routed a vast host with only three hundred men so the glory would be God's alone. Also named Jerubbaal; a jar inscription bearing that rare name was unearthed at Khirbet al-Rai in the Judean foothills.
people.dateNotes: Midian oppressed Israel seven years (Judg 6:1), c. 1252-1245 BC; Gideon's victory c. 1245 BC (Ussher). Ussher counts the forty years of quiet "in the days of Gideon" (Judg 8:28) from Deborah's victory, so Gideon died c. 1236 BC, when Abimelech seized power. His age is not given: his firstborn Jether was still a youth at the victory (Judg 8:20), and he died "in a good old age" (Judg 8:32). Birth is an estimate. Annals §356-357.

people.name: Tola
people.description: A man of Issachar, son of Puah, who lived at Shamir in Mount Ephraim and judged Israel twenty-three years after Abimelech (Judg 10:1-2).
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel 23 years (Judg 10:1-2), c. 1233-1210 BC (Ussher), and died. Birth estimated. Annals §360, §366.

people.name: Abimelech
people.description: Son of Gideon who made himself king; killed at Thebez.
people.dateNotes: Son of Gideon's concubine in Shechem (Judg 8:31). Made king at Shechem after Gideon's death, c. 1236 BC; reigned three years (Judg 9:22) and was killed at Thebez c. 1233 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated. Annals §358-360.

people.name: Jair
people.description: Judge of Israel for 22 years; had 30 sons who rode 30 donkeys.
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel 22 years (Judg 10:3-5), c. 1210-1188 BC (Ussher). Ussher begins the eighteen-year oppression by the Ammonites and Philistines (Judg 10:7-8) c. 1206 BC, in Jair's time, although the narrative tells it after his burial, and ends it with Jephthah's victory in 1188 BC, the year Jair died. Birth estimated. Annals §366-370.

people.name: Gilead, father of Jephthah
people.description: Father of Jephthah the Gileadite. The text names him as the father, while also noting that Jephthah's mother was a prostitute; his other sons drove Jephthah out.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty years before Jephthah (born 1225 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. The name is also that of a region east of the Jordan.

people.name: Boaz
people.description: Kinsman-redeemer who married Ruth; ancestor of David.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated: a kinsman of Elimelech, much older than Ruth (Ruth 2:1; 3:10), father of Obed c. 1170 BC. Matthew names Rahab of Jericho (1451 BC) as his mother (Matt 1:5); as that is nearly three centuries before Ruth's story, the link Salmon-Boaz is generally taken to be abbreviated, "begat" meaning "was ancestor of".

people.name: Ibzan
people.description: Judge of Israel from Bethlehem for 7 years; had 30 sons and 30 daughters.
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel seven years after Jephthah (Judg 12:8-10), c. 1182-1175 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated; he had married off thirty sons and thirty daughters.

people.name: Abdon
people.description: Son of Hillel the Pirathonite, of Ephraim, who judged Israel eight years; he had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy ass colts (Judg 12:13-15).
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel eight years (Judg 12:13-15), c. 1165-1157 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated; he had grandsons of riding age. Annals §377-378.

people.name: Elimelech
people.description: Man of Bethlehem who took his wife Naomi and sons Mahlon and Chilion to Moab in a famine and died there. Boaz later redeemed his land.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about ten years before Naomi (born 1225 BC); he died in Moab, within the period of the judges, before his sons (Ruth 1:1-5). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Goes to Moab with Naomi and their sons and dies there
Boaz buys all that was Elimelech's

people.name: Jephthah
people.description: Gileadite warrior, driven out by his half-brothers, who was recalled to lead Gilead against the Ammonites and defeated them. His rash vow cost him his only daughter, and he afterwards fought the men of Ephraim (Judg 11:1-12:7).
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel six years (Judg 12:7), c. 1188-1182 BC (Ussher), after defeating the Ammonites. His "three hundred years" since Israel took Heshbon (Judg 11:26; Heshbon taken 1452 BC) are about 264 on this reckoning, so a round figure; reconstructions that run the Ammonite and Philistine oppressions together (Judg 10:7) date him several decades later. Birth estimated; he had a grown daughter at the victory.

people.name: Naomi
people.description: Ruth's mother-in-law who returned from Moab to Bethlehem.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Of Bethlehem; returned from Moab a widow, too old to remarry (Ruth 1:12), and nursed her grandson Obed (Ruth 4:16), c. 1170 BC on these estimates. The book is set "when the judges ruled" (Ruth 1:1) without saying which judge.

scripture.context: Husband Elimelech; sons Mahlon and Chilion

people.name: Elon
people.description: A Zebulonite who judged Israel ten years and was buried at Aijalon in Zebulun (Judg 12:11-12).
people.dateNotes: Judged Israel ten years (Judg 12:11-12), c. 1175-1165 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated. Annals §374, §377.

people.name: Eli
people.description: High priest at Shiloh who judged Israel forty years and brought up the boy Samuel. His failure to restrain his sons Hophni and Phinehas brought judgment on his house, and he died at 98 when news came that the ark had been taken (1 Sam 1-4).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1214 BC; judged Israel forty years (1 Sam 4:18), c. 1157-1116 BC, following Abdon, and died aged 98 on hearing that the ark was taken (1 Sam 4:15-18), 1116 BC. Annals §365, §378, §386.

scripture.context: Dies on hearing of his son's death and the ark's capture

people.name: Abiel
people.description: Benjamite, grandfather of King Saul and of Abner. His sons Kish and Ner were brothers, so Saul and Abner were cousins.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before his sons Kish and Ner. 1 Samuel 9:1 and 14:51 call both of them sons of Abiel; 1 Chronicles 8:33 and 9:39 give a different arrangement (Ner begat Kish; 9:36 lists them as brothers), and the genealogies are hard to reconcile. This timeline follows 1 Samuel.

people.name: Manoah
people.description: Father of Samson; visited by the Angel of the LORD.
people.dateNotes: Judg 13-14; 16:31. Life dates estimated: Samson was born c. 1155 BC, Manoah went with him to Timnah (Judg 14:5), and Samson was buried in Manoah's tomb (Judg 16:31).

people.name: Mahlon
people.description: Elder son of Elimelech and Naomi, who married Ruth the Moabite and died childless in Moab. Boaz married Ruth to raise up his name.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about twenty-five years after his parents' birth; he married about ten years before dying in Moab (Ruth 1:4-5). His death is not dated.

scripture.context: Dies in Moab; Ruth is his widow
Ruth is bought to raise up his name

people.name: Chilion
people.description: Younger son of Elimelech and Naomi, husband of Orpah. He died in Moab without children.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born just after Mahlon; he died in Moab about ten years after the marriages (Ruth 1:4-5). His death is not dated.

scripture.context: Dies in Moab; Orpah is his widow

people.name: Orpah
people.description: Moabite woman, wife of Chilion. After his death she kissed Naomi goodbye and stayed in Moab while her sister-in-law Ruth went on to Bethlehem.
people.dateNotes: Estimate; she married about the time Ruth did (Ruth 1:4). Scripture gives no dates for her.

people.name: Ruth
people.description: Moabite great-grandmother of David.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. The story is set "in the days when the judges ruled" (Ruth 1:1); placing Obed's birth c. 1170 BC leaves a natural three generations to David (b. 1085 BC). Boaz praised her for not following young men (Ruth 3:10).

scripture.context: Wife of Mahlon, bought by Boaz

people.name: Elkanah, father of Samuel
people.description: Man of Ramathaim in the hills of Ephraim who went up yearly to Shiloh with his wives Hannah and Peninnah. He was the father of Samuel.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about forty years before Samuel (born 1150 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. 1 Samuel 1:1 calls him an Ephrathite, while 1 Chronicles 6:27-28 lists a Levite Elkanah as father of Samuel; the sources differ on his tribe.

scripture.context: Husband of Hannah; goes up to Shiloh

people.name: Hannah
people.description: Mother of Samuel; prayed fervently for a child and dedicated him to God.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated (1 Sam 1-2); mother of Samuel (born c. 1150 BC).

people.name: Hophni
people.description: Elder son of Eli, priest at Shiloh with his brother Phinehas. The two abused the sacrifices and were condemned by a prophet; both died on the day the Philistines took the ark.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born while Eli (born 1214 BC) was in his thirties. His death in the battle in which the ark was captured (1116 BC) is dated by that event (1 Sam 4:11).

scripture.context: Priest at Shiloh, son of Eli
Doomed to die with his brother in one day
Slain when the ark is taken

people.name: Phinehas, son of Eli
people.description: Younger son of Eli, priest at Shiloh with Hophni. He died in the battle in which the ark was taken, and his wife died giving birth to Ichabod on hearing the news.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born shortly after Hophni. His death in the battle in which the ark was captured (1116 BC) is dated by that event (1 Sam 4:11). Not the same as Phinehas, son of Eleazar.

scripture.context: Priest at Shiloh, son of Eli
Dies when the ark is taken; Ichabod is born

people.name: Obed
people.description: Son of Boaz and Ruth; father of Jesse, grandfather of David. Central link in the Messianic lineage.
people.dateNotes: Ruth 4:13-17, 21-22; 1 Chr 2:12; Matt 1:5. Life dates estimated.

people.name: Kish
people.description: Benjamite, "a mighty man of power," father of King Saul. Saul was sent out to look for his father's lost donkeys on the day Samuel met him.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before Saul (born 1135 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Son of Abiel; father of Saul

people.name: Ner
people.description: Benjamite, brother of Kish and uncle of King Saul. His son Abner commanded Saul's army.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born near his brother Kish, about forty years before Abner (born 1130 BC). The KJV of 1 Samuel 14:50 calls Abner "Saul's uncle," but verse 51 shows Ner to be the uncle and Abner the cousin. 1 Chronicles 8:33 places Ner as Kish's father; this timeline follows 1 Samuel.

scripture.context: Father of Abner; son of Abiel

people.name: Samson
people.description: Nazirite judge endowed with extraordinary strength, he battled the Philistines single-handedly until Delilah's betrayal cost him his hair, his eyes, and his freedom. In death he toppled Dagon's temple, and his story mirrors Israel's own struggle with compromised devotion.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born c. 1155 BC, soon after the Philistines' forty years of domination began (Judg 13:1); judged Israel twenty years "in the days of the Philistines" (Judg 15:20; 16:31), c. 1137-1117 BC, and died at Gaza in 1117 BC, the year before Eli. Annals §380, §382, §384.

people.name: Samuel
people.description: Last of the judges and first of the great prophets, dedicated at the Shiloh sanctuary in answer to Hannah's prayer. He anointed both Saul and David, guiding Israel's passage from tribal confederation to monarchy while insisting that obedience outweighs sacrifice.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated (Ussher gives no year). Serving Eli at Shiloh as a child (1 Sam 1-3), he judged Israel after Eli's death in 1116 BC, routed the Philistines at Mizpah c. 1096 BC (1 Sam 7), anointed Saul in 1095 BC and David c. 1063 BC, and died c. 1060 BC, before David's second flight to Gath (1 Sam 25:1; 27:1-2).

people.name: Delilah
people.description: A woman of the valley of Sorek whom Samson loved. Bribed by the Philistine lords, she drew out the secret of his strength and betrayed him (Judg 16:4-21); Scripture does not say whether she was a Philistine or an Israelite.
people.dateNotes: Judg 16:4-21. Betrayed Samson c. 1117 BC (Ussher). Life dates are estimates.

people.name: Jesse
people.description: A Bethlehemite of the tribe of Judah, grandson of Ruth and Boaz, and father of eight sons, the youngest of whom Samuel anointed as king. Isaiah's promise of a shoot from the stump of Jesse made his name shorthand for the messianic hope Christians see fulfilled in Jesus.
people.dateNotes: 1 Sam 16:1-13; 17:12-14; Ruth 4:22; Isa 11:1, 10; Matt 1:5-6. Life dates estimated: "an old man in the days of Saul" (1 Sam 17:12), father of David (b. 1085 BC) in his old age.

people.name: Saul
people.description: Israel's first king, a tall Benjaminite anointed by Samuel, who won early victories over Ammon and the Philistines. His impatience and disobedience cost his house the throne, and his tragic decline beside David's rise ended on Mount Gilboa, where he fell in battle.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned forty years (Acts 13:21), 1095-1055 BC, and fell at Gilboa. His age at accession is not given (the Hebrew of 1 Sam 13:1 is defective); the birth year is an estimate allowing for a son, Jonathan, who commanded a thousand men in Saul's second year (1 Sam 13:2). Mainstream scholarship dates his reign c. 1050-1010 BC.

scripture.context: Kish was the father of Saul

people.name: Ahitub, father of Zadok
people.description: Priest, father of Zadok, who served David and anointed Solomon. He is not the Ahitub who was the grandson of Eli.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about forty-five years before Zadok (born 1090 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him. 1 Chronicles 6:8 places Zadok in the line of Eleazar, whereas Eli's Ahitub was of the line of Ithamar.

people.name: Abner
people.description: Commander of Saul's army; supported Ish-bosheth then defected to David. Killed by Joab.
people.dateNotes: Birth estimated: son of Ner, Saul's uncle (1 Sam 14:50-51), and already captain of Saul's army early in the reign. Killed by Joab at Hebron in 1048 BC (Ussher; 2 Sam 3:27). Annals §415.

people.name: Ahinoam, wife of Saul
people.description: Wife of King Saul, daughter of Ahimaaz. The text names her as his wife but does not say which of his children were hers. She is a different woman from David's wife Ahinoam of Jezreel.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Roughly the age of Saul (born 1135 BC), who had grown sons by the time he became king. Scripture gives no dates for her.

people.name: Joel, son of Samuel
people.description: Eldest son of Samuel. With his brother Abiah he judged at Beer-sheba, but they took bribes and perverted justice, and the elders used their conduct to ask for a king.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born while Samuel (born 1150 BC) was in his twenties; Samuel made his sons judges when he was old (1 Sam 8:1-2), shortly before Saul's anointing in 1095 BC. 1 Chronicles 6:28 gives the firstborn's name as Vashni; the two names are commonly reconciled but the text does not say so.

people.name: Abiah, son of Samuel
people.description: Second son of Samuel, judge at Beer-sheba with his brother Joel. Their corruption led Israel's elders to ask Samuel for a king.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born shortly after Joel; Samuel made his sons judges when he was old (1 Sam 8:1-2). His death is not recorded.

scripture.context: Listed among the sons of Samuel
Samuel's second son; judge at Beer-sheba

people.name: Eliab, son of Jesse
people.description: Eldest son of Jesse. Samuel took him for the Lord's anointed because of his height, but God had chosen another; later he rebuked David for coming to the battle line against Goliath.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty-five years before David (born 1085 BC), as the eldest of Jesse's eight sons. Scripture gives no dates for him.

events.role: rebukes David at the battle line

scripture.context: Passed over when Samuel looks for the king
Eldest of the three sons with Saul's army

people.name: Abinadab, son of Jesse
people.description: Second son of Jesse. He was passed over by Samuel and followed Saul to the battle against the Philistines.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born between Eliab and Shammah (about 1120 to 1114 BC). Scripture gives no dates for him.

scripture.context: Passed over when Samuel looks for the king
Second of the three sons with Saul's army

people.name: Ichabod
people.description: Son of Phinehas and grandson of Eli, born as his mother died after hearing that the ark was lost. She named him Ichabod, "the glory has departed." His brother Ahitub appears in 1 Samuel 14:3.
people.dateNotes: Born at the time the ark was captured (1116 BC; 1 Sam 4:19-21). The text does not record his death. Ussher, Annals §386.

events.role: born on the day the ark was taken

scripture.context: Born as the ark is taken; named Ichabod

people.name: Jonathan
people.description: Saul's son and David's closest friend; died at Gilboa.
people.dateNotes: Birth estimated: he commanded a thousand men in Saul's second year (1 Sam 13:2-3), c. 1093 BC, and had a five-year-old son when he died (2 Sam 4:4). Died with Saul at Gilboa, 1055 BC (Ussher; 1 Sam 31:2).

people.name: Shammah, son of Jesse
people.description: Third son of Jesse, passed over by Samuel and a soldier in Saul's army. The Chronicles list him as Shimma; his son Jonadab, a wily man, advised Amnon.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty years before David (born 1085 BC). The identification of Shammah (1 Sam 16:9; 17:13) with Shimma (1 Chron 2:13) and Shimeah (2 Sam 13:3) is the usual reading; the text gives the names separately.

scripture.context: Passed over when Samuel looks for the king
Third of the three sons with Saul's army

people.name: Ahithophel
people.description: David's counselor who defected to Absalom; hanged himself when his advice was rejected.
people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 15:12, 31; 16:20-17:23. Hanged himself during Absalom's revolt, 1023 BC. If Bathsheba's father Eliam (2 Sam 11:3) is the Eliam son of Ahithophel among David's mighty men (2 Sam 23:34), he was her grandfather; the birth year is an estimate allowing for that. Ussher, Annals §442-444.

people.name: Merab
people.description: Saul's elder daughter, offered to David as a reward for fighting the Philistines but given instead to Adriel the Meholathite.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born before her younger sister Michal (born 1085 BC) and after Jonathan (born 1115 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

scripture.context: Promised to David, given to Adriel

people.name: Jether, father of Amasa
people.description: Husband of Abigail, David's sister, and father of Amasa. 1 Chronicles calls him an Ishmaelite; 2 Samuel calls him Ithra an Israelite.
people.dateNotes: Estimate; born slightly before his wife Abigail (born about 1106 BC). The two names and descriptions (Jether the Ishmaelite, 1 Chron 2:17; Ithra the Israelite, 2 Sam 17:25) are usually taken to be one man, with a difference in the manuscripts.

people.name: Zeruiah
people.description: Sister of David and mother of the three brothers Joab, Abishai and Asahel, who served in his army. The text calls her David's sister but does not name her husband or say which parent she shared with David.
people.dateNotes: Estimate, born before her son Joab (born 1085 BC). 1 Chronicles 2:16 calls Zeruiah and Abigail "sisters" of Jesse's sons. 2 Samuel 17:25 calls Abigail the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah, so Zeruiah and Abigail may have had a different father or mother from David; no parent is recorded for her here.

scripture.context: Sister of Jesse's sons; mother of Abishai, Joab and Asahel

people.name: Abigail, sister of David
people.description: Sister of David and of Zeruiah, mother of Amasa, whom Absalom made commander of his army. She is a different woman from Abigail the wife of Nabal and David.
people.dateNotes: Estimate, born before her son Amasa. 1 Chronicles 2:16 calls her a sister of Jesse's sons; 2 Samuel 17:25 calls her the daughter of Nahash. The text does not reconcile the two, and no parent is recorded for her here.

scripture.context: Sister of Jesse's sons; mother of Amasa
Daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah

people.name: Nabal
people.description: Wealthy but foolish man married to Abigail; refused to help David. Died after the LORD struck him.
people.dateNotes: 1 Sam 25:2-42. Died about ten days after his feast (1 Sam 25:38), soon after Samuel's death and before David fled to Gath, c. 1060 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Ish-bosheth
people.description: Saul's surviving son; made king over Israel by Abner while David reigned in Judah.
people.dateNotes: Scripture: forty when he began to reign, and reigned two years (2 Sam 2:10). Ussher, Annals 409: he was made king at Mahanaim in 1055 BC, the year of Saul's death, so born 1095 BC, the year Saul became king; the two years are the two years of peace with David, followed by a long war (2 Sam 3:1; Annals 411), and he was murdered in 1048 BC (Annals 416), just before the tribes made David king (2 Sam 4-5). Others place his two years at the end of David's seven and a half years at Hebron, making him born c. 1090 BC.

people.name: Eliam, father of Bathsheba
people.description: Father of Bathsheba, wife of Uriah and later of David. 2 Samuel 23:34 names an Eliam son of Ahithophel among David's mighty men; the text does not say that the two are the same man.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born about thirty years before Bathsheba (born 1065 BC). 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives her father as Ammiel, a reversal of the same name. Scripture gives no dates for him.

people.name: Abigail
people.description: Wise woman who became David's wife after the death of Nabal.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Married David after Nabal's death, c. 1060 BC (1 Sam 25); with him at Ziklag and Hebron (1 Sam 30:5; 2 Sam 2:2) and mother of his second son (2 Sam 3:3). Death unrecorded.

people.name: David
people.description: Shepherd of Bethlehem who felled Goliath and rose to the throne after Saul, uniting the tribes and taking Jerusalem as his capital. Psalmist and covenant king promised an everlasting dynasty, his house is named on the Tel Dan stele, the earliest extrabiblical witness to his royal line.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: born 1085 BC; anointed by Samuel at Bethlehem c. 1063 BC; king at Hebron aged 30 in 1055 BC and over all Israel from 1048 BC; reigned forty years, seven and a half at Hebron and thirty-three at Jerusalem (2 Sam 5:4-5), and died 1015 BC. Mainstream scholarship dates his reign c. 1010-970 BC.

people.name: Nathan the prophet
people.description: Prophet during David and Solomon's reigns.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Active from the Davidic covenant (c. 1044 BC, 2 Sam 7) to Solomon's anointing (1015 BC, 1 Kgs 1).

events.role: prophet who helped secure the succession

people.name: Joab
people.description: Commander of David's army; politically shrewd and ruthless.
people.dateNotes: Birth estimated; son of David's sister Zeruiah (1 Chr 2:16). Executed by Benaiah at Solomon's command early in his reign, 1014 BC (Ussher; 1 Kgs 2:28-34).

events.role: commander who carried out the order

scripture.context: One of the three sons of Zeruiah

people.name: Michal
people.description: Saul's daughter; David's first wife who helped him escape.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Saul's younger daughter (1 Sam 14:49), married to David after his victory over Goliath (c. 1063-1062 BC), given to Phaltiel, and returned to David in 1048 BC (2 Sam 3:14-16). Childless (2 Sam 6:23). Death unrecorded.

people.name: Ahinoam of Jezreel
people.description: One of David's wives, taken during his years as a fugitive from Saul. She bore his first son, Amnon.
people.dateNotes: Estimate, a contemporary of David (born 1085 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

scripture.context: Taken by David as a wife

people.name: Abishai
people.description: Son of Zeruiah, nephew of David, and one of his best-known commanders. He went with David into Saul's camp by night and later saved David's life in battle.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born between his brothers Joab (born 1085 BC) and Asahel. His death is not recorded in Scripture.

events.role: commander of a third of David's army

scripture.context: One of the three sons of Zeruiah

people.name: Asahel
people.description: Youngest son of Zeruiah and a nephew of David, "light of foot as a wild roe." He pursued Abner after the battle at Gibeon and was killed by him, which later led Joab to kill Abner.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born after Joab (1085 BC) and Abishai. He was killed in the first years of David's reign at Hebron, about 1055 BC (2 Sam 2:18-23).

scripture.context: Third of the three sons of Zeruiah

people.name: Amasa
people.description: Nephew of David and cousin of Joab. Absalom made him commander of his army; after Absalom's death David offered him Joab's place, and Joab killed him.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born after his mother Abigail (born about 1106 BC); an adult commander by Absalom's revolt (1023 BC). His death is not dated in this table.

people.name: Zadok the priest
people.description: Faithful priest who supported David and anointed Solomon. His line continued as high priests.
people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 15:24-29; 1 Kgs 1:32-45; Ezek 44:15. Life dates estimated; "a young man mighty of valour" when he came with the tribes to David at Hebron (1 Chr 12:27-28), 1048 BC (Ussher, Annals 413), so born about 1075 BC. Anointed Solomon with Nathan in 1015 BC (1 Kgs 1:39; Annals 457).

events.role: Priest summoned to bring up the ark (1 Chr 15:11)
priest who stayed loyal to David

people.name: Maacah, daughter of Talmai
people.description: Princess of Geshur, a wife of David and the mother of Absalom and Tamar. Her father Talmai gave Absalom refuge after he killed Amnon.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born before Absalom (born 1053 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her. Not the same as Maacah, daughter of Absalom, Rehoboam's wife.

scripture.context: Mother of Absalom, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur

people.name: Hiram
people.description: King of Tyre; ally of David and Solomon. Supplied materials for the Temple.
people.dateNotes: On Ussher's dates Hiram sent builders to David c. 1046 BC (2 Sam 5:11) and still dealt with Solomon c. 992 BC (1 Kgs 9:10-14). Josephus (Against Apion 1.18, from Menander of Ephesus) gives him a reign of 34 years and a life of 53, which mainstream chronology places c. 980-947 BC; on that reckoning 2 Sam 5:11 is told out of sequence. Life dates are estimates.

people.name: Shimei
people.description: Cursed David during Absalom's rebellion; later executed by Solomon.
people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 16:5-13; 19:16-23; 1 Kgs 2:36-46. Executed three years after Solomon confined him to Jerusalem, 1011 BC (Ussher). Birth estimated.

people.name: Hushai
people.description: David's friend who pretended to join Absalom and thwarted Ahithophel's counsel.
people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 15:32-37; 16:16-17:16. Active in Absalom's revolt, 1023 BC (Ussher, Annals 442-445). Life dates estimated; Scripture gives no ages.

people.name: Haggith
people.description: Wife of David and mother of Adonijah, who tried to take the throne before Solomon was crowned.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born before Adonijah (born 1051 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

people.name: Bathsheba
people.description: Wife of David; mother of Solomon.
people.dateNotes: Life dates estimated. Taken by David c. 1035 BC (Ussher; 2 Sam 11); mother of Solomon (b. 1034 BC); alive early in Solomon's reign (1 Kgs 2:19). Death unrecorded.

events.role: mother, who pleaded for her son

people.name: Mephibosheth
people.description: Son of Jonathan; lame in both feet. David showed him kindness for Jonathan's sake.
people.dateNotes: Born 1060 BC: five years old when news came of the deaths of Saul and Jonathan in 1055 BC (2 Sam 4:4; Ussher). 2 Sam 9:1-13; 16:1-4; 19:24-30. Death unrecorded; c. 1000 BC is an estimate.

people.name: Uriah
people.description: Loyal soldier; husband of Bathsheba. Killed by David's order to cover his sin.
people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 11:1-27; Matt 1:6. Ussher, Annals 433: killed at the siege of Rabbah in 1035 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Amnon
people.description: David's firstborn, born at Hebron. He raped his half-sister Tamar and was killed two years later on Absalom's orders.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born at Hebron in the first year of David's reign there (David anointed there 1055 BC; 2 Sam 3:2). His death at Absalom's sheep-shearing is not dated in the text.

scripture.context: David's firstborn, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess
Listed first among the sons born at Hebron

people.name: Chileab
people.description: David's second son, born at Hebron to Abigail, widow of Nabal. He is mentioned once in Samuel; Chronicles calls him Daniel.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born at Hebron the year after Amnon (2 Sam 3:3). 1 Chronicles 3:1 gives the name Daniel; the two are usually taken to be the same son. His death is not recorded.

scripture.context: David's second son, of Abigail the wife of Nabal

people.name: Absalom
people.description: David's rebellious son who temporarily seized the throne.
people.dateNotes: Born at Hebron to Maacah (2 Sam 3:2-3), so before David took Jerusalem in 1048 BC; Ussher (Annals 410) puts the marriage to Maacah in 1055 BC; exact birth year estimated. Scripture's sequence: Amnon's crime, two full years to the sheepshearing (2 Sam 13:23), three years in Geshur (13:38), two full years in Jerusalem before seeing the king (14:28), then revolt "after forty years" (15:7; the Septuagint, Syriac and Josephus read four). Ussher counts the forty from David's anointing (1063 BC) and dates Amnon's murder 1030 BC and the revolt and death 1023 BC (Annals 437-445).

scripture.context: Son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai

people.name: Adonijah
people.description: David's fourth son who tried to seize the throne; executed by Solomon.
people.dateNotes: Fourth son of David, born at Hebron after Absalom (2 Sam 3:4); birth estimated. Claimed the throne as David lay dying in 1015 BC and was executed by Solomon early in his reign, 1014 BC (Ussher; 1 Kgs 1-2).

people.name: Tamar, daughter of David
people.description: Beautiful daughter of David and full sister of Absalom, assaulted by her half-brother Amnon. Absalom took her into his house and later killed Amnon.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born in the years after Absalom (born 1053 BC), before the rape described in 2 Samuel 13. Not the same as Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law.

scripture.context: Absalom's fair sister, loved by Amnon
Named as the sister of David's sons

people.name: Naamah the Ammonitess
people.description: Wife of Solomon and mother of King Rehoboam. She was from Ammon, one of the foreign peoples whose women are named among Solomon's wives.
