people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born before Rehoboam (born 1016 BC). Scripture gives no dates for her.

people.name: Solomon
people.description: Son of David famed for God-given wisdom, he built the first temple in Jerusalem and presided over a golden age of trade, building, and proverbs. Monumental gates at Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer have long been associated with his projects, yet his foreign marriages sowed the kingdom's division.
people.dateNotes: Scripture: reigned forty years (1 Kgs 11:42); began the Temple in his 4th year, the 480th year from the Exodus (1 Kgs 6:1), and finished it in seven years (6:38), then built his own house thirteen years (7:1). Ussher, Annals 435, 459, 465: born 1034 BC to Bathsheba after the death of her first child by David (2 Sam 12:24), so about 19 at his accession; reign 1015-975 BC; Temple begun 1012 BC and finished 1005 BC; palace 1005-992 BC. Rehoboam was 41 when Solomon died (1 Kgs 14:21), so born the year before Solomon took the throne (Annals 455). Mainstream scholarship dates his reign c. 970-931 BC.

people.name: Nathan son of David
people.description: Son of David and Bathsheba. Ancestor of Jesus in Luke 3:31. Not the prophet Nathan.
people.dateNotes: 2 Sam 5:14; 1 Chr 3:5; Luke 3:31. Born in Jerusalem to Bathsheba. 1 Chr 3:5 lists him before Solomon, but Solomon was evidently her first son after the death of the child of 2 Sam 12 (c. 1034 BC), so a birth c. 1030 BC is estimated. Not to be confused with Nathan the prophet (2 Sam 7).

people.name: Rehoboam
people.description: Solomon's son; his harshness caused the kingdom to divide.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 975-958 BC (17 years, 1 Kgs 14:21); 41 at accession, so born 1016 BC. Thiele: 931-913 BC.

events.role: Rival king in Jerusalem whose temple the calves were meant to replace
King of Judah; surrendered the temple treasures

people.name: Jeroboam
people.description: First king of the northern kingdom of Israel.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 975-954 BC (22 years counted inclusively, 1 Kgs 14:20); Nadab succeeded in Asa's second year (1 Kgs 15:25). Thiele: 931-910 BC. Birth estimated.

events.role: Made the two calves and a rival priesthood
King of Israel defeated by Judah

people.name: Abijah
people.description: King of Judah, son of Rehoboam. Reigned 3 years. Ancestor of Jesus in Matthew 1:7.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 958-955 BC (3 years, 1 Kgs 15:1-2), from the 18th year of Jeroboam. Birth estimated: the text gives no age, but he had fourteen wives and 38 children (2 Chr 13:21). Thiele: 913-911 BC. Not to be confused with Abijah the priest.

events.role: King of Judah who led Judah to victory

people.name: Nadab
people.description: Son and successor of Jeroboam I; killed by Baasha after two years.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 954-953 BC (2 years counted inclusively, 1 Kgs 15:25-28), killed by Baasha in Asa's third year. Thiele: 910-909 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Baasha
people.description: King of Israel who destroyed the house of Jeroboam.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 953-930 BC (24 years counted inclusively, 1 Kgs 15:33); Elah succeeded in Asa's 26th year (16:8). Thiele: 909-886 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Asa
people.description: Good king of Judah who removed idols and sought the Lord.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 955-914 BC (41 years, 1 Kgs 15:9-10), from the 20th year of Jeroboam. Birth estimated: his son Jehoshaphat was 35 when Asa died (1 Kgs 22:42) and Asa was diseased in his feet in his old age (1 Kgs 15:23). Thiele: 911-870 BC. 1 Kings 15:9-24; 2 Chronicles 14-16. Scripture gives Asa's accession in the 20th year of Jeroboam (1 Kgs 15:9), while Jeroboam's 22 years (14:20) and Nadab's accession in Asa's 2nd year (15:25) make Asa's first year Jeroboam's 21st; Ussher's harmonising choice (Abijah's 3 years run 958-955) puts Asa's first year at 955 BC, in Jeroboam's 20th year as it ended. The 36th year of 2 Chr 16:1 is counted from the division of the kingdom, i.e. Asa's 16th (940 BC, Annals Sec. 496), since Baasha died in Asa's 26th year (1 Kgs 16:6-8).

people.name: Omri
people.description: King of Israel who founded Samaria; politically powerful but godless.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 929-918 BC (12 years, 1 Kgs 16:23), at first contested by Tibni; his sole rule began in Asa's 31st year. Named on the Moabite Stone. Thiele: 885-874 BC. Birth estimated. Scripture: Omri began in Asa's 31st year and reigned 12 years (1 Kgs 16:23), yet Ahab began in Asa's 38th (16:29), only seven years later. Ussher's choice (Annals Sec. 500-503): the 12 years are counted from 929 BC, Asa's 27th year, when the army made him king; Tibni's rival party held half the people for about four years until Omri prevailed in the 31st.

events.role: King who bought the hill and built the city

people.name: Zimri
people.description: King of Israel for only seven days; died by suicide during Omri's siege.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned seven days in 929 BC, the 27th year of Asa (1 Kgs 16:15-18). Thiele: 885 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Elah
people.description: King of Israel, son of Baasha, who reigned two years. While he was drinking himself drunk in his steward's house at Tirzah, Zimri, captain of half his chariots, killed him and destroyed the house of Baasha, as the prophet Jehu son of Hanani had foretold (1 Kgs 16:1-14).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 930-929 BC (2 years counted inclusively, 1 Kgs 16:8), from the 26th year of Asa; killed in Asa's 27th year (16:10). Thiele: 886-885 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.description: Good king of Judah who strengthened the nation and sent teachers through the land.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 914-889 BC (25 years, 1 Kgs 22:42), from the 4th year of Ahab. Age 35 at accession: born 949 BC. Thiele: 872-848 BC (including a coregency).

events.role: King who taught and judged Judah
King of Judah allied with Ahab
King of Judah who joined it

people.name: Ahab
people.description: Wicked king of Israel; husband of Jezebel.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 918-897 BC (22 years counted inclusively, 1 Kgs 16:29), from Asa's 38th year; killed at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kgs 22:34-37). Thiele: 874-853 BC; Shalmaneser III's Kurkh Monolith names him at Qarqar in 853 BC. Birth estimated.

events.role: King of Israel killed in battle

people.name: Jezebel
people.description: Phoenician wife of Ahab; promoted Baal worship and persecuted prophets.
people.dateNotes: Her marriage to Ahab is reported at his accession in 918 BC (1 Kgs 16:31) and may have been earlier. Killed by Jehu in 884 BC (2 Kgs 9:30-37). Birth estimated.

events.role: Queen whose threat drove him out

people.name: Widow of Zarephath
people.description: Poor widow who fed Elijah during the famine; her son was raised from death.
people.dateNotes: 1 Kgs 17:8-24; Luke 4:25-26. Cared for Elijah during Ahab's reign c. 910 BC per Ussher. Son raised from death. Est. death c. 870 BC.

events.role: Widow who sheltered him; her son was raised

people.name: Elijah
people.description: Prophet of Gilead who confronted Ahab and the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, where fire from heaven vindicated the Lord. Fed by ravens and met by a still small voice at Horeb, he was taken up in a whirlwind, and Malachi promises his return before the great day of the Lord.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: active during Ahab's reign (918-897 BC). Translated c. 896 BC (2 Kgs 2:11), early in Joram of Israel's reign. 2 Chr 21:12-15 records a writing from Elijah to Jehoram of Judah (reigned from 892 BC): either it was written before his translation or the dating is uncertain. Born c. 930 BC (estimated).

events.role: Prophet sustained by God in the drought
Prophet who met God at Horeb
Pronounced judgment on Ahab and Jezebel

people.name: Naaman
people.description: Syrian army commander healed of leprosy by Elisha.
people.dateNotes: Healed during the reign of Jehoram of Israel, c. 890 BC on Ussher's chain (2 Kgs 5-6). Birth estimated; death unrecorded, estimate only.

people.name: Athaliah
people.description: Wicked queen of Judah who usurped the throne and killed royal heirs.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 884-878 BC (six years, 2 Kgs 11:3), after Ahaziah's death in 884; killed in the seventh year when Joash was crowned (2 Kgs 11:4-16; Annals §535-536). Birth 927 BC from Annals §502 (as it seems, 42 years before her son Ahaziah began to reign in 885). Thiele: 841-835 BC. Called daughter of Ahab (2 Kgs 8:18) and of Omri (8:26), i.e. Ahab's daughter and Omri's granddaughter.

people.name: Jehoram of Judah
people.description: Wicked king of Judah who married Ahab's daughter and led Judah astray.
people.dateNotes: Ussher chain: reigned 892-885 BC (8 years, 2 Kgs 8:16-17), from the fifth year of Joram of Israel while Jehoshaphat was still living; 2 Kgs 1:17 implies an earlier association with his father. Age 32 at accession: born 924 BC; died at about 40 (2 Chr 21:20). Thiele: 848-841 BC, coregent from 853.

people.name: Ahaziah of Israel
people.description: Son of Ahab; wicked king who sought Baal-zebub instead of God.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: began in Jehoshaphat's 17th year as viceroy to his father Ahab (898 BC, 1 Kgs 22:51; Annals Sec. 516), sole king after Ahab's death in 897 and dead in 896 BC; his two years (22:51) were partly with his father, partly alone (Annals Sec. 521). Thiele: 853-852 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Elisha
people.description: Farmer called from the plow to succeed Elijah, receiving a double portion of his spirit. Serving Israel through the reigns of four kings, he healed Naaman's leprosy, multiplied bread and oil, and raised the dead, extending God's mercy to Israelite and foreigner alike.
people.dateNotes: Called by Elijah in Ahab's reign (1 Kgs 19:19-21), before Ahab died in 897 BC; succeeded Elijah c. 896 BC (2 Kgs 2). Died early in the reign of Jehoash of Israel (2 Kgs 13:14-20), c. 839 BC (Ussher). Born c. 920 BC (estimated).

events.role: Prophet who promised water and victory
Sent the prophet who anointed Jehu

people.name: Jehoram of Israel
people.description: Son of Ahab; last king of the Omride dynasty; killed by Jehu.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 896-884 BC (12 years, 2 Kgs 3:1), from Jehoshaphat's 18th year; killed by Jehu (2 Kgs 9:24). Brother of Ahaziah, who had no son (2 Kgs 1:17); the text does not say which was older. Synchronisms: 18th year of Jehoshaphat (2 Kgs 3:1) and 2nd year of Jehoram of Judah (1:17), the latter reconciled by Ussher through Jehoram's earlier viceroyalty (Annals Sec. 515). Thiele: 852-841 BC. Birth estimated.

events.role: King of Israel who led the campaign

people.name: Jehu
people.description: Anointed by Elisha's servant; destroyed the house of Ahab and Baal worship.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 884-856 BC (28 years, 2 Kgs 10:36). Thiele: 841-814 BC; Shalmaneser III's Black Obelisk shows him paying tribute in 841 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Hazael
people.description: King of Aram (Syria) whose accession Elisha foretold in Damascus; he smothered Ben-hadad and reigned in his place, and oppressed Israel through the reigns of Jehu and Jehoahaz.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: king of Aram by 884 BC, when he had recently succeeded Ben-hadad as Elisha foretold (2 Kgs 8:7-15, 28-29; Annals Sec. 533); the accession year (c. 885) is an estimate. He oppressed Israel through the reign of Jehoahaz (856-840 BC; 2 Kgs 10:32; 13:3, 22) and sent a force against Jerusalem in Joash of Judah's last year, 839 BC (2 Kgs 12:17-18; Sec. 544). He was dead when Jehoash of Israel recovered cities from his son Ben-hadad (2 Kgs 13:24-25; Sec. 546), so death is placed c. 838 BC (estimate; was 840). Inscriptions of Shalmaneser III name him king of Damascus by 841 BC; modern dates c. 842-800 BC. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Shunammite Woman
people.description: Wealthy woman who provided for Elisha; her son was raised from death by Elisha.
people.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 4:8-37; 8:1-6. Son raised by Elisha early in his ministry (from c. 896 BC per Ussher). Returned from Philistia after a seven-year absence and appealed to the king, probably Jehoram (896-884 BC). Birth and death estimated (death c. 840 BC).

people.name: Gehazi
people.description: Servant of Elisha who was struck with leprosy for greed after Naaman's healing.
people.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 4:12-37; 5:20-27; 8:4-5. Struck with leprosy for greed during Elisha's ministry (c. 896-839 BC per Ussher, Annals §523, §545). Still alive when telling the king of Israel, probably Jehoram (896-884 BC), about Elisha (2 Kgs 8:4-5). Birth and death estimated (death c. 840 BC).

people.name: Ahaziah of Judah
people.description: Son of Jehoram and Athaliah; king of Judah for one year. Killed by Jehu.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 885-884 BC (1 year, 2 Kgs 8:25-26), from the 12th year of Joram of Israel. Age 22 at accession: born 907 BC; 2 Chr 22:2 reads 42, which would make him older than his father and is usually taken as a copyist's error. Killed by Jehu (2 Kgs 9:27-28). Thiele: 841 BC.

events.role: Son whose death began her rule

people.name: Jehoahaz of Israel
people.description: King of Israel, son of Jehu, who reigned seventeen years. Hazael of Aram and his son Ben-hadad oppressed Israel throughout his reign until he besought the Lord, who gave Israel a deliverer (2 Kgs 13:1-9).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 856-840 BC (17 years counted inclusively, 2 Kgs 13:1), from the 23rd year of Joash of Judah. Thiele: 814-798 BC. Birth estimated. Not Jehoahaz (Shallum) of Judah.

people.name: Joash of Judah
people.description: Boy king hidden in the Temple; restored proper worship under Jehoiada's guidance.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 878-839 BC (40 years counted inclusively, 2 Kgs 12:1), from the 7th year of Jehu; slain by his servants (2 Kgs 12:20-21). Age 7 at accession (2 Kgs 11:21): born 885 BC. Thiele: 835-796 BC.

events.role: Infant heir hidden in the temple

people.name: Jehoash of Israel
people.description: King of Israel, son of Jehoahaz. He wept over the dying Elisha, struck the ground only three times with the arrows, and so defeated Ben-hadad three times (2 Kgs 13:14-25). He also defeated Amaziah of Judah at Beth-shemesh and broke down part of Jerusalem's wall (2 Kgs 14:8-14).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 16 years (2 Kgs 13:10), 840-825 BC counted from his father Jehoahaz's death; made viceroy in the latter end of the 37th year of Joash of Judah (842 BC, 2 Kgs 13:10; Annals Sec. 542), which accounts for the 37th-year synchronism although Jehoahaz's 17 years from Joash's 23rd end in 840. Amaziah began in Jehoash's 2nd year (14:1) = 839 BC, and Amaziah outlived him by 15 years (14:17). Thiele: 798-782 BC. Birth estimated. Not Joash (Jehoash) of Judah.

people.name: Joel
people.description: Prophet who described a locust plague and the Day of the Lord.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §553: prophesied in Judah under Uzziah (810-758 BC) and Jeroboam II, around the 13th Jubilee (808 BC), before Amos. The book names no king and modern dates range from the 9th to the 4th century BC. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Amaziah
people.description: King of Judah who followed the Lord at first but later turned to idols.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 839-810 BC (29 years, 2 Kgs 14:2), from the second year of Jehoash of Israel; he outlived Jehoash by 15 years (14:17) and Jeroboam II began in his 15th year (14:23). Age 25 at accession: born 864 BC. Thiele: 796-767 BC.

people.name: Jeroboam II
people.description: Powerful king of Israel who expanded borders but tolerated idolatry.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: sole reign 825-784 BC (41 years, 2 Kgs 14:23), from Amaziah's 15th year. Ussher also makes him viceroy to his father Jehoash from 836 BC (Annals Sec. 546), counting from which Uzziah's accession in 810 BC falls in Jeroboam's 27th year (2 Kgs 15:1; Sec. 552). Jonah, Amos and Hosea were active in his reign (2 Kgs 14:25; Amos 1:1; Hos 1:1). Thiele: 793-753 BC (coregent from 793). Birth estimated.

events.role: King of Israel who recovered the territory
First king named in his call

people.name: Jonah
people.description: Prophet sent to Nineveh; swallowed by a great fish after fleeing.
people.dateNotes: Foretold the restoration of Israel's borders achieved by Jeroboam II (2 Kgs 14:25), who reigned 825-784 BC on Ussher's chain; the mission to Nineveh is undated. Birth and death estimated (death c. 750 BC).

people.name: Uzziah
people.description: Good king of Judah who became proud and was struck with leprosy.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §547: born 826 BC, 16 at accession (2 Kgs 15:2). §552: reigned 810-759 BC (52 years), succeeding Amaziah in the 27th year of Jeroboam II reckoned from a coregency. §584: died in 759 BC, the year of Isaiah's vision (Isa 6:1); Jotham succeeded him. §564: struck with leprosy when an old man, soon after Menahem took the throne of Israel (about 771 BC); Jotham judged the people meanwhile. Thiele: 792-740 BC (coregent from 792).

events.role: King of Judah in whose days he prophesied
King whose death dates the vision

people.name: Amos
people.description: Shepherd-prophet from Tekoa who denounced social injustice in Israel.
people.dateNotes: Prophesied in the days of Uzziah (810-758) and Jeroboam II (825-784), two years before the earthquake (Amos 1:1): between 810 and 784 BC on Ussher's chain, c. 760 BC in modern reckoning. Birth and death estimated (death c. 740 BC).

people.name: Zechariah of Israel
people.description: King of Israel, son of Jeroboam II and the last of Jehu's dynasty, who reigned six months before Shallum son of Jabesh killed him before the people. His fall fulfilled the word that Jehu's sons would sit on the throne to the fourth generation (2 Kgs 15:8-12; 10:30).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned six months in 773-772 BC, from the 38th year of Azariah (2 Kgs 15:8), after an interregnum following Jeroboam II's death. Thiele: 753 BC. Birth estimated. Not the prophet Zechariah.

people.name: Shallum of Israel
people.description: Usurper who killed Zechariah son of Jeroboam II and reigned over Israel a full month in Samaria, until Menahem son of Gadi came up from Tirzah and killed him (2 Kgs 15:10-15).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: one month in 772 BC, in the 39th year of Uzziah (2 Kgs 15:13). Thiele: 752 BC. Birth estimated. Not Shallum (Jehoahaz) of Judah.

people.name: Menahem
people.description: King of Israel for ten years who seized the throne by killing Shallum and brutally sacked Tiphsah (2 Kgs 15:14-16). He paid Pul king of Assyria a thousand talents of silver, raised from Israel's wealthy men, to secure his kingdom (2 Kgs 15:19-20).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 772-761 BC (ten years from the 39th year of Azariah, 2 Kgs 15:17; Pekahiah succeeded in Azariah's 50th, 15:23). Thiele: 752-742 BC; Assyrian records list Menahem of Samaria among Tiglath-pileser III's tributaries c. 738 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Hosea
people.description: Prophet who married Gomer to illustrate God's love for unfaithful Israel.
people.dateNotes: Prophesied in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah of Judah and of Jeroboam II of Israel (Hos 1:1): on Ussher's chain from before 784 BC into Hezekiah's reign (from 726 BC). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Pekahiah
people.description: King of Israel, son of Menahem, who reigned two years before Pekah son of Remaliah, one of his captains, killed him in the palace at Samaria (2 Kgs 15:23-26).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 761-759 BC, from the 50th year of Azariah (2 Kgs 15:23). Thiele: 742-740 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Isaiah
people.description: Jerusalem prophet who saw the Lord enthroned in the temple and counseled kings Ahaz and Hezekiah through the Assyrian crisis. His visions of Immanuel and the suffering servant shaped messianic hope, and the great Isaiah scroll from Qumran is the best preserved of the Dead Sea Scrolls.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §583-584: called in 759 BC, the year Uzziah died (Isa 6:1); the Annals (§553) also place him in Judah under Uzziah, earlier. Tradition: martyred by Manasseh c. 695 BC (cf. Heb 11:37; Annals §682). Isa 37:38 reports Sennacherib's death, which Assyrian records date to 681 BC, so either Isaiah outlived 695 or the notice was added later. Born c. 783 BC (estimated; Ussher gives no birth year).

events.role: Prophet who gave the Immanuel sign
Prophet who gave the sign and the warning

people.name: Jotham
people.description: Good king of Judah who built the upper gate of the Temple.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §584: succeeded Uzziah in 759 BC and reigned 16 years (2 Kgs 15:33); §597: Ahaz succeeded him in 742 BC. §564: born 783 BC; age 25 at accession in the Annals' reckoning of 2 Kgs 15:33 (783 to 759 is 24 years counted inclusively). Thiele: 750-732 BC (coregent with Uzziah from 750).

people.name: Pekah
people.description: King of Israel, son of Remaliah, who killed Pekahiah and allied with Rezin of Aram against Ahaz of Judah (2 Kgs 16:5; Isa 7:1-9). In his days Tiglath-pileser took Galilee and Gilead and carried their people captive, and Hoshea son of Elah conspired against him and killed him (2 Kgs 15:29-30).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 759-739 BC (20 years from the 52nd year of Azariah, 2 Kgs 15:27, 15:32); Ahaz began at the end of his 17th year (2 Kgs 16:1; Annals §597). He was killed by Hoshea in the 20th year of Jotham (2 Kgs 15:30), counted from Jotham's first year in 759, which is 739 BC and the 4th year of Ahaz (§610). Hoshea's peaceful reign counts from the 12th year of Ahaz (730 BC, 2 Kgs 17:1), after nine years of anarchy. Thiele: 752-732 BC (partly overlapping); Assyrian records place his fall c. 732 BC. Birth estimated.

events.role: King of Israel who attacked Jerusalem
King of Israel who lost Galilee

people.name: Tiglath-Pileser III
people.description: Assyrian king who seized Galilee and Gilead from Pekah (2 Kgs 15:29) and answered Ahaz's plea by capturing Damascus (2 Kgs 16:7-9). He began the Assyrian deportations of Israel (2 Kgs 15:29; 1 Chr 5:26, which names Pul and Tilgath-pilneser).
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §596: began to reign in 747 BC as "Ninus the younger" (19 years, Castor); §604, §607: took Damascus and Galilee in 740 BC, the 3rd year of Ahaz; §615: died in 728 BC and was succeeded by Shalmaneser. Ussher keeps Pul apart from him: Pul took Menahem's tribute in 771 BC (2 Kgs 15:19-20; §574-576), and 1 Chr 5:26 names the two kings separately. Birth unknown (estimate). Mainstream: Pul and Tiglath-pileser are one king, reigned 745-727 BC.

people.name: Jezreel, son of Hosea
people.description: First child of Hosea and Gomer. The Lord told Hosea to give him the name Jezreel, a sign that the blood shed at Jezreel would be avenged on the house of Jehu.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born in the time of Jeroboam II, shortly before the fall of Jehu's dynasty in 772 BC (Hos 1:4), so about 776 BC. His death is not recorded.

scripture.context: Named Jezreel at the Lord's command

people.name: Micah
people.description: Prophet who foretold Bethlehem as the Messiah's birthplace.
people.dateNotes: Prophesied in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah (Mic 1:1; Jer 26:18), 759-698 BC on Ussher's chain (Annals §585, §653). Micah 1:1; 5:2. Birth and death estimated.

events.role: Prophet whose warning is said to have moved him (Jer 26:18-19)

people.name: Lo-ruhamah
people.description: Daughter of Gomer and Hosea's second child. Her name means "not pitied." Hosea 1:6 says Gomer "bare a daughter" without the words "to him," as it says of the first child, but the children are given their names as signs to Hosea and are counted as his.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born after Jezreel, about 774 BC (Hos 1:6). Her death is not recorded.

scripture.context: Named Lo-ruhamah at the Lord's command

people.name: Lo-ammi
people.description: Son of Gomer and the third child. His name means "not my people." As with Lo-ruhamah, the text says Gomer "bare a son" and the children are counted as Hosea's.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born after Lo-ruhamah was weaned (Hos 1:8), about 771 BC. His death is not recorded.

scripture.context: Named Lo-ammi at the Lord's command

people.name: Hoshea
people.description: Last king of Israel; kingdom fell to Assyria during his reign.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: killed Pekah in the 20th year of Jotham, 739 BC (2 Kgs 15:30; Annals §610), then reigned 9 years from the 12th year of Ahaz, 730 BC (2 Kgs 17:1; §614), after nine years of anarchy; Hezekiah began in his 3rd year (2 Kgs 18:1) and Samaria fell in his 9th, 721 BC, Hezekiah's 6th (2 Kgs 18:10; §633). Imprisoned by the king of Assyria (17:4); his death is unrecorded, so the death year is approximate. Thiele: 732-723 BC. Birth estimated.

people.name: Ahaz
people.description: Wicked king of Judah who practiced child sacrifice and shut the Temple doors.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §597: reigned 742-726 BC (16 years, 2 Kgs 16:1-2), from the 17th year of Pekah. §579: born 762 BC (age 20 at accession). Taken as written, the figures make Ahaz about 10 at the birth of Hezekiah (born 752 BC, §586; Ussher himself counts 11 and cites Tremellius, who read the 20 years as Jotham's accession rather than Ahaz's); the text is kept and the difficulty is unresolved. Thiele: 732-715 BC. Isaiah 7.

events.role: King of Judah who refused to trust
King of Judah who submitted to Assyria

people.name: Hezekiah
people.description: A reforming king of Judah who purged idolatry and trusted God when Sennacherib's Assyrian army besieged Jerusalem. His water tunnel from the Gihon spring survives, and the Siloam inscription found in it in 1880 records his workmen's feat, corroborating the biblical account.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §586: born 752 BC to Ahaz and Abi, daughter of Zachariah; 25 at accession (2 Kgs 18:2). §617, §620: made viceroy in Ahaz's last year (727) and reigned alone from 726; 29 years, to 698 BC (§682). Samaria fell in his sixth year (721 BC, §633) and Sennacherib came in his fourteenth (713 BC, §642, §645), after which fifteen years were added to his life (2 Kgs 20:6). By these figures Ahaz was about 10 at Hezekiah's birth (§579). Thiele and most modern scholars: 715-686 BC, with Sennacherib's invasion in 701 BC.

events.role: Last king named in his call
Last king named in his call
King who restored the temple and Passover

people.name: Shear-jashub
people.description: Son of the prophet Isaiah. His name means "a remnant shall return," and Isaiah brought him to meet King Ahaz as a sign.
people.dateNotes: Estimate. He was old enough to walk with his father when Isaiah met Ahaz during the attack of Syria and Israel (Isa 7:1-3), so born around 750 BC. His death is not recorded.

scripture.context: Taken by Isaiah to meet King Ahaz

people.name: Sennacherib
people.description: Assyrian king who besieged Jerusalem under Hezekiah; his army destroyed by the angel of the LORD.
people.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 18:13-19:37; Isa 36-37. Reigned 705-681 BC. His annals (Sennacherib's Prism) date the campaign against Hezekiah to 701 BC; Ussher's chain places it in Hezekiah's 14th year, 713 BC. Assassinated by his sons in 681 BC (2 Kgs 19:37). Birth estimated.

people.name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
people.description: Son of Isaiah and the prophetess. His name, "swift is the plunder, speedy is the spoil," was a sign that Damascus and Samaria would fall to Assyria before the child could say "my father."
people.dateNotes: Estimate. Born at the time of the sign given to Ahaz, when Syria and Israel threatened Judah (Isa 8:1-4; Ussher, Annals §598-599, under 742 BC), about 742 BC. His death is not recorded.

scripture.context: Born to Isaiah and the prophetess; given his sign-name

people.name: Manasseh
people.description: Most wicked king of Judah who later repented in exile.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 698-643 BC (55 years, 2 Kgs 21:1). Age 12 at accession: born 710 BC, within the fifteen years added to Hezekiah's life. Thiele: 697-642 BC (coregent from 697).

events.role: King who led Judah into idolatry

people.name: Nahum
people.description: Prophet who foretold the fall of Nineveh.
people.dateNotes: Prophesied after the fall of No-amon (Nah 3:8) and before the fall of Nineveh. Ussher, Annals §657: No fell to Sennacherib in 712 BC; §739: Nineveh was taken in 626 BC. The year is an estimate between them (c. 660 BC here; Josephus, §585, has Nahum under Ahaz). Mainstream: Thebes fell to Ashurbanipal in 663 BC and Nineveh in 612. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Hilkiah
people.description: High priest who found the Book of the Law in the Temple during Josiah's reforms.
people.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 22:8-14; 2 Chr 34:14-21. Found the book of the law in the 18th year of Josiah (2 Kgs 22:3), 624 BC on Ussher's chain (Annals §742). Birth and death estimated.

events.role: High priest who served at the temple

people.name: Amon
people.description: Son of Manasseh; evil king of Judah for 2 years. Assassinated by his servants.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 643-641 BC (2 years, 2 Kgs 21:19). Age 22 at accession: born 665 BC. Killed by his servants (21:23). Thiele: 642-640 BC.

people.name: Zephaniah
people.description: Prophet during Josiah's reign who warned of the Day of the Lord. His line is given in Zephaniah 1:1 back to Hizkiah, who may be King Hezekiah; that is likely to some readers but not certain, and this table does not link the two.
people.dateNotes: Prophesied in the days of Josiah (Zeph 1:1), 641-610 BC on Ussher's chain; Ussher places his warnings with Jeremiah's call in 629 BC (Annals §737), before the reform of 624 BC (§742). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Huldah
people.description: Prophetess in Jerusalem consulted by King Josiah about the Book of the Law found in the Temple.
people.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 22:14-20; 2 Chr 34:22-28. Consulted in the 18th year of Josiah, 624 BC on Ussher's chain (Annals §742). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.description: The weeping prophet who warned Judah for decades of coming Babylonian judgment, endured imprisonment and a muddy cistern, and promised a new covenant written on the heart. Clay bullae from the City of David bear names of royal officials, such as Jehucal son of Shelemiah, who appear in his book.
people.dateNotes: Called in the 13th year of Josiah (Jer 1:2), 629 BC on Ussher's chain (Annals §737; 627 in modern reckoning), while still a youth (1:6); active to the fall of Jerusalem and afterwards in Egypt (Jer 43-44). Birth and death estimated; tradition says he was stoned in Egypt.

people.name: Habakkuk
people.description: Prophet who questioned God about evil and received answers about faith.
people.dateNotes: The book foresees the rise of the Chaldeans (Hab 1:6) and is usually dated c. 610-600 BC, late in Josiah's reign or under Jehoiakim; it names no king. Contemporary of Jeremiah. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Josiah
people.description: Judah's young king whose temple repairs uncovered the book of the law, igniting the kingdom's most sweeping religious reform. He centralized worship in Jerusalem, renewed the covenant, and kept a Passover unmatched since the judges; scholars link his lawbook to Deuteronomy.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 641-610 BC (31 years, 2 Kgs 22:1). Age 8 at accession: born 649 BC, when Amon was about 16; the text's figures also make Josiah about 14 at the birth of Jehoiakim (25 in 610, 2 Kgs 23:36). Killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho (2 Kgs 23:29). Thiele and modern scholarship: 640-609 BC.

events.role: King in whose days he was called

people.name: Jehoiakim
people.description: King of Judah who burned Jeremiah's scroll and rebelled against Babylon.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 610-599 BC (11 years, 2 Kgs 23:36). Age 25 at accession: born 635 BC. Thiele and modern scholarship: 609-598 BC.

events.role: Placed on the throne by Necho
King of Judah under whom it happened
Father whose death opened the way

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.description: The Babylonian king who besieged Jerusalem, destroyed Solomon's temple, and carried Judah into exile, yet appears in Daniel as a ruler humbled to confess the Most High. The Babylonian Chronicle preserves his own court's terse record of the first capture of the city.
people.dateNotes: Scripture ties his reign to the kings of Judah: his 1st year is Jehoiakim's 4th (Jer 25:1; Dan 1:1), the 18th is Zedekiah's 10th (Jer 32:1), Jehoiachin was taken in his 8th (2 Kgs 24:12) and Jerusalem burned in his 19th (2 Kgs 25:8). Ussher, Annals §768-782, 890: viceroy from 607 BC (20 months), sole king from 605 on his father's death, died 562 BC after 43 years alone. Mainstream: reigned 605-562 BC (Babylonian Chronicle), with the fall of Jerusalem in 587/586. Birth estimated (c. 634-630 BC).

people.name: Jehoahaz of Judah
people.description: Son of Josiah, made king by the people of the land at 23 after his father fell at Megiddo. He reigned three months before Pharaoh Necho bound him at Riblah and took him to Egypt, where he died (2 Kgs 23:30-34; Jer 22:10-12).
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned three months in 610 BC (2 Kgs 23:31); age 23 at accession, so born 633 BC. Modern scholarship: 609 BC. Called Shallum in Jer 22:11 and 1 Chr 3:15. Died in Egypt at an unrecorded date. Not Jehoahaz of Israel; Ahaziah of Judah is also called Jehoahaz (2 Chr 21:17).

people.name: Ezekiel
people.description: Priest deported to Babylon who received his prophetic call amid visions of the divine chariot beside the Chebar canal. Through stark symbolic acts he interpreted Jerusalem's fall and foresaw dry bones living and a new temple; cuneiform records of Judean exile settlements corroborate his community's setting.
people.dateNotes: Taken to Babylon with Jehoiachin (2 Kgs 24:14-16), 599 BC on Ussher's chain (597 modern; Annals §796). Called on 24 July 595 BC, in the fifth year of that captivity (Ezek 1:2; Annals §821). Ussher reads the thirtieth year of 1:1 as thirty years from Josiah's reform of 624 BC; others read it as Ezekiel's age. Last dated oracle in the 27th year (29:17), c. 573 BC. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Daniel
people.description: A Judean noble exiled to Babylon who rose to high office under Babylonian and Persian rulers while refusing to compromise his devotion to God. His deliverance from the lions' den and his sweeping visions of successive empires shaped Jewish and Christian hope in God's coming kingdom.
people.dateNotes: Deported as a youth in the 4th year of Jehoiakim by Ussher's count (Dan 1:1-6), 607 BC (Annals §776; 605 modern). His last dated vision is in the third year of Cyrus (Dan 10:1), 535 BC counting from the edict of 537 (Annals §956; 536 BC in modern reckoning); Ussher puts his death shortly after, which is left unrecorded here. Birth and death estimated.

events.role: Taken captive and trained at court

people.name: Zedekiah
people.description: Last king of Judah; blinded and taken captive to Babylon.
people.dateNotes: Ussher: reigned 599-588 BC (11 years, 2 Kgs 24:18). Age 21 at accession: born 620 BC. Blinded and taken to Babylon when Jerusalem fell in 588 BC; he died in prison there at an unrecorded date (Jer 52:11), so the death year is approximate. Modern scholarship: 597-587/586 BC.

events.role: King who yielded to the officials

people.name: Obadiah
people.description: Prophet who pronounced judgment on Edom for betraying Judah.
people.dateNotes: Usually dated soon after the fall of Jerusalem (Obad 11-14), 588 BC on Ussher's chain (587/586 in modern reckoning); some date the book to Edom's revolt under Jehoram of Judah (2 Kgs 8:20-22). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Shadrach
people.description: One of Daniel's three companions who survived the fiery furnace.
people.dateNotes: Dan 1:6-7; 3:1-30. Deported with Daniel in 607 BC on Ussher's reckoning (Annals §776). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Meshach
people.description: One of Daniel's three companions who survived the fiery furnace.
people.dateNotes: Dan 1:6-7; 3:1-30. Deported with Daniel in 607 BC on Ussher's reckoning (Annals §776). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Abednego
people.description: One of Daniel's three companions who survived the fiery furnace.
people.dateNotes: Dan 1:6-7; 3:1-30. Deported with Daniel in 607 BC on Ussher's reckoning (Annals §776). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Neri
people.description: Named in Luke 3:27 as the son of Melchi and father of Shealtiel, the point where Luke's line through Nathan touches the royal line of Matthew. Matthew 1:12 and 1 Chronicles 3:17 make Shealtiel a son of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah), so the lists disagree. Two classic explanations are offered. One treats it as a levirate or adoptive link, Shealtiel becoming heir to Neri's line when Jehoiachin was recorded as childless (Jer 22:30). The other holds that Luke traces Mary's ancestry, in which Neri is her forebear and the name Shealtiel belongs to a separate line or a shared name. This table keeps Matthew's father for Shealtiel and shows Neri as a parent relationship.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Luke's genealogy. Luke identifies Shealtiel as son of Neri rather than Jeconiah (Matt 1:12).

people.name: Jehoiachin
people.description: Son of Jehoiakim; king of Judah for 3 months. Deported to Babylon; later released by Evil-Merodach. In the lineage of Jesus.
people.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 24:8-16; 25:27-30; Jer 22:24-30; Matt 1:11-12. Ussher: reigned three months in 599 BC, then deported (Annals §794-796); released by Evil-merodach in the 37th year of his captivity (2 Kgs 25:27), 562 BC (§891). Age 18 at accession (2 Kgs 24:8): born 617 BC; 2 Chr 36:9 reads 8. The Babylonian Chronicle dates his surrender to March 597 BC. Ussher thinks he died about 560 BC, when Evil-merodach did (§899); the year is an estimate.

events.role: Exiled king whose captivity dates it

people.name: Darius the Mede
people.description: Ruler called Darius the Median who received the kingdom of Babylon at about 62 after Belshazzar's death (Dan 5:31). Pressed by his officials, he had Daniel thrown to the lions and then honored Daniel's God when he was delivered (Dan 6). He is not named outside Daniel and his identity is debated.
people.dateNotes: Dan 5:31; 6:1-28; 9:1; 11:1. Ussher, Annals §792, 939, 948: Cyaxares, son of Astyages (Ahasuerus of Dan 9:1), born 601 BC and 62 years old when he took the kingdom on Babylon's fall in 538 BC; he reigned two years, and Cyrus's first year followed in 537 BC. Death unrecorded. Mainstream: Babylon fell in 539 BC, and he is variously identified with Gubaru/Ugbaru, Cyaxares II or Cyrus himself; distinct from Darius I (522-486 BC).

people.name: Cyrus
people.description: Founder of the Persian Empire who took Babylon and permitted Judah's exiles to return and rebuild the temple. Isaiah strikingly names this Gentile king the Lord's anointed, and the Cyrus Cylinder documents his wider policy of restoring displaced peoples and their sanctuaries.
people.dateNotes: Isa 44:28; 45:1; 2 Chr 36:22-23; Ezra 1:1-4. Took Babylon in October 539 BC and died in 530 BC. Ussher dates his decree (Ezra 1:1) to 537 BC (Annals §948-949), counting his first year after Darius the Mede; modern scholarship gives 538 BC. Birth estimated.

events.role: King whose decree released the exiles

people.name: Shealtiel
people.description: Son of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) in Matthew 1:12 and 1 Chronicles 3:17, and father of Zerubbabel in Matthew, Luke and Ezra 3:2 (1 Chronicles 3:19 lists Pedaiah as Zerubbabel's father). Luke 3:27 calls him the son of Neri, so the genealogies differ here. Two classic explanations are offered. One holds that Shealtiel was Jehoiachin's son by birth and Neri's heir by levirate or adoptive succession, Jehoiachin being recorded as childless in Jer 22:30. The other holds that Luke follows Mary's line, in which Neri is her ancestor. This table follows Matthew for his father and shows Neri as a parent relationship. He lived in the exile in Babylon.
people.dateNotes: Exilic period. Born in Babylon after Jeconiah's deportation, 599 BC on Ussher's chain (597 BC by the Babylonian Chronicle; 1 Chr 3:17). Birth estimated.

people.name: Belshazzar
people.description: Last king of Babylon; saw the handwriting on the wall at his feast and was killed that night when Persia took the city (Dan 5:30). Ussher identifies him with the Nabonidus of Berosus, a grandson of Nebuchadnezzar through Evil-merodach (Jer 27:7), who reigned 17 years; mainstream scholarship makes him the son and co-regent of Nabonidus, with "father" in Daniel 5 meaning predecessor or ancestor.
people.dateNotes: Dan 5:30. Ussher, Annals §912, 915, 938: reigned 17 years from 555 BC; slain the night Babylon fell, 538 BC. Mainstream: killed 12 October 539 BC (Nabonidus Chronicle) as the son and coregent of Nabonidus. Birth estimated.

people.name: Jeshua the high priest
people.description: High priest of the first return from Babylon, son of Jozadak. With Zerubbabel he rebuilt the altar and laid the foundation of the Temple, and Zechariah saw him in a vision standing before the angel of the LORD.
people.dateNotes: Estimate: born in exile (his father Jozadak was carried away in 588 BC, 1 Chr 6:15) and high priest by the return of 536 BC (Ezra 3:2). Haggai and Zechariah address him in 520 BC. His death is not recorded.

scripture.context: Builds the altar and begins the Temple with Zerubbabel
Addressed by Haggai as high priest

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.description: Led the first return from exile; rebuilt the Temple.
people.dateNotes: Led the return under Cyrus, 536 BC on Ussher's chain (Ezra 2:2; 3:8), and saw the temple finished in the sixth year of Darius I, 515 BC (Ezra 6:15; Zech 4:9). Birth and death estimated.

events.role: Leader of the first return; governor of Judah
Rebuilt the altar and laid the temple foundation
Governor who obeyed and resumed the building

people.name: Haggai
people.description: Post-exilic prophet who urged rebuilding of the Temple.
people.dateNotes: Prophesied in the second year of Darius I, 520 BC (Hag 1:1; 2:1-20). His age is unknown: the Lives of the Prophets says he came from Babylon as a youth, while some read Hag 2:3 as implying he had seen Solomon's temple. Birth and death estimated.

events.role: Prophet whose word stirred the work

people.name: Darius I
people.description: Persian king who confirmed Cyrus's decree and had the records searched, so that work on the Second Temple resumed and was finished in his sixth year (Ezra 5-6). Haggai and Zechariah prophesied in his second year (Hag 1:1; Zech 1:1).
people.dateNotes: Reigned 522-486 BC, firmly dated by Persian and Babylonian records. Birth c. 550 BC (estimate). Not Darius the Mede (Dan 5:31).

events.role: King in whose second year the work resumed

people.name: Zechariah the prophet
people.description: Post-exilic prophet with messianic visions; contemporary of Haggai.
people.dateNotes: Prophesied 520-518 BC, in the second to fourth years of Darius I (Zech 1:1; 7:1). Grandson of Iddo (Zech 1:1), a priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh 12:4). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Mordecai
people.description: Esther's cousin who raised her; uncovered a plot against the king.
people.dateNotes: Esther 2-10. Cousin and guardian of Esther (Esth 2:7), promoted after Haman's fall in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus. Esth 2:6 (carried away with Jeconiah) is best read of his great-grandfather Kish, since Mordecai himself would otherwise be over 120. Birth and death estimated.

events.role: Cousin and guardian who counselled her

people.name: Vashti
people.description: Queen of Persia before Esther; deposed for refusing to appear before the king.
people.dateNotes: Esth 1:1-22. Deposed c. 483 BC. Talmud (Megillah 12b) identifies her as Nebuchadnezzar's granddaughter. Death unrecorded; est. c. 470 BC.

events.role: Queen who refused the king's summons

people.name: Xerxes
people.description: Persian king who married Esther; issued decree saving the Jews from Haman's plot.
people.dateNotes: Esth 1-10. Reigned 486-465 BC. Most scholars identify him with the Ahasuerus of Esther; some older chronologers, including Ussher, identified Ahasuerus with another Persian king. Birth estimated.

people.name: Haman
people.description: Persian official who plotted the genocide of the Jewish people; hanged on his own gallows.
people.dateNotes: Esth 3-7. Executed in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus (Esth 3:7; 7:10), 474/473 BC if he is Xerxes I. Birth estimated.

people.name: Abiud
people.description: Son of Zerubbabel, ancestor of Jesus in Matthew 1:13. Post-exilic figure.
people.dateNotes: Post-exilic period. Known only from Matthew's genealogy. Birth year is an inferred placeholder, evenly spaced between Zerubbabel and Joseph (Matt 1:13-16); Matthew's list probably omits generations, as it does in 1:8 and 1:11.

people.name: Ezra
people.description: A priest and scribe skilled in the law of Moses who led a company of exiles from Babylon back to Jerusalem under Persian sanction. By publicly reading and teaching the Torah, he re-centered the restored community on Scripture, a legacy foundational to Jewish identity ever after. Ezra 7:1-5 traces his line through Seraiah and Zadok back to Aaron the chief priest, in an abridged list.
people.dateNotes: Came to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes I (Ezra 7:7-8), 458 BC (457 on autumn-to-autumn reckoning), and read the law in Nehemiah's time (Neh 8; 444 BC). Called son of Seraiah (Ezra 7:1), the high priest killed in 588 BC, meaning descendant. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Esther
people.description: A Jewish orphan named Hadassah who became queen of Persia in the citadel of Susa and risked her life to expose Haman's plot to annihilate her people. Her courage is celebrated yearly at Purim; the Ahasuerus of her story is commonly identified with Xerxes I of Persian history. She was Mordecai's cousin, the daughter of his uncle Abihail (Esth 2:7, 15), and was raised by him after her parents died.
people.dateNotes: Became queen in the tenth month of the seventh year of Ahasuerus (Esth 2:16), 479/478 BC if he is Xerxes I; Haman's plot falls in his twelfth year (3:7), 474/473 BC. Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Sanballat
people.description: Governor of Samaria who opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
people.dateNotes: Neh 2:10, 19; 4:1-8; 6:1-14. Confirmed by Elephantine Papyri.

people.name: Tobiah
people.description: Ammonite official who opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding and conspired against him.

people.name: Rhesa
people.description: Son of Zerubbabel, ancestor of Jesus in Luke 3:27.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Luke's genealogy. Post-exilic period.

people.name: Malachi
people.description: Last of the twelve Minor Prophets, who called the restored community back to faithful worship and marriage and promised that Elijah would come before the day of the Lord (Mal 4:5).
people.dateNotes: Usually dated to the mid-5th century BC, c. 460-430, near the time of Ezra and Nehemiah (compare Mal 2:11 with Neh 13:23-29). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Artaxerxes I
people.description: Persian king, son of Xerxes, who sent Ezra to Jerusalem in his seventh year (Ezra 7) and Nehemiah, his cupbearer, in his twentieth (Neh 2:1-8). He also ordered a halt to the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls after complaints from its neighbours (Ezra 4:7-23).
people.dateNotes: Reigned 465-424 BC by Persian and Greek records. Birth estimated. Some scholars identify Ezra's king as Artaxerxes II (404-358 BC).

people.name: Nehemiah
people.description: Cupbearer to the Persian king Artaxerxes who returned as governor of Judah and rebuilt Jerusalem's shattered walls in fifty-two days despite fierce opposition. His memoirs join practical leadership to constant prayer, and with Ezra he anchored the restored community in covenant obedience. His brother Hanani brought him news of Jerusalem (Neh 1:2).
people.dateNotes: Came to Jerusalem in the 20th year of Artaxerxes I (Neh 2:1), 445/444 BC; returned to the king in his 32nd year, 433/432 BC, and later came back (Neh 13:6-7). Birth and death estimated.

people.name: Eliakim, son of Abiud
people.description: Son of Abiud, ancestor of Jesus in Matthew 1:13. Post-exilic figure.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Matthew's genealogy. Not the Eliakim of 2 Kings 18. Birth year is an inferred placeholder, evenly spaced between Zerubbabel and Joseph (Matt 1:13-16); Matthew's list probably omits generations, as it does in 1:8 and 1:11.

people.name: Azor
people.description: Son of Eliakim, ancestor of Jesus in Matthew 1:13–14.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Matthew's genealogy. Birth year is an inferred placeholder, evenly spaced between Zerubbabel and Joseph (Matt 1:13-16); Matthew's list probably omits generations, as it does in 1:8 and 1:11.

people.name: Philip II of Macedon
people.description: King of Macedon who made Macedon the leading power of Greece and was assassinated in 336 BC. Father of Alexander the Great. Not named in Scripture.
people.dateNotes: Standard historical record (not stated in Scripture). Born 382 BC, died 336 BC. Daniel 8:21 and 11:3 speak of the first king of Greece.

people.name: Olympias
people.description: Queen of Macedon, wife of Philip II and mother of Alexander the Great. Not named in Scripture.
people.dateNotes: Standard historical record (not stated in Scripture). Born about 375 BC and killed in 316 BC.

people.name: Alexander the Great
people.description: King of Macedon whose conquest of the Persian empire (334-323 BC) ended Persian rule over Judea and spread Greek language and culture across the east. Daniel's vision of the he-goat whose great horn is the first king of Grecia is traditionally read as pointing to him (Dan 8:5-8, 21; 11:3-4), and 1 Maccabees opens with his conquests (1 Macc 1:1-7).
people.dateNotes: Born July 356 BC, died June 323 BC at Babylon. Reading the Daniel passages as Alexander is the traditional interpretation; scholars differ on the dating of Daniel itself.

people.name: Zadok, son of Azor
people.description: Son of Azor, ancestor of Jesus in Matthew 1:14. Not the priest Zadok of David's time.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Matthew's genealogy. Not to be confused with Zadok the priest (2 Sam 8:17). Birth year is an inferred placeholder, evenly spaced between Zerubbabel and Joseph (Matt 1:13-16); Matthew's list probably omits generations, as it does in 1:8 and 1:11.

people.name: Achim
people.description: Son of Zadok, ancestor of Jesus in Matthew 1:14.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Matthew's genealogy. Intertestamental period. Birth year is an inferred placeholder, evenly spaced between Zerubbabel and Joseph (Matt 1:13-16); Matthew's list probably omits generations, as it does in 1:8 and 1:11.

people.name: Eliud
people.description: Son of Achim, ancestor of Jesus in Matthew 1:14–15.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Matthew's genealogy. Intertestamental period. Birth year is an inferred placeholder, evenly spaced between Zerubbabel and Joseph (Matt 1:13-16); Matthew's list probably omits generations, as it does in 1:8 and 1:11.

people.name: Antiochus IV Epiphanes
people.description: Seleucid king who plundered the temple in Jerusalem, banned Jewish practice, and set up the abomination of desolation on its altar in December 167 BC, provoking the Maccabean revolt (1 Macc 1:10-64; 2 Macc 5-6). Many readers link him to the little horn of Dan 8:9-12 and to Dan 11:21-35, while some traditions also read these passages of a later figure.
people.dateNotes: Reigned 175-164 BC and died late in 164 BC in Persia (1 Macc 6:1-16). Birth estimated.

events.role: Seleucid king who ordered the desecration

people.name: Judas Maccabeus
people.description: Third son of the priest Mattathias, who led the Jewish revolt after his father's death in 166 BC, defeated Seleucid armies, and rededicated the temple in December 165 BC (Ussher; standard dating 164 BC), the event commemorated at Hanukkah (1 Macc 3-4; 2 Macc 8-10; John 10:22). He fell in battle at Elasa in 161 BC (1 Macc 9:5-18; Ussher).
people.dateNotes: Died in year 152 of the Seleucid era (1 Macc 9:3): 161 BC on Ussher (Annals §3528-3532); standard dating 160 BC. Birth estimated. The books of Maccabees are canonical for Catholic and Orthodox Christians and counted among the Apocrypha by Protestants.

people.name: Eleazar, son of Eliud
people.description: Son of Eliud, ancestor of Jesus in Matthew 1:15. Not the priest Eleazar son of Aaron.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Matthew's genealogy. Not to be confused with Eleazar the priest (Num 20:28). Birth year is an inferred placeholder, evenly spaced between Zerubbabel and Joseph (Matt 1:13-16); Matthew's list probably omits generations, as it does in 1:8 and 1:11.

people.name: Matthan
people.description: Son of Eleazar, grandfather of Joseph of Nazareth in Matthew 1:15.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Matthew's genealogy (Matt 1:15). Birth year is an inferred placeholder spacing the ten generations from Zerubbabel to Joseph evenly; Matthew's list is probably selective.

people.name: Pompey
people.description: Roman general who took Jerusalem in 63 BC, ending Hasmonean independence and bringing Judea under Rome; he entered the Holy of Holies but left the Temple treasury untouched (Josephus, Antiquities 14.4). He was killed in Egypt after his defeat by Julius Caesar.
people.dateNotes: Born 106 BC; killed in Egypt in 48 BC. Not named in Scripture.

people.name: Simeon of Jerusalem
people.description: Devout man in Jerusalem who held the infant Jesus and prophesied. Promised he would see the Messiah.
people.dateNotes: Luke 2:25-35. Luke gives no age, only that he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ (Luke 2:26); birth and death years are estimates.

people.name: Anna
people.description: Elderly prophetess who recognized the infant Jesus at the Temple.
people.dateNotes: Luke 2:36-37: daughter of Phanuel of Asher, seven years married, then 'a widow of about fourscore and four years', which may mean aged 84 or widowed 84 years (about 105). Taking 84 as her age at the presentation (c. 5 BC) gives a birth c. 89 BC; the death year is an estimate.

people.name: Matthat, father of Heli
people.description: Son of Levi, ancestor of Jesus in Luke 3:24. Post-exilic Matthat, grandfather of Joseph.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Luke's genealogy. Late Second Temple period.

people.name: Jacob, son of Matthan
people.description: Son of Matthan, father of Joseph of Nazareth in Matthew 1:15–16. Not the patriarch Jacob.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Matthew's genealogy (Matt 1:15-16). Birth year is an inferred placeholder; Matthew's list is probably selective.

people.name: Herod the Great
people.description: King of Judea who rebuilt the Temple but ordered the massacre of infants in Bethlehem. Father of Archelaus, Herod Antipas and Philip the tetrarch, and grandfather of Herod Agrippa I through Aristobulus IV.
people.dateNotes: Matthew 2:1-19; confirmed by Josephus. Death in 4 BC is well-established.

events.role: Began the rebuilding of the temple

people.name: Caesar Augustus
people.description: First Roman emperor (27 BC-AD 14). Luke says his decree that all the world should be taxed brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem (Luke 2:1-5). Augustus adopted his stepson Tiberius in AD 4 and named him his successor.
people.dateNotes: Born 23 September 63 BC; died 19 August AD 14. Luke 2:1.

events.role: Octavian, who backed the Senate's decree
His census decree brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem (Luke 2:1)

people.name: Zechariah, father of John the Baptist
people.description: Priest who was struck mute for doubting Gabriel's announcement of John the Baptist's birth.
people.dateNotes: Luke 1:5-25, 57-80. Luke says only that he and Elizabeth were 'well stricken in years' (Luke 1:7); birth and death years are estimates. A second-century tradition (the Protoevangelium of James), not in Scripture, tells of his murder in the Temple; the Orthodox Church commemorates him as a martyr.

people.name: Heli
people.description: Named in Luke 3:23 as the father of Joseph, in the line running back through Matthat and Levi to Nathan, a son of David. Matthew 1:16 gives Joseph's father as Jacob instead, and the table keeps Matthew's link as Joseph's father_id and shows Heli's link as a separate parent relationship. Two classic explanations are offered. Africanus held that Heli and Jacob were half-brothers, Heli dying childless so that Jacob fathered Joseph by levirate marriage and Joseph counted as Heli's heir. Others hold that Luke gives Mary's ancestry, making Heli Mary's father and Joseph his son-in-law. Scripture does not say which is right.
people.dateNotes: Known only from Luke's genealogy. Some scholars identify Heli as Mary's father, making Luke's genealogy the natural/maternal line.

people.name: Elizabeth
people.description: Wife of Zechariah; mother of John the Baptist. Relative of Mary. Elizabeth was a daughter of Aaron (Luke 1:5) and Mary's "cousin" (Luke 1:36).
people.dateNotes: Luke 1:5-7, 39-45, 57-60. Birth and death years are estimates.

people.name: Tiberius Caesar
people.description: Second Roman emperor (AD 14-37). Luke dates the start of John the Baptist's preaching to his fifteenth year (Luke 3:1), and Jesus was crucified under his prefect Pontius Pilate. Born Tiberius Claudius Nero, he was the stepson of Augustus, who adopted him in AD 4.
people.dateNotes: Born 16 November 42 BC; emperor from 19 August AD 14; died 16 March AD 37. Luke 3:1.

events.role: Emperor in whose fifteenth year John began his ministry (Luke 3:1)

people.name: Aristobulus IV
people.description: Son of Herod the Great and the Hasmonean princess Mariamne, put to death by his father with his brother Alexander. He was the father of Herod Agrippa I and of Herodias, and so grandfather of Agrippa II, Bernice and Drusilla (Josephus). He is not named in Scripture; the link to Acts 12 is through his son.
people.dateNotes: Josephus (Ant. 16.394; Jewish War 1.551): executed at Sebaste, about 7 BC. Birth c. 35 BC is inferred from his mother's marriage to Herod in 37 BC. Not in Scripture.

people.name: Caiaphas
people.description: High priest who presided over Jesus' trial; declared it expedient for one man to die for the people. Annas was his father-in-law (John 18:13).
people.dateNotes: Matt 26:3, 57-68; John 11:49-53; 18:13-28. Ussher, Annals §6278: appointed high priest by Valerius Gratus in AD 26, after Annas's removal; deposed by Vitellius in AD 35 (§6543; Josephus Ant. 18.95 has 36/37). The death year marks the deposition; his death is unrecorded. An ossuary found in 1990 may be his (debated). Birth year is an estimate.

people.name: Joseph of Arimathea
people.description: Rich member of the Sanhedrin who provided his tomb for Jesus' burial.

people.name: Jonas, father of Peter
people.description: Father of Simon Peter. Jesus calls Peter "Simon Bar-jona" (Matt 16:17) and "son of Jona" (John 1:42); in John 21:15-17 the KJV reads "son of Jonas". Some manuscripts of John give the name as John. Peter's brother Andrew is presumed to share this father.
people.dateNotes: Estimate only, about a generation before Peter. Scripture gives no dates for him. Andrew is called Peter's brother (John 1:40) but only Peter is named as Jona's son in the text; Andrew's link rests on that.

scripture.context: Simon, son of Jona (KJV Jonas), lovest thou me?

people.name: Lois
people.description: Timothy's grandmother, in whom Paul says the faith first dwelt before it passed to Timothy's mother Eunice and to Timothy (2 Tim 1:5); Eunice is usually taken to be her daughter.
people.dateNotes: Estimate only. Scripture gives no dates.

people.name: Alphaeus, father of Levi
people.description: Named in Mark 2:14 as the father of Levi, the tax collector whom Jesus called, usually identified with the apostle Matthew (Matt 9:9). The Gospels do not say whether he is the Alphaeus who fathered James the Less (Matt 10:3); some later writers assume so, others do not.
people.dateNotes: Estimate only. Scripture gives no dates for him. Kept separate from the Alphaeus of Matt 10:3 because the text does not identify them.

scripture.context: Father of Levi the tax collector

people.name: Joseph of Nazareth
people.description: Husband of Mary and legal father of Jesus, a carpenter of Nazareth described as a righteous man (Matt 1:19). Matthew 1:16 calls him the son of Jacob, and this table follows Matthew for his father. Luke 3:23 calls him the son of Heli, so the two lists disagree. Two classic explanations are offered. Africanus (3rd century) held that Jacob and Heli were half-brothers by the same mother, and that when Heli died childless Jacob married the widow, so Joseph was Jacob's son by birth and Heli's by levirate law. Other writers, including many later Western and Eastern commentators, read Luke as tracing Mary's line, with Heli as her father and Joseph as his son-in-law. The tradition of the church does not require a choice between them.
people.dateNotes: Matthew 1-2; Luke 2. Disappears from narrative after Jesus' youth.

people.name: Annas
people.description: Former high priest and father-in-law of Caiaphas; influential in Jesus' trial.
people.dateNotes: Luke 3:2; John 18:13-24; Acts 4:6. High priest from AD 6 (Josephus Ant. 18.26, 18.34); removed by Gratus (Ussher, Annals §6268 places the removal in AD 23); five of his sons and his son-in-law Caiaphas held the office afterwards. Ussher still calls him high priest at the trial of Stephen (§6519, AD 33), as Acts 4:6 does. Birth and death years are estimates.

people.name: Zebedee
people.description: Galilean fisherman, father of the apostles James and John. His sons left him mending nets in the boat with his hired servants to follow Jesus.
people.dateNotes: Estimate only, about a generation before his sons. Scripture gives no dates for him, and he does not appear after the calling of his sons.

scripture.context: Mending nets with his sons when Jesus calls them

people.name: Alphaeus, father of James the apostle
people.description: Father of the apostle James son of Alphaeus (Matt 10:3), traditionally identified with James the Less (Mark 15:40). Mark 2:14 calls Levi (Matthew) "the son of Alpheus" too. Whether this is the same Alphaeus, which would make Matthew and James brothers, is not stated in the Gospels; the two are kept as separate rows here.
people.dateNotes: Estimate only. Scripture gives no dates for him.

people.name: Archelaus
people.description: Son of Herod the Great who ruled Judea, Samaria and Idumea as ethnarch after his father's death. When Joseph heard that Archelaus reigned in Judea in his father's place, he was afraid to go there and turned aside to Galilee (Matt 2:22). Augustus removed him in AD 6 after complaints from his subjects.
people.dateNotes: Josephus (Ant. 17.188; Jewish War 2.111): born c. 23 BC, ethnarch 4 BC to AD 6, banished beyond the Alps (Ussher, Annals §6174, AD 6). The year of his death is uncertain, so none is given.

scripture.context: Joseph fears Archelaus and goes to Galilee

people.name: Philip the Tetrarch
people.description: Son of Herod the Great, tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis (Luke 3:1). He rebuilt Caesarea Philippi and Bethsaida, and according to Josephus married Salome, the daughter of Herodias. He should not be confused with the Philip whom Mark 6:17 calls Herodias's first husband; Josephus names that man as another son of Herod the Great.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §6079, §6529: tetrarch from 4 BC (Herod's will); died AD 34 at Julias, in the twentieth year of Tiberius, after governing thirty-seven years (Josephus Ant. 18.106-108). Birth c. 22 BC is inferred from his father's marriage to Cleopatra of Jerusalem.

events.role: Tetrarch named in Luke 3:1 as ruling at the time

people.name: Mary, mother of Jesus
people.description: The young woman of Nazareth chosen to bear Jesus, whose obedient response to the angel's announcement made her the most honored woman in Scripture. Her Magnificat echoes Hannah's song, and she appears from Bethlehem to the cross and among the praying disciples before Pentecost. Luke calls Elisabeth her "cousin" (Luke 1:36), a relative of unspecified degree; the two are not sisters.
people.dateNotes: Birth and death years are estimates. Scripture last mentions her at Acts 1:14. Catholic and Orthodox Christians hold her Assumption or Dormition; Protestants generally hold that Scripture is silent on the end of her life. Tradition places her later life at Jerusalem or Ephesus.

people.name: Nicodemus
people.description: Pharisee who came to Jesus at night; helped bury Jesus.
people.dateNotes: John 3:1-21; 7:50-52; 19:39. Birth c. 20 BC and death c. AD 63 are estimates only: Scripture records neither and no early tradition dates his death.

people.name: Herod Antipas
people.description: Son of Herod the Great; executed John the Baptist and mocked Jesus during his trial.
people.dateNotes: Matt 14:1-12; Mark 6:14-29; Luke 3:1; 13:31-32; 23:6-12. Tetrarch of Galilee and Perea from 4 BC (Ussher, Annals §6079); banished in AD 39 (Ussher, Annals, under 39 AD, citing Josephus Ant. 18.240-255). His birth (c. 20 BC) is inferred and the year of his death is unknown.

events.role: Tetrarch who imprisoned and killed John

people.name: Zacchaeus
people.description: Chief tax collector in Jericho who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus; converted.

events.role: Chief tax collector who received Jesus

people.name: Jairus
people.description: Synagogue ruler whose 12-year-old daughter Jesus raised from the dead.
people.dateNotes: Mark 5:22-43; Luke 8:41-56. Synagogue ruler in Galilee. Daughter raised by Jesus c. AD 31. Birth and death years are estimates.

people.name: Mother of James and John
people.description: Wife of Zebedee and mother of the apostles James and John. She asked Jesus that her two sons might sit at his right and left in his kingdom (Matt 20:20-21) and stood among the women at the crucifixion (Matt 27:56). Scripture does not give her name. Mark 15:40 lists a Salome in the same group of women, and many readers identify the two; that is an inference, and some traditions identify her differently. She is not Salome the daughter of Herodias.
people.dateNotes: Estimate only, about a generation before her sons. The identification with Salome (Mark 15:40) is a common inference, not stated in Scripture; compare Matt 27:56 with Mark 15:40.

scripture.context: Asks Jesus for places for her sons
Among the women at the crucifixion
Salome, listed among the women, is commonly identified with her

people.name: Herodias
people.description: Wife of Herod Antipas; orchestrated John the Baptist's execution through her daughter. Her father was Aristobulus IV (Josephus), so she was the sister of Herod Agrippa I and Antipas's niece. Her first husband was another son of Herod the Great (Mark 6:17 calls him Philip; Josephus calls him Herod).

events.role: Wife of Antipas who demanded John's death

people.name: Martha
people.description: Sister of Lazarus and Mary; known for her hospitality and service.
people.dateNotes: Luke 10:38-42; John 11; 12:2. Birth and death years are estimates. Later tradition (Provence) is legendary; Scripture is silent.

people.name: Pontius Pilate
people.description: Roman governor of Judea who authorized the crucifixion of Jesus.
people.dateNotes: Prefect of Judea from AD 26 (Ussher, Annals §6279; Luke 3:1); ordered to Rome by Vitellius in AD 36 (§6564); Ussher, citing Eusebius and Jerome, has him take his own life under Caligula in AD 39 (§6609), a late tradition. Birth year is conjecture.

people.name: Simon of Cyrene
people.description: Man from Cyrene compelled to carry Jesus' cross.
people.dateNotes: Matt 27:32; Mark 15:21; Luke 23:26.

people.name: Mary of Bethany
people.description: Sister of Martha and Lazarus; sat at Jesus' feet; anointed him with expensive perfume.
people.dateNotes: Luke 10:38-42; John 11:1-2; 12:1-8. Birth and death years are estimates. She is distinct from Mary Magdalene; the Western identification of the two (and of the sinful woman of Luke 7) goes back to Gregory the Great (AD 591), was never held in the East, and was dropped from the Roman calendar in 1969.

people.name: Gamaliel
people.description: Respected Pharisee and teacher of Paul; counseled moderation toward the apostles.
people.dateNotes: Acts 5:34-39; 22:3. His counsel falls in AD 33 (Ussher, Annals §6516). Birth and death years are estimates; Scripture gives neither.

events.role: Pharisee and teacher of the law who counselled restraint

people.name: Herod Agrippa I
people.description: Grandson of Herod the Great; executed James son of Zebedee and imprisoned Peter. Struck dead by God. Son of Aristobulus IV, a son of Herod the Great, so grandson of Herod the Great; father of Agrippa II, Bernice and Drusilla, and brother of Herodias (Josephus).
people.dateNotes: Acts 12:1-23. Josephus says he died in AD 44 aged 54 (Ant. 19.343-352), so born c. 11/10 BC.

people.name: Claudius
people.description: Fourth Roman emperor (AD 41-54). Acts dates the famine foretold by Agabus to his reign (Acts 11:28) and says his expulsion of the Jews from Rome brought Aquila and Priscilla to Corinth (Acts 18:2).
people.dateNotes: Born 1 August 10 BC; died 13 October AD 54. The expulsion of the Jews: Ussher (Annals 6792) places it just before Paul reached Corinth, AD 54; Orosius gives AD 49, the usual modern date (compare Suetonius, Claudius 25).

events.role: Emperor in whose reign the famine came

scripture.context: Famine in the days of Claudius

people.name: Jesus
people.description: The central figure of the Christian faith, proclaimed as Messiah and Son of God, whose teaching, crucifixion under Pontius Pilate, and resurrection stand at the heart of the gospel. The Pilate stone from Caesarea and the Caiaphas ossuary attest the very officials named at his trial.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §6057: born 5 BC (before Herod's death, Matt 2:1, 19); crucified Friday 3 April AD 33 (§6474-6477). Baptised about thirty (Luke 3:23) in AD 27 (§6288). Many modern scholars place the birth 6-4 BC; AD 30 is the main alternative for the crucifixion.

events.role: Heard of John's death and withdrew
Called Zacchaeus down and stayed at his house

people.name: John the Baptist
people.description: A wilderness prophet who called Israel to repentance and baptism in the Jordan and pointed to Jesus as the coming one. Executed by Herod Antipas, he is also attested by Josephus, who reports that many Jews saw Antipas's later military defeat as divine judgment for the killing.
people.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §6043: born 5 BC, about six months before Jesus (Luke 1:26, 36). His ministry began in the fifteenth year of Tiberius (Luke 3:1; §6282-6283); imprisoned AD 30 after the first Passover (John 3:24; Mark 1:14; §6311) and beheaded AD 32 shortly before the feeding of the 5,000 (Matt 14:12-13; §6362). Josephus (Ant. 18.116-119) names Machaerus.

people.name: Lazarus
people.description: Brother of Mary and Martha; raised from the dead by Jesus after four days.
people.dateNotes: John 11:1-44; 12:1-11. Birth and death years are estimates. Later traditions of his life (bishop of Kition on Cyprus, or Marseille) are legendary; Scripture is silent.

people.name: Mary Magdalene
people.description: Follower of Jesus; first witness of the resurrection.
people.dateNotes: Luke 8:2; Mark 15:40; 16:9; John 20:1-18. Birth and death years are estimates. She is not the sister of Lazarus (that is Mary of Bethany), and the Gospels do not identify her with the sinful woman of Luke 7; that identification is a later Western tradition (Gregory the Great, AD 591). Traditions of her later life (Ephesus; Provence) are late.

people.name: Barabbas
people.description: Criminal released by Pilate instead of Jesus at the crowd's demand.
people.dateNotes: Matt 27:15-26. Released instead of Jesus in AD 33 (AD 30 on the alternative). No further record; birth and death years are estimates.

people.name: Cleopas
people.description: Disciple who encountered the risen Jesus on the road to Emmaus.

people.name: Cornelius
people.description: Roman centurion in Caesarea; first Gentile convert. His household received the Holy Spirit.

people.name: Ethiopian Eunuch
people.description: Official of the Ethiopian queen Candace; baptized by Philip after reading Isaiah.

people.name: Ananias and Sapphira
people.description: Husband and wife who lied to the Holy Spirit about the price of their property; both struck dead.
people.dateNotes: Acts 5:1-11. Ussher, Annals §6514: AD 33, soon after Pentecost. Was 34. Birth year is an estimate. Death: Ussher, Annals 6514: AD 33, soon after Pentecost (Acts 5:1-11); earlier row had AD 34.

people.name: Eunice
people.description: Jewish believer of Lystra and mother of Timothy. Paul praises the "unfeigned faith" that dwelt first in Timothy's grandmother Lois and then in Eunice (2 Tim 1:5). Timothy's father was a Greek whom Scripture does not name (Acts 16:1).
people.dateNotes: Estimate only, about a generation before Timothy (born c. AD 17). Scripture gives no dates. 2 Tim 1:5 names Lois as Timothy's grandmother and Eunice as his mother; that Lois was Eunice's mother, not Timothy's paternal grandmother, is the natural reading but is not stated.

scripture.context: A Jewess who believed; her husband a Greek

people.name: Mary, mother of John Mark
people.description: Jerusalem believer in whose house many were praying when Peter came knocking after his release from prison (Acts 12:12). Her son was John, surnamed Mark. Colossians 4:10 calls Mark "sister's son to Barnabas" (KJV; the Greek anepsios is often rendered "cousin"), which makes her Barnabas's sister (or, if the word means cousin, his relative).
people.dateNotes: Estimate only, about a generation before Mark (born c. AD 15). The event is dated to AD 44 (Acts 12). Her husband is not named.

scripture.context: Peter comes to her house after his release
Mother of Mark, whom Barnabas is related to

people.name: Peter
people.description: A Galilean fisherman whom Jesus called to lead the apostles, remembered for his bold confession, his denial, and his restoration. He preached at Pentecost, opened the door to Gentile believers at Cornelius's house, and by early tradition was martyred in Rome under Nero. His wife is not named: the Gospels mention his mother-in-law (Mark 1:30) and Paul says Cephas took a wife with him on his travels (1 Cor 9:5).
people.dateNotes: Scripture does not record his death; Jesus foretells it (John 21:18-19). Ussher, Annals 6949, following early church tradition (Eusebius), dates the martyrdom of Peter and Paul at Rome to 29 June AD 67. Many modern scholars prefer about AD 64-68, under Nero.

events.role: Apostle who answered for the others

people.name: James, brother of Jesus
people.description: The Lord's brother who came to faith after the resurrection and became the acknowledged leader of the Jerusalem church, remembered as James the Just. Paul names him a pillar, the historian Josephus records his execution, and the practical wisdom of his letter still guides believers.
people.dateNotes: Acts 15:13-21; Gal 1:19; 2:9; James 1:1. Josephus (Ant. 20.200) records his stoning (Ussher: AD 63; commonly AD 62), between the death of Festus and the arrival of Albinus; Hegesippus (in Eusebius) gives a fuller account. Birth year is an estimate that assumes the brothers were younger sons of Mary and Joseph (the common Protestant view). The Orthodox tradition holds they were sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage (older than Jesus); the Catholic tradition, following Jerome, holds they were cousins. Death: Ussher, Annals 6885-6887: AD 63, after the death of Festus (Josephus Ant. 20.200); many modern scholars give AD 62.

people.name: Stephen
people.description: First Christian martyr.
people.dateNotes: Born c. AD 1 (estimated). A Hellenistic Jewish believer, mature enough to be chosen as one of the Seven (Acts 6:5). Stoned: Ussher, Annals §6519-6521, AD 33 (was c. AD 35; Paul's conversion follows in AD 35, §6533). Death: Ussher, Annals 6518-6521: stoned late AD 33 (Acts 7:58-60); earlier row had AD 35.

people.name: Joses, brother of Jesus
people.description: Brother of Jesus mentioned in Mark 6:3 and Matthew 13:55.
people.dateNotes: Mark 6:3; Matthew 13:55. Birth year is an estimate that assumes the brothers were younger sons of Mary and Joseph (the common Protestant view). The Orthodox tradition holds they were sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage (older than Jesus); the Catholic tradition, following Jerome, holds they were cousins.

scripture.context: Named among the brothers of Jesus

people.name: Matthew
people.description: Tax collector called by Jesus (Matt 9:9), one of the Twelve; traditionally the author of the first Gospel. Mark 2:14 calls him Levi the son of Alpheus; whether this is the father of James son of Alphaeus is not stated.
people.dateNotes: Matt 9:9; 10:3; called Levi son of Alphaeus in Mark 2:14 and Levi in Luke 5:27. Birth and death years are estimates; Scripture does not record his death and later traditions of it disagree.

people.name: Simon, brother of Jesus
people.description: Brother of Jesus mentioned in Mark 6:3 and Matthew 13:55. Not to be confused with Simon Peter or Simon the Zealot.
people.dateNotes: Mark 6:3; Matthew 13:55. Birth year is an estimate that assumes the brothers were younger sons of Mary and Joseph (the common Protestant view). The Orthodox tradition holds they were sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage (older than Jesus); the Catholic tradition, following Jerome, holds they were cousins.

scripture.context: Named among the brothers of Jesus

people.name: James, son of Zebedee
people.description: Son of Zebedee and brother of John, one of the inner three with Peter and John. Herod Agrippa I had him killed with the sword (Acts 12:2), the only one of the Twelve whose martyrdom Scripture records. Matthew 27:56 mentions "the mother of Zebedee's children" at the cross; Mark 15:40 names Salome in the same group, and she is commonly identified with her (an inference).
people.dateNotes: Killed shortly before Peter's arrest at Passover (Acts 12:1-3); Agrippa died soon after in AD 44 (Acts 12:23; Josephus Ant. 19.343-352), so AD 44. Birth year is an estimate. The tradition of his preaching in Spain and burial at Santiago de Compostela is medieval.

people.name: Judas Iscariot
people.description: Apostle who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
people.dateNotes: Matthew 26:14-16, 47-50; 27:3-10; Acts 1:16-20. Death in the passion week: Ussher, Annals §6473 (AD 33). Birth is an estimate.

people.name: Jude, brother of Jesus
people.description: Brother of Jesus mentioned in Mark 6:3 and Matthew 13:55. Traditionally identified as the author of the Epistle of Jude.
people.dateNotes: Mark 6:3 (Juda); Matthew 13:55 (Judas); Jude 1:1 ('brother of James'). Birth year is an estimate that assumes the brothers were younger sons of Mary and Joseph (the common Protestant view). The Orthodox tradition holds they were sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage (older than Jesus); the Catholic tradition, following Jerome, holds they were cousins.

scripture.context: Named among the brothers of Jesus

people.name: Paul
people.description: A Pharisee who persecuted the church until an encounter with the risen Jesus made him the apostle to the Gentiles. His missionary journeys and letters shaped Christian theology more than any other early figure, and the Gallio inscription at Delphi helps anchor his career in history.
people.dateNotes: Scripture does not record his death; he expects it in 2 Tim 4:6-8. Ussher, Annals 6949, following early church tradition (Eusebius), dates the martyrdom of Peter and Paul at Rome to 29 June AD 67.
