people.description: Roman monk sent by Pope Gregory the Great in 597 to bring Christianity to the Anglo-Saxons of Kent. He became the first Archbishop of Canterbury. He is not the same person as Augustine of Hippo.
people.dateNotes: Birth year unknown. Died 26 May in 604 or 605; 604 is the usual date.

people.name: Sheshbazzar
people.description: "Prince of Judah" to whom Cyrus entrusted the Temple vessels, and the first governor of the return, who laid the foundation of the house of God. Some identify him with Zerubbabel, others with Shenazar, an uncle of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:18); the text does not say.
people.dateNotes: Scripture gives no dates. He led the return of 536 BC (Ezra 1:8-11; 5:14-16).

events.role: Prince of Judah who brought back the vessels (Ezra 1:8-11)

scripture.context: Receives the Temple vessels from Cyrus
Governor; lays the foundation of the house of God

people.name: Shishak
people.description: King of Egypt who gave refuge to Jeroboam when Solomon sought his life (1 Kgs 11:40) and in the fifth year of Rehoboam came up against Jerusalem with 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen, taking the treasures of the temple and the palace (1 Kgs 14:25-26; 2 Chr 12:2-9).
people.dateNotes: Birth and death not recorded. Scripture: invaded in Rehoboam's 5th year (1 Kgs 14:25), 971 BC on Ussher's chain. Ussher, Annals Sec. 474, 485: began to reign 978 BC. Mainstream: Pharaoh Shoshenq I, Karnak list, campaign c. 925 BC.

events.role: Pharaoh who invaded Judah and carried off the temple treasures

people.name: Ben-hadad, son of Tabrimon
people.description: King of Syria at Damascus, son of Tabrimon, son of Hezion. Asa of Judah sent him the temple and palace silver to break his league with Baasha; he struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maachah and all Naphtali, and Baasha stopped building Ramah (1 Kgs 15:16-22; 2 Chr 16:1-6).
people.dateNotes: Birth and death not recorded. Ussher, Annals Sec. 496-497: the league with Asa falls in 940 BC (Asa's 16th year; the '36th year' of 2 Chr 16:1 is counted from the division of the kingdom). Ussher leaves open whether this is the same king as Ahab's Ben-hadad; the dataset keeps two rows.

people.name: Ben-hadad, king of Aram in Ahab's day
people.description: King of Aram who besieged Samaria with thirty-two kings and was beaten twice by Ahab, who then let him go under a covenant (1 Kgs 20). Later, sick, he sent Hazael to ask Elisha whether he would recover; Hazael smothered him and reigned in his place (2 Kgs 8:7-15).
people.dateNotes: Birth not recorded. Ussher, Annals Sec. 512-513: wars with Ahab from 900 BC. Death c. 885 BC is an estimate: Hazael is already king at Ramoth-gilead in 884 (Sec. 533).

events.role: King of Aram smothered by Hazael

people.name: Mesha, king of Moab
people.description: King of Moab, a sheep-breeder who paid Israel a tribute of 100,000 lambs and the wool of 100,000 rams until Ahab died, then rebelled. Jehoram of Israel, Jehoshaphat and Edom invaded; besieged in Kir-hareseth, Mesha took his eldest son, who should have reigned after him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall (2 Kgs 3:4-27).
people.dateNotes: Birth and death not recorded. Ussher, Annals Sec. 524: the campaign falls in 895 BC, Jehoram of Israel's 2nd year. Ussher (Sec. 524) reads the victim as the son of the king of Edom; Scripture says his own eldest son (2 Kgs 3:27), which is followed here. The Moabite Stone (Mesha Stele) names Omri and Mesha; mainstream dates c. 850 BC.

events.role: King of Moab who rebelled against Israel

people.name: Zerah the Ethiopian
people.description: Commander or king of a vast Cushite army, a million men and three hundred chariots, who came against Judah at Mareshah and was routed by Asa after he cried to the Lord (2 Chr 14:9-15).
people.dateNotes: Birth and death not recorded. Scripture places the invasion after ten years of quiet in Asa's reign (2 Chr 14:1) and before the covenant of Asa's 15th year, 941 BC (15:10-11). Ussher (Annals Sec. 494) sets it in the early part of that span; the year is not fixed.

events.role: Cushite invader whose defeat preceded the reform

people.name: Shalmaneser
people.description: King of Assyria who came up against Hoshea, made him a tributary, and shut him up in prison when he sent to So of Egypt. He besieged Samaria three years and took it in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth of Hoshea (2 Kgs 17:3-6; 18:9-10).
people.dateNotes: Modern history: reigned 727-722 BC. Scripture names him as the king who came up against Hoshea and besieged Samaria (2 Kgs 17:3-6; 18:9-10). Ussher (Annals 640) has him die in 717 BC and makes him the father of Sennacherib; on the modern account Sennacherib's father is Sargon II.

events.role: Assyrian king who besieged and took Samaria

scripture.context: Comes up against Hoshea and besieges Samaria

events.name: Creation
events.description: In the Bible's opening scene, God speaks an ordered cosmos into being, crowning it with humanity made in the divine image and a day of rest. Unlike Babylon's Enuma Elish, where creation follows divine combat, Genesis presents one sovereign God whose word alone brings light, life, and order.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals sec. 1: 4004 BC (AM 1), beginning at the evening before 23 October. Mainstream scholarship does not derive the age of the world from the Genesis genealogies, which may omit generations; Ussher's figure is one traditional reading.

events.name: The Fall
events.description: In Eden, Adam and Eve eat from the forbidden tree at the serpent's urging, breaking trust with their Creator. Their exile from the garden brings sin, death, and alienation into the human story, setting the stage for the long biblical drama of redemption that Scripture traces to Christ.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals secs. 10-11: 4004 BC, probably on the 10th day of the world (1 November).

events.name: Cain Kills Abel
events.description: Cain, angered that God accepted Abel's offering and not his own, kills his brother in the field. It is the first death recorded in Scripture, and God sends Cain away as a restless wanderer, yet under a protective mark.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Abel was killed before Seth was born when Adam was 130 (Gen 4:25; 5:3), so no later than 3874 BC. Ussher, Annals sec. 13 (130 AM, 3874 BC): Seth was given after the murder, with man about 128 years on the earth. Exact year not fixed; 3880 BC is a display estimate.

events.name: Enoch Taken by God
events.description: Enoch walks with God for 300 years after the birth of Methuselah and then is not, for God takes him in the 365th year of his life. Hebrews says he was taken up without seeing death.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: AM 987 from Gen 5:21-24 (born 3382 BC, aged 365). Matches the year given in Enoch's row.

events.name: The Flood
events.description: Grieved by human violence, God cleanses the earth with a flood while preserving Noah, his family, and the animals in the ark, then seals a covenant with the rainbow sign. Mesopotamian epics like Gilgamesh and Atrahasis preserve parallel flood tales, yet Genesis uniquely grounds the deluge in divine justice.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: began 2349 BC (AM 1656), ended 2348 BC. Gen 8:13-14 puts the drying of the earth in Noah's 601st year. Mainstream scholarship does not date the Flood from the Genesis genealogies.

people.role: Son of Noah; entered the ark (Gen 7:13)
Son of Noah; entered the ark (Gen 7:13)
Son of Noah; entered the ark (Gen 7:13)

events.name: Tower of Babel
events.description: United humanity builds a tower on the plain of Shinar to make a name for itself, and God scatters the builders by confusing their language. The story evokes Mesopotamian ziggurats such as Babylon's Etemenanki and explains the dispersion of nations, which Genesis places generations before God's call of Abraham.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 2247 BC (AM 1757), when Peleg was born and the earth was divided (Gen 10:25), about 326 years before Abraham left Haran in 1921 BC.

events.name: Call of Abraham
events.description: God summons Abram to leave his homeland and his father's house, going by way of Haran, for a country God would show him, promising to make him a great nation and a blessing to all peoples of the earth. His obedient departure launches the covenant story that the rest of Scripture traces through Israel to the Messiah.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals secs. 71-72: 1921 BC (AM 2083), when Abraham left Haran aged 75 (Gen 12:4) after Terah's death at 205 (Acts 7:4). Acts 7:2-4 and Gen 15:7 indicate that God first called him in Ur, which Ussher places in 1922 BC (sec. 70).

events.name: Abrahamic Covenant
events.description: In a solemn night ceremony, God passes between divided animal carcasses as a smoking firepot and blazing torch, swearing to give Abram countless descendants and the land of Canaan. The rite mirrors ancient Near Eastern treaty customs, yet here God alone walks the path, bearing the covenant obligation himself.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals sec. 77: 1912 BC (AM 2092), after Abram's defeat of Chedorlaomer and the blessing by Melchizedek (sec. 76; Gen 14), when God renewed the promise and made the covenant of Gen 15.

events.name: Birth of Ishmael
events.description: After ten years in Canaan Sarai gives her servant Hagar to Abram, and Hagar bears Ishmael when Abram is 86. God hears the boy's cry and promises to make him a great nation, though the covenant line runs through Isaac.
events.dateNotes: Gen 16:3, 16: Abram aged 86 (Ussher 1910 BC).

events.name: Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
events.description: Fire and sulfur destroy Sodom and Gomorrah after the outcry against their wickedness reaches heaven, though angels lead Lot's family out; his wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. The doomed cities of the Dead Sea plain become Scripture's enduring emblem of judgment, invoked by prophets and by Jesus.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: c. 1897 BC (Gen 19). Abraham was 99 years old.

people.role: Rescued from the city by the angels (Gen 19)

events.name: Covenant of Circumcision
events.description: God gives Abraham circumcision as the enduring sign of the covenant, marking every male of his household and renaming Abram and Sarai as heirs of the promise of nations and kings. Though circumcision was practiced in Egypt and elsewhere, Israel uniquely made it a covenant emblem binding each generation to God.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: c. 1897 BC. Abraham aged 99 (Gen 17:1, 24).

people.role: Received the covenant sign and circumcised his household (Gen 17)
Promised a son within the covenant (Gen 17:15-16)

events.name: Birth of Isaac
events.description: Isaac is born to Abraham at 100 and Sarah at 90, the child of promise whose name means laughter. He is circumcised on the eighth day, and the covenant line runs through him.
events.dateNotes: Gen 21:5; 17:17: Abraham aged 100 (Ussher 1896 BC).

events.name: Binding of Isaac
events.description: God tests Abraham by commanding the sacrifice of Isaac, the son of promise, on Mount Moriah; at the final moment an angel stays the knife and a ram is offered instead. Known in Jewish tradition as the Akedah, the event affirms that God himself provides the sacrifice, a theme Christians hear echoed at Calvary.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals sec. 90: 1871 BC (AM 2133). Scripture gives no age for Isaac (Gen 22:5 calls him a lad); Ussher's dates make him 25, and Josephus (Antiquities 1) says 25 (Annals sec. 91).

events.name: Death of Sarah and Purchase of Machpelah
events.description: Sarah dies at 127 in Hebron, and Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite for 400 shekels of silver. It is his only possession in the promised land, and later holds Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah and Jacob.
events.dateNotes: Gen 23:1-20: Sarah aged 127 (born 1986 BC).

events.name: Isaac Marries Rebekah
events.description: Abraham's servant travels to Mesopotamia and brings back Rebekah, who marries Isaac when he is 40, three years after Sarah's death. Isaac is comforted after his mother's death.
events.dateNotes: Gen 24; 25:20: Isaac aged 40 (born 1896 BC).

events.name: Jacob Flees to Haran
events.description: Having gained Isaac's blessing and the birthright, Jacob flees Esau's anger toward Haran, and at Bethel dreams of a ladder to heaven where God confirms the Abrahamic promise to him.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals sections 111-112: 1760 BC (AM 2245). Jacob was 77 when he left (Gen 27-28), because he was 91 at Joseph's birth (Gen 41:46; 45:6; 47:9) at the end of 14 years of service (Gen 30:25; 31:41).

events.name: Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel
events.description: Jacob serves Laban seven years for Rachel but is given Leah; he receives Rachel a week later and serves seven more. Eleven of the twelve tribal ancestors and Dinah are born over the following years.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Jacob served seven years for Rachel before the marriage (Gen 29:18-21), then received Leah and, a week later, Rachel (29:22-28); he arrived in Haran in 1760 BC (Ussher, Annals 111), so the marriages fall in 1753 BC, and Joseph is born at the end of the second seven years, 1745 BC (30:25; 31:41). Ussher (Annals 114-115, following Tremellius) instead puts both marriages in 1760 BC with the service afterwards; the text is followed here.

events.name: Jacob Wrestles God
events.description: Jacob wrestles with God and is renamed Israel.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: c. 1739 BC (Gen 32:22-32).

events.name: Joseph Sold into Slavery
events.description: Joseph's brothers sell him to traders going to Egypt.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Joseph was 17 when sold (Gen 37:2) and 30 when he stood before Pharaoh (Gen 41:46), so 13 years before 1715 BC = 1728 BC. Ussher, Annals section 128, agrees.

events.name: Joseph Made Ruler of Egypt
events.description: Sold by his brothers yet raised from prison to Pharaoh's right hand, Joseph interprets dreams of coming famine and administers Egypt's grain stores. His rise turns betrayal into rescue, positioning him to preserve Jacob's family, the fledgling covenant line, through seven years of scarcity.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Joseph was 30 when he stood before Pharaoh (Gen 41:46), nine years before Jacob stood before Pharaoh at 130 in 1706 BC (two years of famine after seven of plenty, Gen 45:6; 47:9), so 1715 BC. Ussher, Annals section 131, agrees.

people.role: Given to Joseph as wife by Pharaoh (Gen 41:45)

events.name: Seven Years of Famine Begin
events.description: After seven years of plenty, famine spreads across Egypt and the nearby lands, and Joseph opens the storehouses. Jacob's sons come twice to buy grain; on the second journey, when two years of the famine have passed and five remain, Joseph reveals himself to them (Gen 45:6).
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Joseph was 30 when he stood before Pharaoh (Gen 41:46) and seven plenteous years follow (Gen 41:47-53), so the famine begins 1715 - 7 = 1708 BC (Ussher, Annals section 133: from the harvest of that year). At the reunion two years of famine had passed and five were to come (Gen 45:6), i.e. 1706 BC, the beginning of the third year (Ussher, sections 137-138); the first journey, when Simeon was held, is 1707 BC (section 134). Jacob enters Egypt 1706 BC.

events.name: Judah and Tamar
events.description: Judah fails to give his widowed daughter-in-law Tamar to his youngest son, and Tamar secures her rights by a bold ruse; Judah himself concedes, "She hath been more righteous than I." Her twin sons Perez and Zerah are born, and Perez stands in the line of David and of Jesus (Matt 1:3).
events.dateNotes: Ussher does not date Genesis 38 in the Annals. It must fall between Judah's birth in 1755 BC (section 120) and the descent into Egypt in 1706 BC (section 138), but it does not fit neatly into the lives of Judah's sons, so the year is only anchored on Perez's birth in this table. Estimate.

events.name: Israel Enters Egypt
events.description: Jacob and his whole household migrate to Egypt at Joseph's invitation, settling in the fertile land of Goshen and growing there into a numerous people. Egyptian art such as the Beni Hasan tomb painting depicts Semitic families entering Egypt, illustrating this well-traveled path in times of famine.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Jacob was 130 when he stood before Pharaoh (Gen 47:9), two years into the famine (Gen 45:6). Jacob's birth in 1836 BC is Ussher's, so 1836 - 130 = 1706 BC (Ussher, Annals section 138, AM 2298). Gen 41:46 and 45:6 give the same result from Joseph's age: 91 + 30 + 9 = 130. The 215 years from here to the Exodus are the second half of the 430 of Exod 12:40 counted from Abraham's call in 1921 BC (Gal 3:17); Ussher, Annals section 138.

people.role: Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:23)
Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:24)
Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:16)
Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:17)
Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:13)
Son of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:14)
Grandson of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:11)
Joseph's son, born in Egypt and counted among Jacob's house (Gen 46:20,27)
Joseph's son, born in Egypt and counted among Jacob's house (Gen 46:20,27)
Grandson of Jacob who came into Egypt (Gen 46:12)

events.name: Joseph Reveals Himself to His Brothers
events.description: After two years of famine, with five still to come, Joseph can hold back no longer and tells his brothers who he is. He assures them that God sent him ahead to preserve life, and sends for his father Jacob to come to Egypt.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Gen 45:6, two years of famine behind and five ahead; the famine began 1708 BC (Joseph ruler at 30 in 1715 + seven plenteous years, Gen 41:46-53), so 1706 BC. Ussher, Annals section 137 agrees: 1706 BC, the same year Jacob's household went down (section 138, the beginning of the third year of the famine). The first journey, when Simeon was held, is 1707 BC (section 134).

people.role: brother who had pleaded for Benjamin (Gen 44)

events.name: Jacob Blesses His Sons and Dies
events.description: Gathered at his bedside in Egypt, Jacob adopts Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh and pronounces a blessing over each of his twelve sons, including the promise that the sceptre will not depart from Judah. He charges them to bury him at Machpelah and dies; Joseph and his brothers carry him to Canaan.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Jacob lived 17 years in Egypt and was 147 at his death (Gen 47:28), so 1706 - 17 = 1689 BC. Ussher, Annals section 145, agrees (1689 BC, AM 2315).

people.role: son, who brings Ephraim and Manasseh

events.name: Birth of Moses
events.description: In the days when Pharaoh ordered every newborn Hebrew boy thrown into the Nile, a Levite woman hides her son for three months and then sets him afloat in a basket of reeds. Pharaoh's daughter finds him and raises him as her own, with his own mother as nurse.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Moses was 80 when he spoke to Pharaoh (Exod 7:7), the year of the Exodus (1491 BC), so 1571 BC; he died at 120 (Deut 34:7) in 1451 BC. Ussher, Annals section 162, agrees. The Exodus year itself is Ussher's, from the 430 years of Exod 12:40-41 and Gal 3:17 counted from Abraham's call in 1921 BC. Most modern scholars place Moses a century or more later.

people.role: sister, who watched over the basket

events.name: The Exodus
events.description: After ten plagues break Pharaoh's resistance, Israel departs Egypt under Moses on Passover night, freed from slavery to become a covenant nation. The Merneptah Stele, an Egyptian victory monument, preserves the earliest known extrabiblical mention of Israel as a people.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: 430 years from the promise to Abraham (Exod 12:40-41; Gal 3:17) and the 480th year before the founding of the Temple in Solomon's fourth year (1 Kgs 6:1), which Ussher fixes at 1012 BC; 1012 plus 479 years (the 480th year) gives 1491 BC. Ussher, Annals 172-190: AM 2513, 1491 BC, on the fifteenth day of the first month (Num 33:3). Many scholars favour an early date c. 1446 BC (also from 1 Kgs 6:1, counting 480 years to a Temple dated c. 966 BC); others a late date c. 1260-1250 BC.

events.name: Crossing the Red Sea
events.description: Trapped between Pharaoh's chariots and the sea, Israel watches God part the waters at Moses' outstretched hand, crossing on dry ground while the pursuing army is drowned. The Song of the Sea celebrating this rescue is reckoned among the oldest poetry preserved in the Hebrew Bible.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1491 BC.

people.role: Led the women in song after the crossing (Ex 15:20-21)

events.name: Giving of the Law
events.description: Amid thunder and fire on Mount Sinai, God speaks the Ten Commandments and gives Moses the Torah, constituting rescued slaves as a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. Scholars note that the covenant's structure parallels ancient suzerainty treaties, casting God as Israel's sovereign King.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1491 BC (AM 2513), third month after Exodus.

events.name: Wilderness Wandering
events.description: After refusing to enter Canaan at the spies' fearful report, Israel wanders the wilderness for forty years until the unbelieving generation passes away. Sustained by manna, water from the rock, and the guiding cloud, the nation is disciplined and shaped for covenant life in the promised land.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1491-1451 BC.

people.role: Moses' father-in-law; visited him at the mount of God (Ex 18)
Spoke against Moses and died at Kadesh (Num 12; 20:1)
Moses' wife; came to him with Jethro (Ex 18:2)
Led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron (Num 16)
Moses' son; came to him with Jethro (Ex 18:3)
Moses' son; came to him with Jethro (Ex 18:4)
King of Moab who hired Balaam (Num 22-24)
Priest who ended the plague at Baal-peor (Num 25)

events.name: Moses at the Burning Bush
events.description: While tending Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush that burns without being consumed, and God calls him by name to bring Israel out of Egypt. God reveals his name, "I AM THAT I AM," and sends Aaron to speak for Moses.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: Moses was eighty when he stood before Pharaoh (Exod 7:7), which puts his call in 1491 BC, shortly before the Exodus; the interval is not given in the text. Ussher, Annals §172: 1491 BC (AM 2513).

events.name: The Ten Plagues and the First Passover
events.description: When Pharaoh refuses to let Israel go, ten plagues strike Egypt, from the Nile turned to blood to the death of the firstborn. Israel is spared by the blood of the Passover lamb on their doorposts, and Pharaoh at last sends them out; the feast is kept as a lasting memorial.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: the plagues fall in the months before the Exodus in 1491 BC, ending with the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month (Exod 12:6). Annals §179-190.

events.name: The Golden Calf
events.description: While Moses is on Sinai receiving the tablets, the people press Aaron to make them gods, and he casts a golden calf. Moses breaks the tablets, destroys the calf, and intercedes for the people; the Levites rally to him, and about three thousand die.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1491 BC, during the forty days Moses spent on Sinai soon after the giving of the Law (Exod 24:18; 32:1). Annals §198-199 (AM 2513d, fourth month).

people.role: made the calf at the people's demand
waited with Moses on the mountain (Exod 32:17)

events.name: Tabernacle Completed
events.description: Following the pattern revealed on Sinai, Israel completes the tabernacle, a portable tent sanctuary where God's glory descends to dwell at the center of the camp. Its gilded frames recall Egyptian portable shrines of the era, while its design anticipates the temple and, for Christians, the incarnation.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1490 BC (Exod 40:17). One year after the Exodus.

people.role: Consecrated as priest for the tabernacle (Ex 40:12-15)
Oversaw the work and set up the tabernacle (Ex 39-40)
First prince to bring an offering at its dedication (Num 7:12)
Craftsman called to build the tabernacle (Ex 31:2-5)

events.name: The Twelve Spies at Kadesh
events.description: Moses sends twelve men, one from each tribe, to explore Canaan. Ten bring back a report of giants and walled cities, and the people refuse to enter; only Joshua and Caleb urge them on, and God decrees forty years in the wilderness for that generation.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: the second year after the Exodus (Num 10:11; 13:20), 1490 BC. Annals §239-241.

people.role: spy who urged the people to go up
spy who urged the people to go up

events.name: Balaam and Balak
events.description: Balak, king of Moab, hires the seer Balaam to curse Israel camped on the plains of Moab. Balaam's donkey sees the angel he cannot, and each time he opens his mouth he can only bless, including a prophecy of a star out of Jacob and a sceptre out of Israel.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: the fortieth year in the wilderness (1452 BC), after Israel's defeat of Sihon and Og (Num 21) and before the death of Moses. Annals §281-284.

events.name: Conquest of Canaan
events.description: Under Joshua, Israel crosses the Jordan and campaigns through Canaan, defeating coalitions of kings and allotting the land among the twelve tribes. Destruction layers at sites like Hazor, the greatest Canaanite city of the region, fuel lively scholarly debate over the conquest's scope and character.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: the war began in 1451 BC (AM 2553), after forty years in the wilderness, and ended in 1445 BC, when Caleb was 85 (Josh 14:7-10) and "the land rested from war" (Josh 11:23; 14:15). Early-date scholars place the conquest c. 1406 BC; late-date scholars c. 1220 BC.

events.name: Fall of Jericho
events.description: Israel circles Jericho for seven days behind the ark until the walls collapse at the trumpet blast and shout, giving Joshua his first victory in Canaan; only faithful Rahab's family is spared. Famous excavations by John Garstang and Kathleen Kenyon made Jericho a landmark case in biblical archaeology.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1451 BC.

events.name: Death of Moses
events.description: At 120 years old, his eye not dim nor his strength abated, Moses climbs Mount Nebo, views the promised land, and dies in Moab; the LORD buries him in a valley there and no one knows his grave. Israel mourns thirty days, and Joshua, full of the spirit of wisdom, leads in his place.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1451 BC, in the last month of the 40th year after the Exodus (Deut 1:3; 34:5-8).

events.name: Israel Crosses the Jordan
events.description: On the tenth day of the first month, the priests bearing the ark step into the Jordan in flood and the waters stand up in a heap; the whole nation crosses on dry ground. Twelve stones from the riverbed are set up at Gilgal as a memorial.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1451 BC, forty years after the Exodus (Josh 4:19).

events.name: Achan's Sin and the Defeat at Ai
events.description: After Jericho, Achan keeps some of the devoted spoil, and Israel is routed in its first attack on Ai. When Achan is exposed by lot and put to death, Israel takes Ai by an ambush.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: the first year in Canaan (1451 BC), directly after the fall of Jericho (Josh 6-8). Annals §313.

events.name: The Sun Stands Still at Gibeon
events.description: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon, which had made peace with Israel. Joshua marches up overnight and, as the enemy flees, asks the Lord that the sun and moon stand still; the day is lengthened and the kings are defeated.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §315-319: 1451 BC (AM 2553c), the same year as the crossing of the Jordan and the fall of Jericho; §320 sums up "that most busy year of the world, 2553".

events.name: Period of the Judges
events.description: Between Joshua and the monarchy, Israel cycles through apostasy, oppression, and rescue as God raises deliverers such as Deborah, Gideon, and Samson. Archaeology reveals a surge of small highland villages in this era, the material footprint of early Israel taking root in Canaan's hill country.
events.dateNotes: Scripture first. 1 Kgs 6:1 puts Solomon's fourth year, when the Temple was founded (1012 BC), in the 480th year from the Exodus: 1491 to 1012 is 479 years and 16 days (Ussher, Annals 465, 4053). Inside that span Scripture gives 40 years in the wilderness, Saul 40 (Acts 13:21), David 40 (1 Kgs 2:11) and three full years of Solomon, leaving 356 years from the crossing of the Jordan (1451) to Saul (1095) for Joshua, the elders and every judge. The judges' own figures (Cushan 8, rest 40, Moab 18, rest 80, Jabin 20, rest 40, Midian 7, Gideon 40, Abimelech 3, Tola 23, Jair 22, Ammon 18, Jephthah 6, Ibzan 7, Elon 10, Abdon 8, Philistines 40) total 390 if laid end to end, before Joshua, Eli and Samuel, so they cannot all run in sequence if 1 Kgs 6:1 stands. Ussher reconciles them as follows. (1) Each rest figure (Judg 3:11, 3:30, 5:31, 8:28) is counted from the previous deliverance and so contains the oppression that ended it: Othniel 1405 (40 years from the rest of c. 1445, Cushan 1413-1405), Ehud 1325 (80 years from Othniel, Moab 1343-1325), Deborah 1285 (40 from Ehud, Jabin 1305-1285), Gideon 1245 (40 from Deborah, Midian 1252-1245; he died 1236). (2) The Ammonite oppression (1206-1188) runs inside Jair's 22 years, and the Philistine forty years inside Eli's forty and Samson's twenty (Samson died 1117, Eli 1116). The sequence then reads Abimelech 1236-1233, Tola to 1210, Jair to 1188, Jephthah to 1182, Ibzan, Elon and Abdon to 1157, Eli 1156-1116, Samuel at Mizpah 1096 and Saul 1095. Acts 13:20 ("about 450 years") does not conflict: Ussher (Annals 337) counts it from the birth of Isaac (1896) to the allotment of the land (1445), about 451 years. The start is Joshua's death, 1443 BC (Ussher, Annals 340; Judg 1:1), and is approximate. Mainstream scholarship places the judges c. 1200-1050 BC, many of them regional and overlapping.

events.name: Death of Joshua
events.description: Joshua son of Nun dies at 110 and is buried at Timnath-serah in Mount Ephraim. Israel serves the LORD all his days and the days of the elders who outlived him.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: he died aged 110 (Josh 24:29-30) and Israel served the LORD all the days of the elders who outlived him (Josh 24:31; Judg 2:7); no year is given. Ussher, Annals 340-341: AM 2561, 1443 BC, placed in the same year as his building of Timnath-serah, after the land had rest (Josh 23:1; 1445 BC); the apostasy and the first oppression (Cushan, eight years, 1413-1405 BC) follow. Marked approximate because Ussher places it by summary. An earlier figure of c. 1426 BC came from Josephus (Antiquities 5.117, 25 years of leadership after Moses), which is neither Scripture nor Ussher.

events.name: Deborah Defeats Sisera
events.description: Deborah and Barak defeat Canaanite general Sisera.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: c. 1285 BC, after twenty years of oppression by Jabin (Judg 4:3). Annals §351 (AM 2719d).

events.name: Gideon Defeats Midian
events.description: Gideon defeats the Midianites with 300 men.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: c. 1245 BC, after seven years of Midianite oppression (Judg 6:1). Annals §354, §356 (AM 2759d).

events.name: Jephthah Defeats the Ammonites
events.description: Recalled from exile by the elders of Gilead, Jephthah argues Israel's title to the land and then defeats the Ammonites, ending eighteen years of oppression. His vow to offer whatever first came out of his house to meet him falls on his only daughter.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1188 BC, ending the eighteen-year oppression begun c. 1206 BC (Judg 10:8). Annals §367-371.

events.name: Ruth and Boaz
events.description: Naomi returns to Bethlehem from Moab with her widowed daughter-in-law Ruth, who gleans in the field of Boaz and wins his notice. Boaz redeems the family's land and marries Ruth, and their son Obed becomes the grandfather of David.
events.dateNotes: The book says only "in the days when the judges ruled" (Ruth 1:1). The years are estimated back from Obed's birth c. 1170 BC and David's birth in 1085 BC (Ruth 4:17-22), as in the life dates of Ruth, Naomi and Boaz.

events.name: Birth of Samson
events.description: An angel of the Lord promises a barren wife of Dan that she will bear a son who will begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines, and Samson is born a Nazirite from the womb. His parents Manoah and his wife are told he must never touch a razor or strong drink.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §380: born 1155 BC (AM 2849b), soon after the forty-year Philistine oppression began (§378). He judged Israel twenty years, 1137-1117 BC (§382, §384).

events.name: Hannah's Prayer and the Birth of Samuel
events.description: Childless Hannah weeps and prays at Shiloh, vowing to give a son to the Lord if he will grant her one. Eli blesses her, Samuel is born, and when he is weaned she brings him to serve at the sanctuary and sings a song of thanks.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: the Eli years run 1157-1116 BC (Annals §378, §386), and Samuel was a child at Shiloh before Eli's death; 1150 BC follows the table's birth year for Samuel (approximate).

events.name: The Call of Samuel
events.description: As a boy serving under Eli, Samuel hears his name called in the night and learns it is the Lord. The word he receives is a judgment on Eli's house, and from then on all Israel knows that Samuel is a prophet.
events.dateNotes: Scripture gives Samuel's age only as a boy (1 Sam 3:1). Josephus says twelve, which gives about 1138 BC from the table's birth year; the date is approximate.

events.name: Death of Samson
events.description: Blinded and set to grind in the prison at Gaza after Delilah's betrayal, Samson is brought out to entertain the Philistines at a feast to Dagon. Praying for strength one last time, he pulls down the pillars of the temple, killing more Philistines at his death than in his life.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1117 BC, after Samson had judged Israel twenty years (Judg 15:20; 16:31). Annals §384.

events.name: Ark Captured by Philistines
events.description: The Philistines capture the Ark of the Covenant at the battle of Aphek. Eli dies upon hearing the news.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1116 BC (1 Sam 4:1-22). Eli, aged 98, died on hearing the news, having judged Israel forty years (1 Sam 4:15-18). Annals §386 (AM 2888d); §365 has Eli dying in AM 2888.

people.role: born on the day the ark was taken

events.name: Samuel Judges Israel at Mizpah
events.description: After twenty years of the ark at Kirjath-jearim, Samuel calls Israel to put away their idols and gathers them at Mizpah to fast and confess. When the Philistines attack, the LORD thunders against them and Israel routs them; Samuel sets up the stone Ebenezer, "Hitherto hath the LORD helped us."
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1096 BC, twenty years after the ark came to Kirjath-jearim (1 Sam 7:2) and a year before Saul. Annals §390 (AM 2908c).

events.name: Saul Anointed King
events.description: When the people demand a king like the nations, God directs Samuel to anoint Saul of Benjamin as Israel's first monarch. Tall, striking, and initially victorious over Ammon and the Philistines, Saul forfeits his dynasty through disobedience, opening the way for David's rise.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals 391: 1095 BC. Scripture: Saul reigned forty years (Acts 13:21); 1 Sam 13:1 is textually difficult in the Hebrew (the age and length of reign are damaged or missing), so Acts 13:21 is the figure used. Mainstream scholarship places his accession c. 1050 BC.

events.name: Saul Rejected as King
events.description: Sent to destroy the Amalekites, Saul spares their king Agag and the best of the flocks and then offers excuses. Samuel tells him that obedience is better than sacrifice and that the Lord has rejected him as king.
events.dateNotes: The text gives no year, and Ussher dates none (Annals §395 says only that Saul had been rejected before Samuel anointed David in 1063 BC). Placed in the middle of Saul's reign (1095-1055 BC); approximate.

events.name: David Anointed by Samuel
events.description: God sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint David, Jesse's youngest son and a shepherd, declaring that the Lord looks on the heart rather than outward stature. The Tel Dan inscription's reference to the house of David gives his dynasty its earliest extrabiblical attestation.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §395: 1063 BC, forty years before Absalom's revolt (2 Sam 15:7); David was then a youth keeping his father's sheep (1 Sam 16:11-12). He became king at Hebron only after Saul's death, in 1055 BC.

events.name: David Defeats Goliath
events.description: In the valley of Elah the Philistine champion Goliath of Gath defies the armies of Israel for forty days. The young David, sent by Jesse with food for his brothers, faces him in the name of the LORD and kills him with a sling stone, and Israel routs the Philistines.
events.dateNotes: Year estimated: soon after Samuel anointed David (Ussher c. 1063 BC) and before David fled from Saul to Gath (Ussher 1060 BC).

people.role: rebukes David at the battle line

events.name: David Spares Saul at En-gedi
events.description: Pursued by Saul with three thousand men, David is hidden in a cave where Saul comes in alone. He cuts off a corner of Saul's robe but refuses to harm the Lord's anointed, and Saul weeps and admits that David will be king.
events.dateNotes: The text gives no year and Ussher does not date it; it falls between David's flight to Gath (Ussher §397, 1060 BC) and Saul's death (1055 BC) and is approximate.

events.name: Death of Saul at Gilboa
events.description: Routed by the Philistines on Mount Gilboa, with Jonathan and two other sons already dead, the wounded Saul falls on his own sword. The men of Jabesh-gilead recover the bodies from the wall of Beth-shan and bury them.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals 405: 1055 BC, closing Saul's forty-year reign (Acts 13:21; 1 Sam 31). David was thirty and Ish-bosheth forty at their accessions the same year (2 Sam 5:4; 2 Sam 2:10).

events.name: David Made King at Hebron
events.description: After Saul's death, David goes up to Hebron and the men of Judah anoint him king over the house of Judah. Abner sets up Saul's son Ish-bosheth over the other tribes, and David reigns in Hebron seven and a half years.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: David was thirty when he began to reign, forty years in all, seven years and six months at Hebron over Judah and thirty-three at Jerusalem over all Israel and Judah (2 Sam 5:4-5; 1 Kgs 2:11). Ussher, Annals 409-410: 1055 BC, the year Saul died.

events.name: David Captures Jerusalem
events.description: David takes the Jebusite stronghold of Zion and makes Jerusalem his capital, uniting the tribes around a city belonging to none of them; a few years later he brings the ark there (2 Sam 6). Excavations in the City of David, including the massive Stepped Stone Structure, illuminate the ancient citadel he claimed.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1048 BC, at the start of David's 33 years in Jerusalem (2 Sam 5:5-9).

events.name: David Anointed King over All Israel
events.description: After Abner's death and the murder of Ish-bosheth, the elders of all the tribes come to David at Hebron, make a covenant with him, and anoint him king over Israel. He goes on to reign thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: seven years and six months at Hebron (2 Sam 5:5). Ussher, Annals 413-416: 1048 BC, after Abner's defection and Ish-bosheth's murder; David was thirty-seven.

events.name: David Brings the Ark to Jerusalem
events.description: David brings the ark up from Kirjath-jearim; after Uzzah is struck down it rests three months in the house of Obed-edom, then enters the city of David with sacrifice and dancing. Michal despises David for dancing before the LORD.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §422: 1045 BC, a sabbatical year (2 Sam 6; 1 Chr 13; 15-16).

people.role: Priest summoned to bring up the ark (1 Chr 15:11)

events.name: Davidic Covenant
events.description: Through the prophet Nathan, God promises David an everlasting house, kingdom, and throne, pledging a son whose reign will never end. This oath anchors the royal psalms and Israel's prophetic hope, and the New Testament proclaims Jesus, son of David, as its ultimate fulfillment.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §428: 1044 BC, when David was settled in his house of cedar (2 Sam 7:1-2).

events.name: David and Bathsheba
events.description: David sees Bathsheba bathing, takes her, and arranges the death of her husband Uriah at the siege of Rabbah. The prophet Nathan confronts him with the story of the ewe lamb, and David confesses (Ps 51); the child dies, and Solomon is born to them later.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1035 BC (2 Sam 11), the year given for Uriah's death in this table.

people.role: commander who carried out the order

events.name: Absalom Kills Amnon
events.description: Amnon wrongs his half-sister Tamar, and her brother Absalom hides his anger for two years before having Amnon killed at a sheepshearing feast. Absalom flees to Geshur, and David mourns for both sons.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §437: 1030 BC, two years after Amnon's rape of Tamar (§436, 1032 BC); Absalom then spent three years in Geshur (§438) and returned in 1027 BC (§439).

events.name: Absalom's Revolt
events.description: Absalom wins the hearts of Israel, has himself proclaimed king at Hebron, and drives David out of Jerusalem. Hushai's counsel defeats Ahithophel's, David's army wins in the forest of Ephraim, and Joab kills Absalom against the king's orders.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §442: 1023 BC, forty years after Samuel anointed David (2 Sam 15:7), between Passover and Pentecost; Absalom died the same year (§445).

people.role: commander of a third of David's army
priest who stayed loyal to David

events.name: Solomon Anointed King
events.description: As David lies dying, Adonijah has himself proclaimed king. Bathsheba and Nathan appeal to David, who has Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon at Gihon, and David dies soon after.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1015 BC, the year David died and Solomon began to reign (1 Kgs 2:10-11).

people.role: prophet who helped secure the succession
mother, who pleaded for her son

events.name: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
events.description: At Gibeon Solomon offers a thousand burnt offerings, and God appears to him in a dream, offering whatever he asks. He asks for an understanding heart to judge the people, and is given wisdom, riches and honour besides.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §463: 1013 BC (AM 2991c), at Gibeon, after Solomon's marriage to Pharaoh's daughter (§462, 1014 BC). The text of Kings gives no year.

events.name: Solomon Builds Temple
events.description: Solomon builds the first temple on Jerusalem's Mount Moriah, a cedar-lined house of hewn stone where the ark comes to rest and God's glory fills the sanctuary at its dedication. Its long-room, tripartite plan resembles excavated Syrian temples such as Ain Dara, rooting it firmly in its ancient world.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: begun in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, the 480th year after the Exodus (1 Kgs 6:1), in the month Zif; finished in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, "seven years" in building (6:37-38); Solomon's own house then took thirteen years (7:1), 1005-992 BC. Ussher, Annals 465: begun 1012 BC (AM 2992). Mainstream chronology (Thiele) dates the start c. 966 BC.

events.name: Dedication of the Temple
events.description: Once the Temple is complete the priests carry the ark into the Most Holy Place, and a cloud fills the house so that they cannot minister. Solomon prays before the altar, blesses the people, and holds a seven-day festival.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 1004 BC, the year after the Temple was finished (1 Kgs 6:38; 8:2); some place it in the same year as completion.

events.name: Solomon's Apostasy
events.description: In his old age Solomon's many foreign wives turn his heart to their gods, and he builds high places for Chemosh and Molech. The Lord tells him the kingdom will be torn away from his son, and the prophet Ahijah promises Jeroboam ten tribes.
events.dateNotes: The text gives no year, only that it happened when Solomon was old (1 Kgs 11:4), before his death in 975 BC.

events.name: Kingdom Divides
events.description: After Solomon's death, Rehoboam's harsh answer at Shechem drives ten northern tribes to crown Jeroboam, splitting the nation into Israel and Judah. The rupture sets the two kingdoms on divergent paths, and Pharaoh Shishak's invasion, carved at Karnak, soon exploited their weakness.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 975 BC (AM 3029), upon Solomon's death. Thiele and most modern scholars date the division c. 931/930 BC.

events.name: Jeroboam's Golden Calves
events.description: Fearing that pilgrimage to Jerusalem would draw his people back to Rehoboam, Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan and appoints his own priests and feast. The Bible repeatedly names this the sin of Jeroboam that Israel's later kings never abandoned.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 975 BC, the year of the division (1 Kgs 12:25-33). Mainstream chronology places the division c. 931/930 BC.

people.role: Rival king in Jerusalem whose temple the calves were meant to replace
Made the two calves and a rival priesthood

events.name: Shishak Invades Judah
events.description: In Rehoboam's fifth year Shishak of Egypt marches against Jerusalem with a great army. Rehoboam and the princes humble themselves, and the city is spared, but the temple and palace treasures, including Solomon's gold shields, are carried off.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 971 BC, Rehoboam's 5th year (1 Kgs 14:25; 2 Chr 12:2). Shishak is Pharaoh Shoshenq I; his Karnak relief records the campaign, usually dated c. 925 BC.

people.role: King of Judah; surrendered the temple treasures
Pharaoh who invaded Judah and carried off the temple treasures

events.name: Abijah Defeats Jeroboam at Mount Zemaraim
events.description: Abijah of Judah calls out to Jeroboam and his army from Mount Zemaraim, reminding Israel of the Lord's covenant with David. Trusting in God, Judah wins a great victory and takes Bethel and nearby towns.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §487: 957 BC (3047c AM), Abijah's 2nd year and Jeroboam's 19th (2 Chr 13). Mainstream chronology dates Abijah about 30 years later.

people.role: King of Israel defeated by Judah
King of Judah who led Judah to victory

events.name: Baasha Destroys the House of Jeroboam
events.description: Baasha of Issachar assassinates Nadab, son of Jeroboam, during the siege of Gibbethon, and kills every member of Jeroboam's family. It fulfils the word of the prophet Ahijah and begins a new dynasty that proves no better.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 953 BC, Nadab's 2nd year (1 Kgs 15:25-30).

events.name: Asa's Reform and Covenant
events.description: After defeating Zerah the Ethiopian, Asa hears the prophet Azariah and removes idols from Judah. He deposes his grandmother Maacah as queen mother for her idol and gathers the people to renew the covenant by oath.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §492, §494: 941 BC (3063c AM), Asa's 15th year, in the third month (2 Chr 15:10). Mainstream dates are about 30 years later.

people.role: Queen mother removed for making an idol
Cushite invader whose defeat preceded the reform

events.name: Zimri's Coup and Omri's Rise
events.description: Zimri murders King Elah while he is drunk and destroys Baasha's house, but reigns only seven days. When the army besieging Gibbethon proclaims its commander Omri king, Zimri burns the palace over himself.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 929 BC, Elah's 2nd year (1 Kgs 16:8-20).

events.name: Omri Founds Samaria
events.description: Omri buys the hill of Shemer and builds Samaria as the new capital of the northern kingdom. It remains the capital until its fall two centuries later, and Assyrian records still call Israel the land of the house of Omri.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §505: 924 BC (3080d AM), when Omri had reigned 6 years in Tirzah (1 Kgs 16:23-24); his reign counts from 929 BC (§500-501). Mainstream c. 880 BC.

people.role: King who bought the hill and built the city

events.name: Jehoshaphat's Reforms
events.description: Jehoshaphat removes the high places, sends officials and Levites through Judah with the book of the law, and later appoints judges in the fortified cities with the charge to judge for the Lord. His reign is remembered as a time of peace and teaching.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §509: 912 BC (3092c AM), the 3rd year of his reign (914-889 BC; 2 Chr 17:7-10). The later judges (2 Chr 19:4-11) are not dated by Ussher.

people.role: King who taught and judged Judah

events.name: Elijah Fed by Ravens and the Widow of Zarephath
events.description: Elijah announces a drought to Ahab, then is fed by ravens at the brook Cherith and, when it dries up, by a Phoenician widow in Zarephath whose flour and oil never run out. He raises her son from death, and she confesses that the word of the Lord in his mouth is truth.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: the drought began c. 910 BC and lasted three and a half years (1 Kgs 17:1; Luke 4:25; Jas 5:17).

people.role: Widow who sheltered him; her son was raised
Prophet sustained by God in the drought

events.name: Elijah on Mount Carmel
events.description: On Mount Carmel, Elijah stands alone against the prophets of Baal, and fire from heaven consumes his water-drenched sacrifice, turning Israel's heart back to the Lord. The contest confronts Baal, the Canaanite storm god, on his own claimed terrain of fire and rain, and ends a long drought at God's word.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: during Ahab's reign (918-897 BC). 1 Kgs 18:20-40.

events.name: Elijah at Mount Horeb
events.description: Fleeing Jezebel's threat, Elijah walks to Horeb, where the Lord comes to him not in wind, earthquake or fire but in a still small voice. He is sent to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha, and finds Elisha ploughing.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: shortly after the contest on Carmel (1 Kgs 19). The year is an estimate.

people.role: Queen whose threat drove him out
Prophet who met God at Horeb

events.name: Naboth's Vineyard
events.description: Naboth refuses to sell his family vineyard beside the palace at Jezreel. Jezebel arranges his death by false witnesses and Ahab seizes the land, and Elijah meets him there with God's sentence on his house.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §514: 899 BC (3105 AM), Ahab's 20th year, the year after Ben-hadad's surrender, two years before Ahab's death in 897 BC (1 Kgs 21).

people.role: Pronounced judgment on Ahab and Jezebel

events.name: Death of Ahab at Ramoth-gilead
events.description: Ahab and Jehoshaphat go to war against Aram to retake Ramoth-gilead. The prophet Micaiah foretells defeat, and Ahab, though disguised, is killed by an arrow shot at random, as Elijah had said.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 897 BC, the last year of Ahab (1 Kgs 22; 2 Chr 18).

people.role: King of Judah allied with Ahab
King of Israel killed in battle

events.name: Elijah Calls Fire on Ahaziah's Messengers
events.description: Ahaziah of Israel, injured in a fall, sends to ask Baal-zebub of Ekron whether he will recover. Elijah intercepts the messengers with the Lord's rebuke, and fire falls on two companies of soldiers sent to seize him before the third captain begs for mercy.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §521: 896 BC (3108b AM), Ahaziah's fall and death in Samaria, before Elijah was taken up (2 Kgs 1).

events.name: Elijah Taken Up and Elisha Succeeds Him
events.description: At the Jordan Elijah parts the water and is carried up to heaven in a whirlwind with a chariot and horses of fire. Elisha takes up his fallen mantle, asks for a double portion of his spirit and parts the river again.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §523: 896 BC (3108c AM), the first year of Jehoram of Israel (2 Kgs 2).

events.name: Israel and Judah Attack Moab
events.description: Jehoram of Israel, Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom march against Moab after Mesha stops paying tribute. With no water for the army, Elisha promises a miraculous flood, and the allies drive Moab back to Kir-hareseth.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §524: 895 BC (3109c AM), Jehoram of Israel's 2nd year, while Edom was still under Judah (2 Kgs 3). Moab's side is told in the Mesha Stele.

people.role: King of Judah who joined it
Prophet who promised water and victory
King of Israel who led the campaign
King of Moab who rebelled against Israel

events.name: Healing of Naaman
events.description: Naaman, commander of Aram's army, sought healing from leprosy on the word of a captive Israelite servant girl. Directed by the prophet Elisha to wash seven times in the Jordan, he was cleansed and confessed Israel's God; Jesus later cited him at Nazareth as a Gentile who received God's mercy.
events.dateNotes: 2 Kgs 5:1-27; during the ministry of Elisha, in the reign of Jehoram of Israel (896-884 BC on Ussher's chain). Year estimated.

events.name: Hazael Becomes King of Aram
events.description: Ben-hadad of Damascus, ill, sends Hazael to ask Elisha whether he will recover. Elisha weeps at what Hazael will do to Israel; the next day Hazael smothers the king and takes the throne.
events.dateNotes: Ussher does not date the accession itself: Annals §533 says that by 884 BC (Ramoth-gilead) Hazael had recently succeeded Benhadad as Elisha foretold (2 Kgs 8:7-15); c. 885 BC is the estimate. Assyrian records of Shalmaneser III also name Hazael as king of Damascus.

people.role: King of Aram smothered by Hazael

events.name: Jehu's Revolt
events.description: Elisha sends a young prophet to anoint Jehu, an army commander at Ramoth-gilead. Jehu drives to Jezreel and kills Jehoram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah, Jezebel is thrown from her window, and Ahab's seventy sons and the priests of Baal are destroyed.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 884 BC (2 Kgs 9-10); the Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III shows Jehu paying tribute, usually dated c. 841 BC.

people.role: Sent the prophet who anointed Jehu

events.name: Athaliah Seizes the Throne of Judah
events.description: When her son Ahaziah is killed, Athaliah destroys the royal family of Judah and rules for six years. Only the infant Joash is saved, hidden in the temple by his aunt Jehosheba.

people.role: Son whose death began her rule
Infant heir hidden in the temple

events.name: Joash Crowned by Jehoiada
events.description: In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest brings out the seven-year-old Joash, crowns him in the temple and makes a covenant with the king and the people. Athaliah cries treason and is put to death, and the house of Baal is torn down.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: 878 BC (2 Kgs 11:4-20; 2 Chr 23).

people.role: Hid the king for six years

events.name: Joash Repairs the Temple
events.description: In his 23rd year Joash finds the priests have not repaired the temple and has a chest set at the altar for the people's gifts. The money is paid straight to the workmen and the house of the Lord is restored.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §538, §540: the poll-tax repair is ordered in 857 BC and, in Joash's 23rd year (3148c AM, 856 BC), the king takes the work from the slow priests (2 Kgs 12:4-16).

events.name: Jeroboam II Restores Israel's Borders
events.description: Jeroboam II, though he continues the sin of Jeroboam, restores Israel's coast from Hamath to the Dead Sea as Jonah had foretold. It is the northern kingdom's last season of power and wealth, which Amos and Hosea would condemn.
events.dateNotes: Ussher: Jeroboam II reigned 825-784 BC (2 Kgs 14:23-29).

people.role: King of Israel who recovered the territory

events.name: Amos Prophesies at Bethel
events.description: Amos, a herdsman of Tekoa, comes north in the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam II, two years before the earthquake. He denounces Israel's injustice and false worship and is ordered to leave Bethel.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §553, §557: Amos was called two years before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam II (810-784 BC, Amos 1:1; 7:10-15); §553 mentions him under the 13th Jubilee (808 BC) but gives no single year. 787 BC is an estimate within the reign of Jeroboam II. Mainstream c. 760 BC.

people.role: King of Judah in whose days he prophesied

events.name: Hosea's Ministry to Israel
events.description: Hosea marries Gomer at God's command, and the names of his children become messages of judgment and hope. His long ministry from Jeroboam II to Hezekiah pictures the Lord's faithful love for an unfaithful people.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §554-556: Hosea prophesied under Jeroboam II (825-784 BC, Hos 1:1-3) and lived to see Israel's ruin in 721 BC, continuing into Hezekiah's time. The start (-785) and end are estimates within those limits.

people.role: First king named in his call
Last king named in his call

events.name: Jonah's Mission to Nineveh
events.description: Called to warn Nineveh, Jonah flees by sea, is swallowed by a great fish and prays from its belly. Sent again, he preaches in the Assyrian capital, the city repents, and God relents, to Jonah's anger and the Lord's rebuke.
events.dateNotes: Scripture dates Jonah only to the reign of Jeroboam II (2 Kgs 14:25; Ussher 825-784 BC, Annals §555) and does not date the mission. Ussher says only that he was "later sent to Nineveh" and takes the repentant king to be Pul (§575, under 771 BC), so the mission is placed there. Estimate within Ussher's reading.

events.name: Uzziah Struck with Leprosy
events.description: Strong and proud, Uzziah enters the temple to burn incense, which only priests may do. Leprosy breaks out on his forehead, he is shut out of the temple, and his son Jotham governs until his death.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §564: struck with leprosy as an old man, soon after Menahem took the throne of Israel (about 771 BC), not in his 25th year as the Jews held; Jotham ruled in the king's house until Uzziah died in 759 BC (§584). Scripture gives no year (2 Chr 26:16-21; 2 Kgs 15:5). The start is an inference from Ussher's words "a short time later".

events.name: Isaiah's Vision and Call
events.description: In the year King Uzziah dies Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up in the temple, with seraphim crying holy, holy, holy. A burning coal touches his lips and he answers, Here am I; send me.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §583-584: 759 BC, the year of Uzziah's death and the 14th Jubilee (Isa 6:1).

people.role: King whose death dates the vision

events.name: Micah's Ministry
events.description: Micah of Moresheth prophesies against Samaria and Jerusalem under Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, denouncing the greed of the powerful. He foretells that the ruler of Israel will come from Bethlehem.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §585: Micah and Isaiah succeeded Jotham-era prophets from 759 BC; §653: Micah prophesied in Hezekiah's days (to 698 BC). The span of the three kings named (Mic 1:1); the exact years of his ministry are an estimate.

people.role: Last king named in his call

events.name: Syro-Ephraimite War
events.description: Rezin of Aram and Pekah of Israel march on Jerusalem to force Ahaz into an alliance against Assyria. Isaiah meets Ahaz with the sign of Immanuel and tells him to trust God, but Ahaz sends tribute to Tiglath-pileser instead.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §598-599: Rezin and Pekah come against Judah at the end of Jotham's reign and the accession of Ahaz (742 BC; Isa 7); §600: Ahaz is defeated in 741 BC (2 Chr 28:5-15); §604: the war ends when Tiglath-pileser takes Damascus in 740 BC. Mainstream c. 735-732 BC.

people.role: Prophet who gave the Immanuel sign
King of Israel who attacked Jerusalem
King of Judah who refused to trust

events.name: Tiglath-pileser Takes Damascus and Galilee
events.description: Answering Ahaz's call, Tiglath-pileser of Assyria captures Damascus and kills Rezin, and carries off the people of Galilee and Gilead. Ahaz goes to meet him at Damascus and copies its altar for the temple.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §604, §607: 740 BC, the third year of Ahaz (2 Kgs 15:29; 16:7-10). Assyrian records date the campaign to 733-732 BC.

people.role: King of Israel who lost Galilee
King of Judah who submitted to Assyria

events.name: Hezekiah's Reform and Passover
events.description: In his first year Hezekiah reopens and cleanses the temple, and removes the high places and the bronze serpent. He invites all Israel to a great Passover in Jerusalem, and the whole assembly keeps a second week of joy.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §620-623: 726 BC, the first year of Hezekiah; the temple is cleansed in the first month and the Passover kept in the second month (2 Kgs 18:1-6; 2 Chr 29-31).

people.role: Prophet whose warning is said to have moved him (Jer 26:18-19)
King who restored the temple and Passover

events.name: Fall of Samaria
events.description: Shalmaneser of Assyria besieges Samaria three years, from Hoshea's seventh year, and takes it in the sixth year of Hezekiah, the ninth of Hoshea. The Israelites are carried to Halah, Habor and Gozan and the cities of the Medes, and foreigners are settled in their place, which ends the northern kingdom (2 Kgs 17:3-6, 24; 18:9-11). Mainstream scholarship credits Sargon II, whose annals boast of 27,290 captives.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: Hezekiah's 6th year and Hoshea's 9th (2 Kgs 18:10); Ussher, Annals §633: 721 BC (AM 3283), toward the end of the third year of the siege begun in Hoshea's 7th. Mainstream: 722 or 721 BC.

people.role: Assyrian king who besieged and took Samaria

events.name: Hezekiah's Deliverance
events.description: When Sennacherib's armies overrun Judah, Hezekiah spreads the Assyrian threat before the Lord and Isaiah promises rescue; the invader withdraws with Jerusalem untaken. Sennacherib's prism boasts of shutting Hezekiah up like a caged bird yet claims no capture, while the Lachish reliefs depict the campaign's fury.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §642, §645: 713 BC, the end of the 14th year of Hezekiah (2 Kgs 18:13; Isa 36:1), fifteen years before his death in 698 (2 Kgs 20:6). (The Annals place the Egyptian campaign and Lachish under 710 BC, but §645 fixes the slaughter in Hezekiah's 14th year.) Sennacherib's prism dates the campaign to 701 BC, which most scholars follow, placing Hezekiah's accession c. 715 BC.

events.name: Hezekiah's Illness and the Babylonian Envoys
events.description: Told by Isaiah to set his house in order, Hezekiah prays and is given fifteen more years, with the shadow going back ten steps as a sign. Envoys of Merodach-baladan of Babylon then come, and Hezekiah shows them all his treasures, which Isaiah says will one day be carried to Babylon.
events.dateNotes: Scripture: fifteen years were added to Hezekiah's life (2 Kgs 20:6; Isa 38:5), and he reigned 29 years (2 Kgs 18:2), so the illness fell in his 14th year, 713 BC on Ussher's chain (Annals §643-650); the envoys come at the beginning of his 15th year (2 Kgs 20:1-19; Isa 38-39). Ussher puts the illness before the slaughter of Sennacherib's army (§644).

people.role: Prophet who gave the sign and the warning

events.name: Manasseh's Apostasy
events.description: Manasseh rebuilds the high places, sets altars to the host of heaven in the temple and passes his son through the fire. He fills Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the Lord announces that the city will be wiped like a dish.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §682: Manasseh reigned from 698 BC (55 years, 2 Kgs 21:1) and at once rebuilt the high places and set up altars in the temple (2 Kgs 21:2-16; 2 Chr 33:2-9). The date is the start of his reign; the rest of the evil continued through it.

people.role: King who led Judah into idolatry

events.name: Sennacherib Assassinated
events.description: Sennacherib returns to Nineveh and is killed by his own sons as he worships in the house of Nisroch, and his son Esarhaddon succeeds him. The Bible records it as the end of the king who defied the Lord at Jerusalem.
events.dateNotes: Standard Assyrian date, 681 BC, from the Babylonian Chronicle (2 Kgs 19:36-37; Isa 37:37-38). Ussher, Annals §668-669, puts it 45 to 55 days after the slaughter of his army in Hezekiah's 14th year (713 BC).

events.name: Manasseh's Captivity and Repentance
events.description: The Assyrians take Manasseh in hooks to Babylon, and there he humbles himself and prays. God hears him and returns him to Jerusalem, where he removes the idols and rebuilds the wall.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §697-699: taken to Babylon in 677 BC, the 22nd year of his reign, under Esarhaddon, and restored after repenting, 33 years before his death (2 Chr 33:10-20). Not mentioned in Kings.

people.role: Assyrian king under whom, on Ussher's reading, this occurred

events.name: Jeremiah's Call
events.description: In Josiah's 13th year the word of the Lord comes to Jeremiah, a priest's son from Anathoth: before you were formed I knew you. Though he protests that he is a youth, God touches his mouth and appoints him over nations and kingdoms.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §737: 629 BC, Josiah's 13th year (Jer 1:2). Ussher places Zephaniah's warnings in the same year.

people.role: King in whose days he was called

events.name: Fall of Nineveh
events.description: A Babylonian and Median coalition destroys Nineveh, the Assyrian capital, as Nahum and Zephaniah had foretold. Assyria's power is broken.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §739: 626 BC, when Nabopolassar and Astyages took Nineveh and its king (Nah 1-3; Zeph 2:13-15). Mainstream: 612 BC (Babylonian Chronicle).

events.name: Josiah's Reforms
events.description: King Josiah finds the Book of the Law and reforms worship.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §742: 624 BC, the 18th year of Josiah (2 Kgs 22:3; 2 Chr 34:8), counting his accession as 641 BC. Ussher takes the covenant renewal as the start of the 30 years of Ezek 1:1, which end at Ezekiel's call in 595 BC. The purge had begun in his 12th year (2 Chr 34:3). Modern scholarship: 622 BC.

events.name: Josiah's Passover
events.description: After the covenant renewal, Josiah keeps the Passover in Jerusalem on a scale not seen since the days of Samuel. Priests and Levites are set in their courses and the whole assembly takes part.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §743: 623 BC, the Passover of the same 18th year of Josiah, on the 14th of the first month (Monday, 4 May). The reforms of §742 fall earlier, in 624 BC (2 Kgs 23:21-23; 2 Chr 35:1-19).

people.role: High priest who served at the temple

events.name: Death of Josiah at Megiddo
events.description: Josiah goes out to stop Pharaoh Necho marching to Carchemish and is shot by archers at Megiddo. All Judah mourns, and Jeremiah composes a lament.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §753-754: 610 BC, the year Necho marched against Carchemish (2 Kgs 23:29-30; 2 Chr 35:20-27). Mainstream 609 BC.

people.role: Placed on the throne by Necho

events.name: Daniel Taken to Babylon
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem in Jehoiakim's reign and carries off temple vessels and young nobles. Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, renamed Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, are trained for the king's service and refuse his food.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §774-776: 607 BC, the 9th month (Chisleu) of Jehoiakim's 4th year, which Ussher counts as Nebuchadnezzar's first as viceroy (Dan 1:1-7; Jer 25:1). Ussher starts the 70 years of captivity here (§775). Mainstream 605 BC.

people.role: King of Judah under whom it happened
Taken captive and trained at court

events.name: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Statue
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of a great statue of gold, silver, bronze and iron leaves him troubled, and his wise men cannot tell it. God reveals it to Daniel, who explains the kingdoms to come and the stone cut without hands, and the king promotes him.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §786: 604 BC, Nebuchadnezzar's 2nd year (Dan 2:1), after the three years of training of §785.

events.name: Jehoiachin Exiled to Babylon
events.description: After Jehoiakim's death, Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem, carries King Jehoiachin, his mother and ten thousand leading men to Babylon and makes Zedekiah king. Ezekiel is among the captives.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §794-796: 599 BC, Nebuchadnezzar's 8th year; Ezekiel and Mordecai are among the captives (2 Kgs 24:8-17; 2 Chr 36:9-10). Babylonian Chronicle: 597 BC.

people.role: Father whose death opened the way

events.name: Ezekiel's Call by the Chebar
events.description: In the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile Ezekiel, a priest among the captives, sees the heavens opened and the glory of the Lord on a throne above living creatures. God sends him as a watchman to a rebellious people.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §821: 595 BC, the 4th month, 5th day (Saturday, 24 July) of the 5th year of Jehoiachin's captivity (Ezek 1:1-3), which Ussher counts as 30 years from Josiah's reform of 624 BC.

people.role: Exiled king whose captivity dates it

events.name: Siege of Jerusalem Begins
events.description: Zedekiah rebels against Babylon, and Nebuchadnezzar camps against Jerusalem in Zedekiah's ninth year. Jeremiah urges surrender, and the siege lasts until the city falls.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §831: 590 BC, Zedekiah's 9th year, tenth month, tenth day (2 Kgs 25:1-2; Jer 52:4-5). Mainstream January 588 BC.

events.name: Jeremiah Cast into the Cistern
events.description: Accused of weakening the soldiers' morale, Jeremiah is thrown into a muddy cistern. Ebed-melech, an Ethiopian court official, has him lifted out, and Zedekiah secretly asks him again for God's word.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §842: 589 BC, late in the siege, when the princes cast Jeremiah into Malchiah's dungeon and Ebed-melech brought him out (Jer 38). His earlier imprisonment in the house of Jonathan falls in 590 BC (§837; Jer 37).

people.role: King who yielded to the officials

events.name: Fall of Jerusalem
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar's Babylonian army breaches Jerusalem after a long siege, burning the temple, razing the walls, and deporting Judah's people. The Babylonian Chronicle independently records his earlier seizure of the city, corroborating the biblical account of Judah's collapse and exile.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §846-850: 588 BC (AM 3416), the 11th year of Zedekiah and 19th of Nebuchadnezzar (2 Kgs 25:2, 8): the city is broken up on the 9th of the 4th month, and the temple burnt on the 10th of the 5th (Jer 39:2; 52:12-13). Most modern scholarship dates the fall to 587 or 586 BC, anchored in the Babylonian Chronicle.

events.name: Babylonian Exile
events.description: Uprooted to Babylon, Judah's exiles mourn Zion by foreign rivers while prophets like Ezekiel and Daniel proclaim God's presence far from the ruined temple. Cuneiform records, including ration tablets naming King Jehoiachin and the Al-Yahudu archive, document the exiled community's life in Babylonia.
events.dateNotes: Dated here from the fall of Jerusalem (588 BC, Ussher, Annals §846-850) to Cyrus's edict (537 BC, §948-949). Ussher counts the seventy years (Jer 25:11-12; 29:10; Dan 9:2) from the first deportation in 607 BC (§775) to the edict in 537 BC; the first return followed in 536 BC (§951). Modern scholarship dates the exile 586-538 BC.

events.name: The Fiery Furnace
events.description: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and are thrown into a furnace heated seven times hotter. The king sees four men walking in the fire, one like a son of the gods, and brings them out unharmed.
events.dateNotes: Scripture gives no year (Dan 3) and the Annals do not date it. The date is an estimate between the dream (604 BC, Ussher §786) and the king's humbling.

events.name: Jehoiachin Released by Evil-merodach
events.description: In the 37th year of his exile, Evil-merodach lifts Jehoiachin out of prison, gives him a seat above other kings and a place at his table for life. The book of Kings ends on this sign that David's line is not finished.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §891: 562 BC, the 37th year of Jehoiachin's captivity, about the 25th of the 12th month, in Evil-merodach's first year (2 Kgs 25:27-30; Jer 52:31-34). Mainstream 561 BC.

events.name: Fall of Babylon to Cyrus
events.description: Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians in a single night. Belshazzar is killed after the writing on the wall is read at his feast, and Darius the Mede takes the kingdom (Dan 5). The Nabonidus Chronicle independently records the city's capture without a battle.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §935-939: 538 BC (AM 3466), the night Belshazzar was slain and Darius the Mede took the kingdom (Dan 5:30-31), the year before Cyrus's edict of 537. Mainstream: 12 October 539 BC (Nabonidus Chronicle).

people.role: King of Babylon when the city fell to Cyrus, not in Scripture by name

events.name: Daniel in the Lions' Den
events.description: Darius the Mede is tricked into a decree forbidding prayer, and Daniel keeps praying three times a day and is thrown to the lions. God shuts their mouths, Daniel's accusers are cast in instead, and Darius honours the God of Daniel.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §939-944: 538 BC, in the first year of Darius the Mede, the same year Ussher gives for the fall of Babylon (Dan 6).

events.name: Edict of Cyrus
events.description: Cyrus of Persia, having taken Babylon, decrees that the exiled Judeans may return to Jerusalem to rebuild the house of the Lord, restoring the plundered temple vessels. The Cyrus Cylinder reflects his wider policy of restoring displaced peoples and shrines, and Isaiah strikingly names him God's anointed.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §948-949: 537 BC (AM 3468), the first year of Cyrus (Ezra 1:1) as Ussher counts it, after the two years of Darius the Mede from 538 BC; the seventy years from 607 BC end here. The return follows in 536 BC (§951). Modern scholarship dates the decree to 538 BC; the Cyrus Cylinder reflects the same policy.

events.name: First Return under Zerubbabel and Jeshua
events.description: After Cyrus's decree, about 42,000 exiles led by Zerubbabel and the priest Jeshua go up from Babylon to Judah, carrying back the temple vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had taken. Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah, receives the vessels. The return is the first step in restoring worship at Jerusalem.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §951: 536 BC, the year after Cyrus's edict of 537 BC (§948-949) (Ezra 1:1; 2:1-2). Mainstream dating places the edict in 538 BC and the first return c. 538-537 BC.

people.role: King whose decree released the exiles
Leader of the first return; governor of Judah
Prince of Judah who brought back the vessels (Ezra 1:8-11)

events.name: Altar Rebuilt and Temple Foundation Laid
events.description: In the seventh month the returned exiles gather at Jerusalem, and Jeshua and Zerubbabel set up the altar and restore the daily burnt offerings, though the temple foundation is not yet laid. In the second year of their coming the builders lay the foundation to trumpets and praise; the young shout for joy and the old who remembered the first temple weep.
events.dateNotes: Ussher, Annals §952-953: altar in the seventh month of 536 BC, foundation in the second month of 535 BC (Ezra 3:1-13). Mainstream dating puts these a year or two earlier, c. 538-536 BC.

people.role: Rebuilt the altar and laid the temple foundation

events.name: Haggai and Zechariah Rouse the Rebuilding
events.description: After the work on the temple has stalled for years under local opposition, the word of the LORD comes by Haggai in the second year of Darius, and Zechariah begins to prophesy soon after. Zerubbabel the governor and Jeshua the high priest obey, and the building resumes within a few weeks.
events.dateNotes: Haggai 1:1 dates the first oracle to the first day of the sixth month of Darius's second year, 520 BC (Ussher, Annals §1015-1018: the building resumed on the 24th day of the ninth month). Ezra 5:1-2; Zechariah 1:1 (eighth month, same year). Standard historical dating also gives 520 BC.

people.role: Governor who obeyed and resumed the building
Prophet whose word stirred the work
King in whose second year the work resumed

events.name: Second Temple Built
events.description: Led by Zerubbabel and Jeshua and stirred by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, the returned exiles complete a new temple in Jerusalem despite opposition and slender means. Elders wept remembering Solomon's house, yet this second temple would anchor Jewish worship for centuries until the Roman era.
events.dateNotes: Begun in the second year of the return (Ezra 3:8), halted, and resumed in the second year of Darius I, 520 BC (Hag 1:1; Ezra 4:24); finished on 3 Adar in his sixth year (Ezra 6:15), March 515 BC. Ussher likewise gives 515 BC.

events.name: Vashti Deposed
events.description: At the end of a six-month display of the wealth of his empire and a feast at Susa, king Ahasuerus (Xerxes) summons Queen Vashti, and she refuses to come. On the advice of his counsellors he deposes her and issues a decree to every province, which clears the way for a new queen.
events.dateNotes: Esther 1:3 dates the feast to the third year of Ahasuerus. Taking Ahasuerus as Xerxes I (reigned 486-465 BC, standard historical dating), that is 484/483 BC. Ussher identifies Ahasuerus with Darius Hystaspes and Vashti with Atossa (Annals §1009, §1027), so he places the feast in 518 BC; this dataset follows the standard identification, as for the existing Esther event.

people.role: Queen who refused the king's summons

events.name: Esther Made Queen
events.description: Esther, a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, is taken to Ahasuerus at Susa in the tenth month of his seventh year. He loves her above the other candidates, sets the royal crown on her head and makes her queen in place of Vashti. Esther keeps her people and family secret at Mordecai's direction.
events.dateNotes: Esther 2:16 gives the tenth month of the seventh year of Ahasuerus, i.e. Tebeth, January 478 BC on Xerxes I (reigned 486-465 BC); entered as 479 BC, the regnal year. Ussher (Annals §1035), reading Ahasuerus as Darius Hystaspes, has this in 514 BC.

people.role: Cousin and guardian who counselled her

events.name: Esther Saves Her People
events.description: In the Persian court at Susa, the Jewish queen Esther risks her life to expose Haman's plot to annihilate her people, and the king's counter-decree turns doom into deliverance. Commemorated each year at Purim, the story displays providence at work even though God is never named in the book.
events.dateNotes: The lot was cast in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus and the decree fell on 13 Adar (Esth 3:7; 9:1), 473 BC if Ahasuerus is Xerxes I (486-465 BC).

events.name: Ezra's Return
events.description: Ezra leads a second return and reforms worship.
events.dateNotes: Seventh year of Artaxerxes I (Ezra 7:7-9): 458 BC by Persian reckoning, 457 BC if his years are counted autumn to autumn (the traditional start of the seventy weeks). Ussher, Annals §1203-1204, dates the departure and arrival to 467 BC, because his Artaxerxes begins reigning about nine years earlier; this dataset keeps the standard date. Some scholars place Ezra in 398 BC under Artaxerxes II.

events.name: Nehemiah Rebuilds Walls
events.description: Nehemiah, cupbearer to the Persian king, returns to Jerusalem and rallies the people to rebuild the ruined walls in fifty-two days despite armed opposition from Sanballat and Tobiah. The Elephantine papyri independently name Sanballat as governor of Samaria, anchoring the memoir in Persian-era history.
